metadata.title: Explicit formulas, symmetry and symmetry breaking for Willmore surfaces of revolution

extraction_notes.note: Corollary 1 restates Theorem 2 word for word; both are numbered environments, so the tie-break rule does not decide. Kept Theorem 2 (the main-text statement) as the node and pointed Corollary 1's proof at it with a proves edge; Corollary 1 has no node.
The appendix proofs are prose (closed by \hfill $\Box$) and start with a restatement of the proposition. The restatement was kept inside the proof as a setup step, and the closing box was left out.
The figure table of k_{m,n}, W_{m,n}, L_{m,n} and S_{m,n} for small m,n is numerical data and was not extracted as nodes. Only the defining sentence of the tabulated quantities is a node.
The paper calls it the Willmore Conjecture but says Marques-Neves proved it. Typed as an external theorem rather than a conjecture.
Proposition 12 and Remark 1(a) are asserted with the proof omitted (analogy / computer check). Kept their types and marked rigor semi_formal.
Left out: purely bibliographic comments (Bryant-Griffiths formulas, Eichmann's circle parameters, the Li-Yau comparison) and the figures.

metadata.extraction_comment: Many defining equations (Z, Delta theta_k, W_j, vartheta, xi, sigma) are numbered equations nested inside prose definition nodes, so \eqref-edges start at the equation node, not at the definition.

nodes.name: Willmore surface
nodes.statement: A Willmore surface is, by definition, a critical point of the Willmore functional $$ \mathcal{W}(\Sigma) = \int_\Sigma H^2 \,d\mu $$ where $H=\frac{1}{2}(k_1+k_2)$ is the mean curvature, $k_1,k_2$ are the principal curvatures and where $d\mu$ denotes the associated volume form of the surface.
nodes.genus: a critical point of the Willmore functional
nodes.statement_short: Willmore surfaces are critical points of the Willmore functional, the integral of squared mean curvature.

nodes.name: Elasticae (elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane)
nodes.statement: It it known \cite{LanSing_Curves_in_the} that Willmore surfaces of revolution are generated by elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}$ (called elasticae), which, by definition, are critical for the total squared curvature functional.
nodes.genus: elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane
differentia: critical for the total squared curvature functional

nodes.name: Langer-Singer classification of closed elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma$ be a regular closed curve in $\mathbb{H}$ which is critical for the elastic energy functional. Then either $\gamma$ is the $m$-fold cover of the ball for some $m$, or $\gamma$ is a member of the family of solutions $\gamma_{m,n}$ having the following description: if $m>1$ and $n$ are integers satisfying $1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt{2}$ there is (up to congruence) a unique curve $\gamma_{m,n}$, which closes up in $n$ periods of its curvature $\kappa=\kappa_0 \mathrm{cn}^2(rs,p)$ while making $m$ orbits about the fixed point of the associated rotation field $J$. Further, $\gamma_{m,n}$ oscillates between a pair of invariant circles of $J$ with the $n$ maxima of $\kappa$ equally spaced around the outer circle and the $n$ minima of $\kappa$ equally spaced around the inner circle. Also, $\gamma_{m,n}$ has $n(m-1)$ points of selfintersections.
nodes.origin_citation: Langer & Singer, Curves in the hyperbolic plane..., Theorem 3
nodes.statement_short: Closed elasticae in H are multiply covered circles or the curves gamma_{m,n} (1<2m/n<sqrt 2), which close after n curvature periods, wind m times, oscillate between two circles and have n(m-1) selfintersections.
assumptions: Let $\gamma$ be a regular closed curve in $\mathbb{H}$ which is critical for the elastic energy functional.
conclusions: either $\gamma$ is the $m$-fold cover of the ball for some $m$, or $\gamma$ is a member of the family of solutions $\gamma_{m,n}$
Also, $\gamma_{m,n}$ has $n(m-1)$ points of selfintersections.
nodes.label: thm:LanSin

nodes.name: Typo in the Langer-Singer curvature formula
nodes.statement: Notice that $\kappa=\kappa_0 \mathrm{cn}^2(rs,p)$ is a typo in \cite{LanSing_Curves_in_the} since the curvature function is basically a $\mathrm{dn}$-function (cf. \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}), as we will see later.

nodes.name: Orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement: Following \cite{LanSing_Curves_in_the} (not necessarily closed) elastic curves generated by such curvature functions will be called orbitlike.

nodes.name: Surface of revolution Sigma_gamma
nodes.statement: \Sigma_\gamma = \Big\{ (\gamma_1(s),\gamma_2(s)\cos(t),\gamma_2(s)\sin(t)) : s\in I, t\in [0,2\pi) \Big\}
nodes.label: eq:Sigma_gamma

nodes.name: Dirichlet problem for Willmore surfaces of revolution
nodes.statement: The problem then is to find a Willmore surface with preassigned initial or end positions and angles, i.e. for given $(A_1,A_2),(B_1,B_2)$ in the hyperbolic plane and $\phi_A,\phi_B\in\mathbb{R}$ one has to find an elastic curve $\gamma$ with (unknown) hyperbolic length $L$ such that the following holds: \begin{equation} \mathcal{W}'(\Sigma_\gamma)=0,\quad \gamma(0)=(A_1,A_2),\quad \gamma(L)=(B_1,B_2),\quad e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},\quad e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}. \end{equation} Here, we formally write $\mathcal{W}'(\Sigma_\gamma)=0$ in place of the Willmore equation and the angle function $\phi$ is given by $\gamma'=|\gamma'|e^{i\phi}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Schaetzle; Dall'Acqua, Deckelnick, Grunau et al.
nodes.statement_short: Find an elastica with prescribed endpoints in H and prescribed end angles generating a Willmore surface of revolution.

nodes.name: Dirichlet problem for Willmore surfaces of revolution
nodes.statement: \mathcal{W}'(\Sigma_\gamma)=0,\quad \gamma(0)=(A_1,A_2),\quad \gamma(L)=(B_1,B_2),\quad e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},\quad e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}.
nodes.label: eq:DirichletBVP

nodes.name: Symmetry of orbitlike solutions for symmetric Dirichlet data
nodes.statement: Assume $A_1=-B_1\neq 0, A_2=B_2>0,\phi_A+\phi_B\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ such that $$ \pm\big(\frac{A_2}{A_1}\sin(\phi_A) + \cos(\phi_A)\big) \notin (0,2). $$ Then all positively $(\pm=+)$ respectively negatively $(\pm=-)$ oriented orbitlike solutions of~\eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} are symmetric.
nodes.statement_short: For symmetric Dirichlet data with A_1=-B_1 nonzero and an angle condition, all positively (resp. negatively) oriented orbitlike solutions are symmetric.
conclusions: Then all positively $(\pm=+)$ respectively negatively $(\pm=-)$ oriented orbitlike solutions of~\eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} are symmetric.
nodes.label: thm:Symmetry

nodes.name: Symmetric solution of the Dirichlet problem
nodes.statement: Here, a solution of \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} is called symmetric if we have $$ \gamma_1(L/2+s)=-\gamma_1(L/2-s),\quad \gamma_2(L/2+s)=\gamma_1(L/2-s) \qquad\text{for all }s\in [0,L/2] $$ and it is called nonsymmetric otherwise.

nodes.name: Positive / negative orientation of an elastica
nodes.statement: Positive / negative orientation means that the hyperbolic curvature of the elastica is assumed to be positive / negative at some point (and hence everywhere since the $\mathrm{dn}$-function is zero-free).

nodes.name: Symmetry breaking for the Dirichlet problem
nodes.statement: There are boundary data $A_1=-B_1,A_2=B_2>0,\phi_A=-\phi_B$ such that \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} has uncountably many nonsymmetric solutions.
nodes.statement_short: Some symmetric Dirichlet boundary data admit uncountably many nonsymmetric Willmore surfaces of revolution.
conclusions: There are boundary data $A_1=-B_1,A_2=B_2>0,\phi_A=-\phi_B$ such that \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} has uncountably many nonsymmetric solutions.
nodes.label: thm:Symmetry_breaking

nodes.name: Hyperbolic plane (upper half plane model)
nodes.statement: Willmore surfaces of revolution are known to be generated by elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2: x_2>0\}$, see for instance p.532 in \cite{LanSing_Curves_in_the}.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic metric and distance
nodes.statement: The metric is given by $\frac{dx_1^2+dx_2^2}{x_2^2}$ and the distance between two points $(x_1,x_2),(y_1,y_2)\in \mathbb{H}$ is \begin{equation} d_{\mathbb{H}}((x_1,x_2),(y_1,y_2)) = \mathrm{Arcosh}\Big(1+\frac{(x_1-y_1)^2+(x_2-y_2)^2}{2x_2y_2}\Big). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Parametrization by hyperbolic arclength
nodes.statement: Regular curves $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{H}$ are therefore parametrized by hyperbolic arclength if $(\gamma_1')^2+(\gamma_2')^2\equiv \gamma_2^2$ and in fact all curves studied in this paper will be written down in this parametrization.

nodes.name: Angle function and hyperbolic (geodesic) curvature
nodes.statement: Introducing the angle function $\phi$ via $\gamma_1' = \gamma_2 \cos(\phi),\gamma_2' = \gamma_2 \sin(\phi)$ (such that $\gamma'=|\gamma'|e^{i\phi}$) one finds that the hyperbolic (or geodesic) curvature function is given by \begin{equation} \kappa := - \frac{\gamma_2^2}{\gamma_2'} \Big(\frac{\gamma_1'}{\gamma_2^2}\Big)' = \phi'+\cos(\phi). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Defines the angle function phi by gamma_1'=gamma_2 cos(phi), gamma_2'=gamma_2 sin(phi) and the hyperbolic curvature kappa = phi' + cos(phi).

nodes.name: Hyperbolic curvature formula
nodes.statement: \kappa := - \frac{\gamma_2^2}{\gamma_2'} \Big(\frac{\gamma_1'}{\gamma_2^2}\Big)' = \phi'+\cos(\phi).
nodes.label: eq:hyperbolic_curvature

nodes.name: ODE system for curve, angle and curvature
nodes.statement: \gamma_1' = \gamma_2 \cos(\phi),\quad \gamma_2' = \gamma_2 \sin(\phi),\quad \phi' + \cos(\phi) = \kappa.
nodes.label: eq:ODE_solution

nodes.name: Moebius invariance of the curvature ODE system
nodes.statement: This ODE system is invariant under M\"obius transformations and in particular under the continuous isometries of the hyperbolic plane where only the initial data $\gamma_1(0),\gamma_2(0),\phi(0)$ changes. Identifying $\mathbb{H}$ with $\{x+iy:y>0\}$ and writing $\gamma=\gamma_1+i\gamma_2$ these isometries take the following form: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] horizontal translation: $\gamma\mapsto \gamma+a$ for $a\in\mathbb{R}$, \item[(ii)] dilation: $\gamma \mapsto b\gamma$ for $b>0$, \item[(iii)] hyperbolic rotation: $\gamma\mapsto \tfrac{\cos(\theta/2)\gamma+\sin(\theta/2)}{-\sin(\theta/2)\gamma+\cos(\theta/2)} $ for $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The system (5) is invariant under horizontal translations, dilations and hyperbolic rotations, which only change the initial data.

nodes.name: Elastica curvature ODE and first integral mu
nodes.statement: -\kappa''+\kappa =\frac{1}{2}\kappa^3,\qquad\quad \mu := -(\kappa')^2+ \kappa^2 - \frac{1}{4}\kappa^4 \in\mathbb{R}.
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.label: eq:ODE_kappa

nodes.name: Classification of curvature functions of free elasticae in H
nodes.statement: From Table (2.7)(c) in~\cite{LanSing_the_total} for $G=-1$ we find that $\kappa$ is, up to multiplication by $-1$, one of the following functions: \begin{align*} &(i)\;\;\quad \kappa\equiv \sqrt{2} &&\mu = 1\\ &(ii)\;\quad \kappa(s) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\mathrm{dn}\Big(\frac{s+a}{\sqrt{2-k^2}},k\Big)\quad(0<k<1) && \mu =\frac{4(1-k^2)}{(2-k^2)^2}, \\ &(iii)\quad \kappa\equiv 0 \quad\text{or}\quad \kappa(s)= 2\mathrm{sech}(s+a) &&\mu= 0, \\ &(iv)\;\quad \kappa(s)= \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}} \mathrm{cn}\Big(\frac{s+a}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}},k\Big)\quad (\frac{1}{\sqrt 2}<k<1) && \mu = - \frac{4k^2(1-k^2)}{(2k^2-1)^2}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.origin_citation: Langer & Singer, The total squared curvature of closed curves, Table (2.7)(c)
nodes.statement_short: Up to sign, the curvature of a free elastica in H is constant sqrt 2, a dn-function (orbitlike), 0 or 2 sech (geodesic), or a cn-function (wavelike).
conclusions: $\kappa$ is, up to multiplication by $-1$, one of the following functions:

nodes.name: Circular, orbitlike, geodesic and wavelike elasticae
nodes.statement: These figures motivate the names (i) circular, (ii) orbitlike, (iii) geodesic / asymptotically geodesic or (iv) wavelike, respectively.
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.definiendum: circular, orbitlike, geodesic / asymptotically geodesic, wavelike

nodes.name: Distance function Z(s;P)
nodes.statement: The key to achieve this goal is a thorough discussion of the function \begin{equation} Z(s;P) = \frac{(\gamma_1(s)-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2(s)-P_2)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2(s)} \qquad\text{for all } P=(P_1,P_2)\in \mathbb{C} \text{ with }P_2\neq 0, \end{equation} which for $P\in\mathbb{H}$ is a conformal invariant due to $d_{\mathbb{H}}(\gamma(s),P) = \mathrm{Arcosh}(1+Z(s;P))$, see~\eqref{eq:metric}.
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Z(s;P) is the conformally invariant squared-distance quantity with d_H(gamma(s),P)=Arcosh(1+Z(s;P)).

nodes.name: Distance function Z
nodes.statement: Z(s;P) = \frac{(\gamma_1(s)-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2(s)-P_2)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2(s)} \qquad\text{for all } P=(P_1,P_2)\in \mathbb{C} \text{ with }P_2\neq 0,
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.label: eq:def_Z

nodes.name: Willmore Conjecture
nodes.statement: Notably the Willmore Conjecture says that the infimum of the Willmore energy in the class of immersed tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is achieved by the Clifford-Torus.
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: The Clifford torus minimizes the Willmore energy among immersed tori in R^3.
assumptions: in the class of immersed tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$
conclusions: the infimum of the Willmore energy in the class of immersed tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is achieved by the Clifford-Torus

nodes.name: Clifford torus as circular elastica
nodes.statement: One explicit parametrization of the Clifford torus is given by \begin{align*} \gamma(s) = \Big( \frac{(1+\sqrt{2})\sin(s)}{\sqrt{2}+\cos(s)}, \frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}+\cos(s)}\Big),\quad e^{i\phi(s)} = \frac{1+\sqrt{2}\cos(s)+i\cdot \sin(s)}{\sqrt{2}+\cos(s)}. \end{align*} This precise realization of the Clifford torus corresponds to solving \eqref{eq:ODE_solution} for $\gamma(0)=(0,1),\phi(0)=0$ and $\kappa\equiv \sqrt{2}$.
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Explicit circular elastica with kappa = sqrt 2 generating the Clifford torus.

nodes.name: Geodesics in H as elasticae
nodes.statement: Geodesics in $\mathbb{H}$ are known to be either vertical lines or half circles in dependence of the initial position and angle. If $\phi(0)\in (\pm \frac{\pi}{2}+2\pi)\mathbb{Z}$ then the geodesic through $(0,1)$ is vertical and given by $\gamma(s)=(0,e^{\pm s}),\phi(s)=\phi(0)$. Otherwise, for instance in case $\phi(0)=0$, we find the halfcircles $$ \gamma(s) = (\tanh(s),\mathrm{sech}(s)),\qquad e^{i\phi(s)}= \mathrm{sech}(s) - i\cdot \tanh(s). $$
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Geodesic elasticae: vertical lines or half circles, given explicitly.

nodes.name: Asymptotically geodesic elastica (catenoid)
nodes.statement: The third exceptional family of elasticae is the asymptotically geodesic one which corresponds to the conformal class of the catenoid. By definition, it is the graph of the $\cosh$-function and therefore $$ \gamma(s) = (s,\cosh(s)),\qquad e^{i\phi(s)} = \mathrm{sech}(s)+i\cdot \tanh(s). $$
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: The asymptotically geodesic elastica is the graph of cosh, generating the catenoid.

nodes.name: Linear ODE for the distance function Z
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{H}$ be parametrized by hyperbolic arclength and $Z$ be given by \eqref{eq:def_Z}. Then, for all $P\in \mathbb{C}^2$ with $P_2\neq 0$, the function $Z(\cdot;P)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa(Z+1)\equiv 2\mu C \end{equation} where $C\in\mathbb{C}$ is, for any $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$, given by \begin{align} \begin{aligned} C &= \frac{P_2^2+(\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2(s_0)}\cdot\Big(\frac{\kappa(s_0)}{\mu}+\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0)) - \frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ & + \frac{\gamma_2(s_0)}{2P_2}\cdot \Big(\frac{\kappa(s_0)}{\mu}-\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0)) + \frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ &+ \frac{\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \Big( -\frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0))-\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0)) \Big). \end{aligned} \end{align}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: For an arclength-parametrized curve, Z(.;P) satisfies the linear second order ODE kappa Z''-2kappa'Z'+kappa(Z+1)=2 mu C with an explicit constant C.
assumptions: Let $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{H}$ be parametrized by hyperbolic arclength and $Z$ be given by \eqref{eq:def_Z}.
conclusions: for all $P\in \mathbb{C}^2$ with $P_2\neq 0$, the function $Z(\cdot;P)$ satisfies
nodes.label: prop:ode_Z

nodes.name: ODE for Z
nodes.statement: \kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa(Z+1)\equiv 2\mu C
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.label: eq:ODE_Z

nodes.name: Constant C
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} C &= \frac{P_2^2+(\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2(s_0)}\cdot\Big(\frac{\kappa(s_0)}{\mu}+\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0)) - \frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ & + \frac{\gamma_2(s_0)}{2P_2}\cdot \Big(\frac{\kappa(s_0)}{\mu}-\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0)) + \frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ &+ \frac{\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \Big( -\frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0))-\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0)) \Big). \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.label: eq:def_C

nodes.name: Proof of Linear ODE for the distance function Z
nodes.statement: For convenience we write $Z:=Z(\cdot;P)$. Differentiating $Z$ gives the formula \begin{equation} Z' = \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi). \end{equation} Differentiating once more and using $\phi'+\cos(\phi)=\kappa$ gives \begin{align*} Z'' &= \phi'\cdot \Big( - \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot\cos(\phi) \Big) \\ &\quad + \frac{\gamma_1'}{P_2}\cos(\phi) + \frac{2\gamma_2^2\gamma_2'-2(\gamma_1-P_1)\gamma_2\gamma_1' - (\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2)\gamma_2' }{2P_2\gamma_2^2} \sin(\phi) \\ &= (\kappa-\cos(\phi)) \cdot \Big( - \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot\cos(\phi) \Big) \\ &\quad + \frac{\gamma_2}{P_2}\cdot \cos^2(\phi) + \frac{(\gamma_2^2+P_2^2+ (\gamma_1-P_1)^2) \sin(\phi) -2(\gamma_1-P_1)\gamma_2\cos(\phi)}{2P_2\gamma_2} \cdot \sin(\phi) \\ &= (\kappa-\cos(\phi)) \cdot \Big( - \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot\cos(\phi) \Big) \\ &\quad + \frac{\gamma_2}{P_2}\cdot \cos^2(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2+P_2^2+(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2} \cdot \sin^2(\phi) -\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi)\cos(\phi) \\ &= \frac{\gamma_2^2+P_2^2+(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2} - \kappa w \\ &= Z+1-\kappa w. \end{align*} Here, the auxiliary function $w$ is given by $$ w : = \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \sin(\phi) - \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2} \cdot \cos(\phi). $$ From the identity \begin{align*} w' &= \Big(\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) \Big) \phi' \\ &\;+ \Big( \frac{\gamma_2}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) - \Big(\frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\Big)'\Big) \cdot \cos(\phi) \\ &= \Big(\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) \Big) \phi' \\ &\;+ \Big(\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) \Big) \cos(\phi) \\ &= Z' (\phi'+\cos(\phi)) \\ &= \kappa Z' \end{align*} we get \begin{align*} (\kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa Z + \kappa)' &= (-\kappa^2 w-2\kappa'Z'+ 2\kappa Z + 2\kappa)' \\ &= Z'(-2\kappa''+2\kappa) -2\kappa^2w' + 2\kappa' (- \kappa w -Z'' + Z+1) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa}}{=} Z'(-2\kappa''+2\kappa-\kappa^3) \\ &= 0 \end{align*} so that $\kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa Z + \kappa$ must be constant. If we define $C\in\mathbb{C}$ to be the complex number with $\kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa Z + \kappa\equiv 2\mu C$, then we finally find for all $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$ \begin{align*} 2\mu C &= \kappa(s_0) Z''(s_0)-2\kappa'(s_0)Z'(s_0)+\kappa(s_0)(Z(s_0)+1) \\ &= 2\kappa(s_0) (Z(s_0)+1) -\kappa(s_0)^2 w(s_0) -2\kappa'(s_0)Z'(s_0) \\ &= \frac{P_2^2+(\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2(s_0)}\cdot\Big(2\kappa(s_0) +2\kappa'(s_0) \sin(\phi(s_0)) - \kappa(s_0)^2 \cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ & + \frac{\gamma_2(s_0)}{2P_2}\cdot \Big(2\kappa(s_0) -2\kappa'(s_0) \sin(\phi(s_0)) + \kappa(s_0)^2 \cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ &+ \frac{\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \Big( - \kappa(s_0)^2 \sin(\phi(s_0))-2\kappa'(s_0) \cos(\phi(s_0)) \Big). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Direct differentiation: compute Z', Z'' via an auxiliary function w with w'=kappa Z', show the expression is constant using the curvature ODE, evaluate at s_0.

nodes.name: Compute Z'
nodes.statement: For convenience we write $Z:=Z(\cdot;P)$. Differentiating $Z$ gives the formula \begin{equation} Z' = \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate Z to get the formula for Z'.

nodes.name: Formula for Z'
nodes.statement: Z' = \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi).
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.label: eq:formula_Zprime

nodes.name: Compute Z'' via w
nodes.statement: Differentiating once more and using $\phi'+\cos(\phi)=\kappa$ gives \begin{align*} Z'' &= \phi'\cdot \Big( - \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot\cos(\phi) \Big) \\ &\quad + \frac{\gamma_1'}{P_2}\cos(\phi) + \frac{2\gamma_2^2\gamma_2'-2(\gamma_1-P_1)\gamma_2\gamma_1' - (\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2)\gamma_2' }{2P_2\gamma_2^2} \sin(\phi) \\ &= (\kappa-\cos(\phi)) \cdot \Big( - \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot\cos(\phi) \Big) \\ &\quad + \frac{\gamma_2}{P_2}\cdot \cos^2(\phi) + \frac{(\gamma_2^2+P_2^2+ (\gamma_1-P_1)^2) \sin(\phi) -2(\gamma_1-P_1)\gamma_2\cos(\phi)}{2P_2\gamma_2} \cdot \sin(\phi) \\ &= (\kappa-\cos(\phi)) \cdot \Big( - \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot\cos(\phi) \Big) \\ &\quad + \frac{\gamma_2}{P_2}\cdot \cos^2(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2+P_2^2+(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2} \cdot \sin^2(\phi) -\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi)\cos(\phi) \\ &= \frac{\gamma_2^2+P_2^2+(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2} - \kappa w \\ &= Z+1-\kappa w. \end{align*} Here, the auxiliary function $w$ is given by $$ w : = \frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \sin(\phi) - \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2} \cdot \cos(\phi). $$
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate again using phi'+cos(phi)=kappa; Z''=Z+1-kappa w with auxiliary w.

nodes.name: Constancy of the expression
nodes.statement: From the identity \begin{align*} w' &= \Big(\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) \Big) \phi' \\ &\;+ \Big( \frac{\gamma_2}{P_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) - \Big(\frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\Big)'\Big) \cdot \cos(\phi) \\ &= \Big(\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) \Big) \phi' \\ &\;+ \Big(\frac{\gamma_1-P_1}{P_2} \cdot \cos(\phi) + \frac{\gamma_2^2-P_2^2-(\gamma_1-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2}\cdot \sin(\phi) \Big) \cos(\phi) \\ &= Z' (\phi'+\cos(\phi)) \\ &= \kappa Z' \end{align*} we get \begin{align*} (\kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa Z + \kappa)' &= (-\kappa^2 w-2\kappa'Z'+ 2\kappa Z + 2\kappa)' \\ &= Z'(-2\kappa''+2\kappa) -2\kappa^2w' + 2\kappa' (- \kappa w -Z'' + Z+1) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa}}{=} Z'(-2\kappa''+2\kappa-\kappa^3) \\ &= 0 \end{align*} so that $\kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa Z + \kappa$ must be constant.
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Show w'=kappa Z' and that the derivative of kappa Z''-2kappa'Z'+kappa Z+kappa vanishes by the curvature ODE.

nodes.name: Evaluate the constant
nodes.statement: If we define $C\in\mathbb{C}$ to be the complex number with $\kappa Z''-2\kappa'Z'+\kappa Z + \kappa\equiv 2\mu C$, then we finally find for all $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$ \begin{align*} 2\mu C &= \kappa(s_0) Z''(s_0)-2\kappa'(s_0)Z'(s_0)+\kappa(s_0)(Z(s_0)+1) \\ &= 2\kappa(s_0) (Z(s_0)+1) -\kappa(s_0)^2 w(s_0) -2\kappa'(s_0)Z'(s_0) \\ &= \frac{P_2^2+(\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1)^2}{2P_2\gamma_2(s_0)}\cdot\Big(2\kappa(s_0) +2\kappa'(s_0) \sin(\phi(s_0)) - \kappa(s_0)^2 \cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ & + \frac{\gamma_2(s_0)}{2P_2}\cdot \Big(2\kappa(s_0) -2\kappa'(s_0) \sin(\phi(s_0)) + \kappa(s_0)^2 \cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ &+ \frac{\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1}{P_2}\cdot \Big( - \kappa(s_0)^2 \sin(\phi(s_0))-2\kappa'(s_0) \cos(\phi(s_0)) \Big). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the constant 2 mu C at s_0 to obtain formula for C.

nodes.name: Remarks on a fourth order ODE for Z and the Euclidean analogue
nodes.statement: ~ \begin{itemize} \item[(a)] Differentiating \eqref{eq:ODE_Z} twice one finds $2Z^{(iv)} + \big((3\kappa^2-4)Z'\big)' + (2-\kappa^2)(Z+1) =0$. This ODE is, in contrast to \eqref{eq:ODE_Z}, not singular at zeros of $\kappa$. In particular $Z$ is smooth even in the wavelike case where $\kappa$ has infinitely many zeros. Since we will not make use of this ODE we omit the proof. \item[(b)] A similar result may be shown for elastic curves in the Euclidean plane that have recently been studied in \cite{DecGru_bvp,Man_bvp}. Such curves $\hat\gamma$, now parametrized by Euclidean arclength with curvature $\hat\kappa$, satisfy $\hat \kappa \hat Z''-2\hat\kappa'\hat Z'= const$ where $\hat Z(s):= (\gamma_1(s)-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2(s)-P_2)^2$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3 Classification of elasticae in the hyperbolic plane
nodes.statement_short: Z satisfies a nonsingular fourth order ODE (proof omitted); an analogous identity holds for Euclidean elastic curves.

nodes.name: Elliptic integrals of the first and second kind
nodes.statement: The elliptic integrals of the first and second kind are defined by $$ F(l,k) := \int_0^l \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}\sqrt{1-k^2t^2}}\,dt, \qquad E(l,k) := \int_0^l \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2t^2}}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\,dt $$ and in the special case $l=1$ we obtain the so-called complete elliptic integrals $K(k) := F(1,k)$, $E(k) := E(1,k)$.

nodes.name: Derivatives of complete elliptic integrals
nodes.statement: K'(k) = \frac{E(k)-(1-k^2)K(k)}{k(1-k^2)},\qquad E'(k) = \frac{E(k)-K(k)}{k}.
nodes.label: eq:derivative_EK

nodes.name: Jacobi's elliptic functions sn, cn, dn
nodes.statement: As we will see in \eqref{eq:Jac_Inverse} these functions relate to Jacobi's elliptic functions $\mathrm{sn}(\cdot,k),\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k),\mathrm{dn}(\cdot,k)$ (we omit the arguments for convenience) that can be defined as the unique solution of the initial value problem \begin{align} \mathrm{sn}' = \mathrm{cn}\mathrm{dn}, \quad \mathrm{cn}'=-\mathrm{sn}\mathrm{dn},\quad \mathrm{dn}' = -k^2\mathrm{sn}\mathrm{cn},\quad \mathrm{sn}(0)=0,\;\mathrm{cn}(0)=\mathrm{dn}(0)=1. \end{align}

nodes.name: Jacobi elliptic functions initial value problem
nodes.statement: \mathrm{sn}' = \mathrm{cn}\mathrm{dn}, \quad \mathrm{cn}'=-\mathrm{sn}\mathrm{dn},\quad \mathrm{dn}' = -k^2\mathrm{sn}\mathrm{cn},\quad \mathrm{sn}(0)=0,\;\mathrm{cn}(0)=\mathrm{dn}(0)=1.
nodes.label: eq:Jacobi_ODE_1terOrdnung

nodes.name: Jacobi trigonometric identities
nodes.statement: \mathrm{cn}^2+\mathrm{sn}^2 = 1,\qquad \mathrm{dn}^2+k^2\mathrm{sn}^2 = 1,
nodes.label: eq:Jacobi_trigonometric_identities

nodes.name: Second order ODEs for cn, sn, dn
nodes.statement: \mathrm{cn}'' = (2k^2-1)\mathrm{cn} -2k^2\mathrm{cn}^3, \; \mathrm{sn}'' = -(1+k^2)\mathrm{sn} +2k^2\mathrm{sn}^3,\; \mathrm{dn}'' = (2-k^2)\mathrm{dn} -2\mathrm{dn}^3.
nodes.label: eq:Jacobi_ODE_2terOrdnung

nodes.name: Inverses of Jacobi elliptic functions
nodes.statement: \mathrm{sn}^{-1}(z,k) = F(z,k),\quad \mathrm{cn}^{-1}(z,k) = F(\sqrt{1-z^2},k),\quad \mathrm{dn}^{-1}(z,k) = F(\sqrt{1-z^2}/k,k).
nodes.label: eq:Jac_Inverse

nodes.name: Addition formulas for Jacobi functions
nodes.statement: \mathrm{cn}(s-K(k)) = \sqrt{1-k^2} \frac{\mathrm{sn}(s)}{\mathrm{dn}(s)},\; \mathrm{sn}(s-K(k)) = -\frac{\mathrm{cn}(s)}{\mathrm{dn}(s)},\; \mathrm{dn}(s-K(k)) = \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\mathrm{dn}(s)},
nodes.label: eq:Jac_Additionstheoreme

nodes.name: Heuman's Lambda function
nodes.statement: Next we define Heuman's Lambda function $\Lambda_0$ via $$ \Lambda_0(\arcsin(l),k):=\frac{2}{\pi} (E(k)F(l,k')+K(k)E(l,k')-K(k)F(l,k')), $$ see 150.03 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}.

nodes.name: Complementary modulus k'
nodes.statement: Here and in the text we will write $k':=\sqrt{1-k^2}$.

nodes.name: Derivatives of Heuman's Lambda function
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial}{\partial l} \Lambda_0(\arcsin(l),k) &= \frac{2(E(k)-(1-k^2)l^2K(k))}{\pi l'\sqrt{1-(1-k^2)l^2}},\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial k} \Lambda_0(\arcsin(l),k) &= \frac{2(E(k)-K(k))ll'}{\pi k\sqrt{1-(1-k^2)l^2}}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:derivative_Heuman

nodes.name: Jacobi's eta, theta and zeta functions
nodes.statement: Additionally, we will need Jacobi's eta, theta and zeta functions $H,\Theta,\Theta_1,\zeta:\mathbb{C}\times(0,1)\to\mathbb{C}$ defined through the following formulas (see 144.01 and 1050.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}): \begin{align*} &\Theta(z,k) := \vartheta_0(\frac{\pi z}{2 K(k)},q_k), &&H(z,k) := \vartheta_1(\frac{\pi z}{2 K(k)},q_k), \\ &\Theta_1(z,k) := \vartheta_3(\frac{\pi z}{2 K(k)},q_k), &&\zeta(z,k) := \frac{\Theta_z(z,k)}{\Theta(z,k)}. \end{align*} Here, the Jacobian Theta Functions $\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1$ and the elliptic nome $q_k$ are given by \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \vartheta_0(z,q) &= 1 + 2 \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n q^{n^2}\cos(2nz), \\ \vartheta_1(z,q) &= 2 \sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n q^{(n+1/2)^2}\sin((2n+1)z), \\ \vartheta_3(z,q) &= 1 + 2\sum_{n=1}^\infty q^{n^2}\cos(2nz), \\ q_k &= \exp(-\pi K(k')/K(k)). \end{aligned} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Defines Jacobi's eta, theta, theta_1 and zeta functions via the theta series vartheta_0,vartheta_1,vartheta_3 and the nome q_k.

nodes.name: Jacobian theta series and elliptic nome
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \vartheta_0(z,q) &= 1 + 2 \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n q^{n^2}\cos(2nz), \\ \vartheta_1(z,q) &= 2 \sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n q^{(n+1/2)^2}\sin((2n+1)z), \\ \vartheta_3(z,q) &= 1 + 2\sum_{n=1}^\infty q^{n^2}\cos(2nz), \\ q_k &= \exp(-\pi K(k')/K(k)). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:JacobianTheta_series

nodes.name: Orbitlike elastica with curvature parameters k, s_*
nodes.statement: So from now on let always $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{H}$ denote an orbitlike elastica with (hyperbolic) curvature function \begin{equation} \kappa(s)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\mathrm{dn}(\frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}},k) \end{equation} for $0<k<1,s_*\in\mathbb{R}$ and let $\phi,Z$ be defined as in \eqref{eq:ODE_solution},\eqref{eq:def_Z}.

nodes.name: Orbitlike curvature function
nodes.statement: \kappa(s)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\mathrm{dn}(\frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}},k)
nodes.label: eq:def_kappa_orbitlike

nodes.name: Rotation Delta theta_k
nodes.statement: In order to measure the angular progress of an elastica generated by this curvature function via \eqref{eq:ODE_solution} we will need \begin{equation} \Delta\theta_k := \pi- \pi \Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k) + 2\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k), \end{equation} a function that has been introduced and analyzed in Proposition 5.3 in~\cite{LanSing_the_total}.

nodes.name: Rotation Delta theta_k
nodes.statement: \Delta\theta_k := \pi- \pi \Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k) + 2\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k),
nodes.label: eq:def_rotation

nodes.name: Discrepancy in Langer-Singer's formulas for Delta theta_k
nodes.statement: We mention that Langer and Singer gave two expressions for $\Delta\theta_k$ on page 21 in \cite{LanSing_the_total} which, however, do not coincide. We chose the correct second expression as a definition. In their first expression the factor $(1-p^2)$ has to replaced by $\sqrt{1-p^2}$, as we will see in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}.

nodes.name: Fundamental system of the Lame-type equation w''+2dn^2 w=0
nodes.statement: For all $k\in (0,1)$ the ordinary differential equation $w''+2\mathrm{dn}^2(\cdot,k)w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that the following holds: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $w_1$ is odd about 0, $w_2$ is even about 0, $w_2(0)>0>w_1'(0)$, \item[(ii)] $w_1(s)^2+w_2(s)^2=2-k^2 -\mathrm{dn}^2(s,k)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(iii)] $w_1(s)w_1'(s)+w_2(s)w_2'(s) = k^2\mathrm{dn}(s,k)\mathrm{cn}(s,k)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(iv)] $w_1(s)w_2'(s)-w_2(s)w_1'(s) = \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(v)] $(w_1+iw_2)(s+2lK(k)) = (w_1+iw_2)(s) e^{il\Delta\theta_k}$ for all $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$, \item[(vi)] $(w_1+iw_2)(-K(k)) = e^{i(\pi-\Delta\theta_k)/2}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: w''+2dn^2 w=0 has a fundamental system w_1 (odd), w_2 (even) with explicit modulus, Wronskian and quasi-periodicity e^{i Delta theta_k}.
conclusions: the ordinary differential equation $w''+2\mathrm{dn}^2(\cdot,k)w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that the following holds:
nodes.label: prop:w1w2_orbitlike

nodes.name: Lame equation
nodes.statement: We remark that the equation $w''+2\mathrm{dn}^2(\cdot,k)w=0$ is a special case ($h=2,n=1$) of the so-called Lam\'{e} equation which is typically written in the form $w''=(n(n+1)k^2\mathrm{sn}^2(\cdot,k)-h)w$, where $h$ is called the Lam\'{e} eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Rescaled fundamental system W_1, W_2 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Now, being given $w_1,w_2$ we define \begin{align} W_j(s) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} w_j\big(-K(k)+ \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\big) \qquad (j=1,2). \end{align}

nodes.name: Definition of W_j (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: W_j(s) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} w_j\big(-K(k)+ \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\big) \qquad (j=1,2).
nodes.label: eq:def_Wj

nodes.name: Identities for the fundamental system W_1, W_2 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa$ be given by \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}. Then $\{W_1,W_2\}$ is a fundamental system of the ODE $W''+2\mu\kappa^{-2}W=0$ and the following identities hold on $\mathbb{R}$: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $W_1^2+W_2^2 = \frac{\kappa^2-\mu}{\kappa^2}$, \item[(ii)] $W_1'= \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_1 - \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_2 $, \item[(iii)] $W_2' = \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_1 + \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_2$, \item[(iv)] $W_1W_2'-W_2W_1' = \frac{\sqrt{\mu}}{2}$, \item[(v)] $(W_1+iW_2)(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))=(W_1+iW_2)(s)e^{il\Delta\theta_k}$ for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$, \item[(vi)] $(W_1+iW_2)(s)= (-W_1+iW_2)(-s-2s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k}$ for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: W_1,W_2 solve W''+2 mu kappa^{-2} W=0 and satisfy explicit modulus, derivative, Wronskian, quasi-periodicity and reflection identities.
conclusions: Then $\{W_1,W_2\}$ is a fundamental system of the ODE $W''+2\mu\kappa^{-2}W=0$ and the following identities hold on $\mathbb{R}$:
nodes.label: prop:W1W2_orbitlike

nodes.name: Angle function vartheta (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Next we choose an angle function $\vartheta$ as follows: \begin{align} W_2(s)-iW_1(s) = \frac{ \sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa} e^{i\vartheta(s)}. \end{align} This definition makes sense due to Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(i). Notice that \eqref{eq:def_theta} determines $\vartheta$ only up to additive multiples of $2\pi$ so that we require $\vartheta$ to satisfy the inequality $-2\pi<\vartheta(-s_*)\leq 0$.

nodes.name: Angle function vartheta (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: W_2(s)-iW_1(s) = \frac{ \sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa} e^{i\vartheta(s)}.
nodes.label: eq:def_theta

nodes.name: Properties of the angle function vartheta (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: The following identities hold: $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\qquad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{\frac{-\sqrt{\mu}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cos(\vartheta)}{\sin(\vartheta)}{-\sin(\vartheta)}{\cos(\vartheta)}. $$ Moreover, we have for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$ \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $\vartheta(-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)) = \frac{l-1}{2}\Delta\theta_k$, \item[(ii)] $\vartheta(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(s) = l\Delta\theta_k$, \item[(iii)] $\vartheta(-s_*+s)+\vartheta(-s_*-s) = -\Delta\theta_k$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: vartheta' = sqrt(mu) kappa^2/(2(kappa^2-mu)), the matrix of W_1,W_2 is a rotation by vartheta, and vartheta advances by Delta theta_k per period.
nodes.label: prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike

nodes.name: Auxiliary vector functions xi^1, xi^2, xi^3
nodes.statement: In order to accurately describe the function $Z$ we will need the following functions: \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \xi^1(s) &:= \matII{ W_1(s)}{W_2(s)}{ W_1'(s)}{ W_2'(s)}^{-1} \vecII{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}-\frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu}-\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s)) +\frac{\kappa(s)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s))}{-\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}\sin(\phi(s))-\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}}, \\ \xi^2(s) &:= \matII{ W_1(s)}{ W_2(s)}{ W_1'(s)}{ W_2'(s)}^{-1} \vecII{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}-\frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu}+\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s)) -\frac{\kappa(s)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s))}{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}\sin(\phi(s))-\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}}, \\ \xi^3(s) &:= \matII{ W_1(s)}{ W_2(s)}{ W_1'(s)}{ W_2'(s)}^{-1} \vecII{\frac{\kappa(s)^2}{2\mu}\sin(\phi(s)) +\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\mu}\cos(\phi(s))}{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}\cos(\phi(s))}. \end{aligned} \end{align}

nodes.name: Functions xi^1, xi^2, xi^3
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \xi^1(s) &:= \matII{ W_1(s)}{W_2(s)}{ W_1'(s)}{ W_2'(s)}^{-1} \vecII{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}-\frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu}-\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s)) +\frac{\kappa(s)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s))}{-\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}\sin(\phi(s))-\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}}, \\ \xi^2(s) &:= \matII{ W_1(s)}{ W_2(s)}{ W_1'(s)}{ W_2'(s)}^{-1} \vecII{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}-\frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu}+\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s)) -\frac{\kappa(s)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s))}{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}\sin(\phi(s))-\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}}, \\ \xi^3(s) &:= \matII{ W_1(s)}{ W_2(s)}{ W_1'(s)}{ W_2'(s)}^{-1} \vecII{\frac{\kappa(s)^2}{2\mu}\sin(\phi(s)) +\frac{\kappa'(s)}{\mu}\cos(\phi(s))}{\frac{1}{\kappa(s)}\cos(\phi(s))}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:formula_xi

nodes.name: Formula for Z in terms of W_1, W_2 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: For $P=(P_1,P_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $P_2\neq 0$ we have \begin{equation} Z(s;P) = -1 + \kappa(s)\big( AW_1(s) + BW_2(s) + C\big) \end{equation} where $C$ is given by \eqref{eq:def_C} and $A,B\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy \begin{align} \vecII{A}{B} &= \frac{(\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1)^2+P_2^2}{2\gamma_2(s_0)P_2} \xi^1(s_0) + \frac{\gamma_2(s_0)}{2P_2}\xi^2(s_0) + \frac{\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1}{P_2}\xi^3(s_0) \quad\forall s_0\in\mathbb{R}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Z(s;P) = -1 + kappa(s)(A W_1(s) + B W_2(s) + C) with explicit coefficients A,B given via xi^1,xi^2,xi^3.
conclusions: where $C$ is given by \eqref{eq:def_C} and $A,B\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy
nodes.label: prop:formula_Z_orbitlike

nodes.name: Formula for Z (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Z(s;P) = -1 + \kappa(s)\big( AW_1(s) + BW_2(s) + C\big)
nodes.label: eq:formula_Z

nodes.name: Coefficients A, B
nodes.statement: \vecII{A}{B} &= \frac{(\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1)^2+P_2^2}{2\gamma_2(s_0)P_2} \xi^1(s_0) + \frac{\gamma_2(s_0)}{2P_2}\xi^2(s_0) + \frac{\gamma_1(s_0)-P_1}{P_2}\xi^3(s_0) \quad\forall s_0\in\mathbb{R}.
nodes.label: eq:formula_AB

nodes.name: Proof of Formula for Z in terms of W_1, W_2 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be given by \eqref{eq:def_C} so that $Z(\cdot;P)$ satisfies the ODE \eqref{eq:ODE_Z}. We define the auxiliary function $W(s) := (Z(s;P)+1)\kappa(s)^{-1}-C$. Then we get \begin{align*} W''(s) &= \frac{1}{\kappa(s)^2} \Big( \kappa(s)Z''(s;P)-2\kappa'(s)Z'(s;P) + (Z(s;P)+1)\big(-\kappa''(s)+2\frac{\kappa'(s)^2}{\kappa(s)}\big) \Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_Z}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)^2} \Big( (Z(s;P)+1)\big(-\kappa(s)-\kappa''(s)+2\frac{\kappa'(s)^2}{\kappa(s)} \big) +2\mu C\Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa}}{=} -\frac{2\mu}{\kappa(s)^2} \Big( \frac{Z(s;P)+1}{\kappa(s)}-C\Big) \\ &= -\frac{2\mu}{\kappa(s)^2}W(s). \end{align*} By Proposition \ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike} we can find $A,B\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $W(s)=AW_1(s)+BW_2(s)$ and thus \begin{align*} Z(s;P) = -1 + \kappa(s)\big(W(s)+C\big) = -1 + \kappa(s)\big( AW_1(s) + B W_2(s) + C\big) \end{align*} so that \eqref{eq:formula_Z} is proved. Solving this identity for $W_1,W_2$ and differentiating it with respect to~$s$ we get the following equations for $A,B$: \begin{align*} \matII{ W_1(s_0)}{ W_2(s_0)}{ W_1'(s_0)}{ W_2'(s_0)}\vecII{A}{B} = \vecII{\frac{Z(s_0;P)+1}{\kappa(s_0)}-C}{\big(\frac{Z(\cdot;P)+1}{\kappa}-C\big)'(s_0)} = \vecII{\frac{Z(s_0;P)+1}{\kappa(s_0)}-C}{\frac{Z'(s_0;P)}{\kappa(s_0)}- \frac{\kappa'(s_0)(Z(s_0;P)+1)}{\kappa(s_0)^2}}. \end{align*} Plugging in the formulas for $Z(s_0;P),Z'(s_0;P)$ and $C$, see \eqref{eq:def_Z},\eqref{eq:formula_Zprime},\eqref{eq:def_C}.
nodes.statement_short: W=(Z+1)/kappa - C solves W''+2 mu kappa^{-2}W=0, hence is a combination of W_1,W_2; A,B from initial data at s_0.

nodes.name: ODE for W
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be given by \eqref{eq:def_C} so that $Z(\cdot;P)$ satisfies the ODE \eqref{eq:ODE_Z}. We define the auxiliary function $W(s) := (Z(s;P)+1)\kappa(s)^{-1}-C$. Then we get \begin{align*} W''(s) &= \frac{1}{\kappa(s)^2} \Big( \kappa(s)Z''(s;P)-2\kappa'(s)Z'(s;P) + (Z(s;P)+1)\big(-\kappa''(s)+2\frac{\kappa'(s)^2}{\kappa(s)}\big) \Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_Z}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)^2} \Big( (Z(s;P)+1)\big(-\kappa(s)-\kappa''(s)+2\frac{\kappa'(s)^2}{\kappa(s)} \big) +2\mu C\Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa}}{=} -\frac{2\mu}{\kappa(s)^2} \Big( \frac{Z(s;P)+1}{\kappa(s)}-C\Big) \\ &= -\frac{2\mu}{\kappa(s)^2}W(s). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce W=(Z+1)/kappa - C and show W''=-2 mu kappa^{-2} W.

nodes.name: Expand in fundamental system
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike} we can find $A,B\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $W(s)=AW_1(s)+BW_2(s)$ and thus \begin{align*} Z(s;P) = -1 + \kappa(s)\big(W(s)+C\big) = -1 + \kappa(s)\big( AW_1(s) + B W_2(s) + C\big) \end{align*} so that \eqref{eq:formula_Z} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: By Proposition 3 write W=A W_1+B W_2, giving the formula for Z.

nodes.name: Determine A, B
nodes.statement: Solving this identity for $W_1,W_2$ and differentiating it with respect to~$s$ we get the following equations for $A,B$: \begin{align*} \matII{ W_1(s_0)}{ W_2(s_0)}{ W_1'(s_0)}{ W_2'(s_0)}\vecII{A}{B} = \vecII{\frac{Z(s_0;P)+1}{\kappa(s_0)}-C}{\big(\frac{Z(\cdot;P)+1}{\kappa}-C\big)'(s_0)} = \vecII{\frac{Z(s_0;P)+1}{\kappa(s_0)}-C}{\frac{Z'(s_0;P)}{\kappa(s_0)}- \frac{\kappa'(s_0)(Z(s_0;P)+1)}{\kappa(s_0)^2}}. \end{align*} Plugging in the formulas for $Z(s_0;P),Z'(s_0;P)$ and $C$, see \eqref{eq:def_Z},\eqref{eq:formula_Zprime},\eqref{eq:def_C}.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the linear system at s_0 using Z, Z' and C.

nodes.name: Explicit formulas for orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement: A curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{H}$ is an orbitlike elastica parametrized by hyperbolic arclength if and only if we have \begin{align} \gamma_1(s) &=\frac{b_1 W_1(s)+b_2 W_2(s)+b_3}{a_1 W_1(s)+a_2 W_2(s)+a_3}, \\ \gamma_2(s) &=\frac{1}{\kappa(s)(a_1 W_1(s)+a_2 W_2(s)+a_3)} \end{align} for $a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3\in\mathbb{R}$ such that \begin{equation} a_3= \sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2}>0,\qquad \vecII{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{b_3}{a_3} \vecII{a_1}{a_2} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3} \vecII{-a_2}{a_1}. \end{equation} In this case we moreover have for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ \begin{align} \gamma_2(s)(a_1,a_2)^T&= \xi^1(s) , \\ \gamma_2(s) (b_1,b_2)^T &= \gamma_1(s) \xi^1(s)+ \gamma_2(s) \xi^3(s), \\ \gamma_1(s) &= \frac{b_3}{a_3} +\frac{1}{2\mu a_3}\big(\kappa(s)^2\sin(\phi(s))+2\kappa'(s)\cos(\phi(s))\big), \\ \gamma_2(s) &= \frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu a_3} + \frac{1}{2\mu a_3}\big(2\kappa'(s)\sin(\phi(s))-\kappa(s)^2\cos(\phi(s))\big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A curve is an orbitlike elastica in arclength iff gamma_1, gamma_2 are explicit Moebius-type quotients of W_1, W_2, 1 with coefficients a_i,b_i satisfying a_3=|(a_1,a_2)| and a linear relation for b.
conclusions: A curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{H}$ is an orbitlike elastica parametrized by hyperbolic arclength if and only if we have
nodes.label: thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike

nodes.name: Coefficient relations (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: a_3= \sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2}>0,\qquad \vecII{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{b_3}{a_3} \vecII{a_1}{a_2} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3} \vecII{-a_2}{a_1}.
nodes.label: eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3

nodes.name: Identities for a, b and gamma (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: \gamma_2(s)(a_1,a_2)^T&= \xi^1(s) , \\ \gamma_2(s) (b_1,b_2)^T &= \gamma_1(s) \xi^1(s)+ \gamma_2(s) \xi^3(s), \\ \gamma_1(s) &= \frac{b_3}{a_3} +\frac{1}{2\mu a_3}\big(\kappa(s)^2\sin(\phi(s))+2\kappa'(s)\cos(\phi(s))\big), \\ \gamma_2(s) &= \frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu a_3} + \frac{1}{2\mu a_3}\big(2\kappa'(s)\sin(\phi(s))-\kappa(s)^2\cos(\phi(s))\big).
nodes.label: eq:a1a2b1b2_1

nodes.name: Proof of Explicit formulas for orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement_short: Necessity by equating coefficients of P_2^2 and P_1 in the formula for Z and computing inner products of xi^1,xi^3; sufficiency by defining phi explicitly and checking the ODE system. The key step is the inner product identities for xi^1, xi^3 via the rotation form of the Wronskian matrix.

nodes.name: Proof outline
nodes.statement: The strategy of the proof is the following: First we assume $\gamma$ to be an orbitlike elastica in~$\mathbb{H}$ parametrized by hyperbolic arclength and derive the formulas \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}--\eqref{eq:b3a3_2}. This will prove the ''only if''-part of our claim. Then we check that the formulas \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}--\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} indeed define orbitlike elasticae which, as solutions of \eqref{eq:ODE_kappa}, are parametrized by hyperbolic arclength.
nodes.statement_short: Outline: necessity by deriving the formulas, sufficiency by verification.

nodes.name: Coefficients of P_2^2
nodes.statement: So let us first assume that $\gamma$ is an orbitlike elastica in $\mathbb{H}$ so that identity \eqref{eq:formula_Z} holds for all $s,s_0\in\mathbb{R}$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_orbitlike}. We multiply \eqref{eq:formula_Z} with $2P_2\gamma_2(s)$ and obtain \begin{align*} (\gamma_1(s)-P_1)^2+\gamma_2(s)^2+P_2^2 = 2\gamma_2(s)\kappa(s)P_2\big( A W_1(s) + B W_2(s) + C \big) \end{align*} where $A,B,C$ are given by the formulas \eqref{eq:formula_AB},\eqref{eq:def_C}. Equating the coefficients of the monomial $P_2^2$ we get \begin{align*} 1 &= \frac{\gamma_2(s)\kappa(s)}{\gamma_2(s_0)} \Big( \xi^1(s_0)_1 W_1(s) + \xi^1(s_0)_2 W_2(s) \\ &\quad + \frac{\kappa(s_0)}{\mu}+\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0)) - \frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ &= \gamma_2(s)\kappa(s)\big(a_1 W_1(s)+a_2W_2(s)+a_3\big) \end{align*} and thus \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2} is proved. Notice that the above identity holds for all $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$, which proves the formulas \eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} for $a_1,a_2,a_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Equate coefficients of P_2^2 to get gamma_2 formula and a_1,a_2,a_3 identities.

nodes.name: Coefficients of P_1
nodes.statement: Similarly, equating the coefficients of $P_1$ we get \begin{align*} -2\gamma_1(s) &= \frac{2\gamma_2(s)\kappa(s)}{\gamma_2(s_0)} \Big( - \big(\gamma_1(s_0)\xi^1(s_0)+\gamma_2(s_0)\xi^3(s_0)\big)_1 W_1(s) \\ &-\big(\gamma_1(s_0)\xi^1(s_0)+\gamma_2(s_0)\xi^3(s_0)\big)_2 W_2(s) \\ &- \gamma_1(s_0) \Big(\frac{\kappa(s_0)}{\mu}+\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0)) - \frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \\ &-\gamma_2(s_0)\Big(-\frac{\kappa(s_0)^2}{2\mu}\sin(\phi(s_0))-\frac{\kappa'(s_0)}{\mu}\cos(\phi(s_0))\Big) \Big) \\ &= -2\gamma_2(s)\kappa(s)\big(b_1W_1(s)+b_2W_2(s)+b_3\big). \end{align*} In the same way as above this implies the formulas \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2},\eqref{eq:b3a3_1} involving $b_1,b_2,b_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Equate coefficients of P_1 to get gamma_1 formula and b-identities.

nodes.name: Remaining relations
nodes.statement: It therefore remains to prove \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} to finish the ''only if''-part.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to prove the coefficient relations.

nodes.name: Rotation form of xi
nodes.statement: To this end we introduce the matrices \begin{align*} \mathcal{W}:=\matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'},\qquad \mathcal{R}(\vartheta):=\matII{\cos(\vartheta)}{\sin(\vartheta)}{-\sin(\vartheta)}{\cos(\vartheta)}. \end{align*} Then Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike} gives the following: \begin{align*} \mathcal{W} &= \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{\frac{-\sqrt{\mu}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \mathcal{R}(\vartheta),\qquad \mathcal{W}^{-1} = \mathcal{R}(-\vartheta) \matII{\frac{2\sqrt{\mu}\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{-\frac{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\sqrt{\mu}\kappa}} {\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{0}. \\ \intertext{Combining this with \eqref{eq:formula_xi} and $(\kappa')^2=\kappa^2-\frac{1}{4}\kappa^4-\mu$ we get} \xi^1 &= \mathcal{R}(-\vartheta) \vecII{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\mu(\kappa^2-\mu)}}(2\kappa'\cos(\phi)+\kappa^2\sin(\phi))}{ \frac{1}{2\mu\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}(2\mu-2\kappa^2-2\kappa\kappa'\sin(\phi)+\kappa^3\cos(\phi)) }, \\ \xi^3 &= \mathcal{R}(-\vartheta) \vecII{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\mu(\kappa^2-\mu)}}(2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))}{ \frac{\kappa}{2\mu\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi)) }. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Proposition 4 to write W and xi^1, xi^3 through rotations R(-vartheta).

nodes.name: Inner products
nodes.statement_short: Compute <xi^1,xi^1>, <xi^1,xi^3>, <xi^1 perp,xi^3>.

nodes.name: Inner products of xi^1 and xi^3
nodes.label: eq:formulas_scpr_xi_1

nodes.name: a_3 formula and positivity
nodes.statement: This implies \begin{align*} a_1^2+a_2^2 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1}}{=} \frac{1}{\gamma_2^2}\skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_scpr_xi_1}}{=} a_3^2. \end{align*} Hence, we find the formula for $a_3$ from \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} since $a_3$ is positive due to \begin{align*} a_3 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:b3a3_2}}{=} \frac{2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi)}{2\mu \gamma_2} \geq \frac{2\kappa-\sqrt{(2\kappa')^2+\kappa^4}}{2\mu \gamma_2} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa}}{=} \frac{\kappa-\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\mu\gamma_2} > 0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Deduce a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2 and a_3>0.

nodes.name: b relations
nodes.statement: Similarly we get \begin{align*} b_1a_1+b_2a_2 &\hspace{-3mm}\stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2}}{=} \frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_2^2}\skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1} + \frac{1}{ \gamma_2}\skp{\xi^1}{\xi^3} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_scpr_xi_1},\eqref{eq:formulas_scpr_xi_2}}{=} \gamma_1a_3^2 + a_3(b_3-\gamma_1 a_3) = b_3a_3, \\ -b_1a_2+b_2a_1 &\hspace{-3mm}\stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\gamma_2}\skp{(\xi^1)^\perp}{\xi^3} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_scpr_xi_3}}{=} \frac{a_3}{\sqrt\mu}. \end{align*} Combining these equations we obtain the formulas for $b_1,b_2$ and \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce the formulas for b_1,b_2, completing the 'only if' part.

nodes.name: Sufficiency
nodes.statement: Now we prove the sufficiency of our conditions, so let $a_1,\ldots,b_3$ be given as in \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} we define $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ by the formulas \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1},\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}. Motivated by the formulas~\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} derived in the ''only if''-part we define $\phi$ via \begin{equation} \vecII{\sin(\phi)}{\cos(\phi)} := \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}\matII{\kappa^2}{2\kappa'}{2\kappa'}{-\kappa^2} \vecII{\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}}{\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}}. \end{equation} We have to verify that such a definition makes sense by checking that the Euclidean norm of the vector on the right hand side is 1. We introduce the notation $$ aW:=a_1W_1+a_2W_2,\quad a^\perp W:=-a_2W_1+a_1W_2, \quad bW:= b_1W_1+b_2W_2 $$ so that we can use the following facts: $$ \gamma_1 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3},\quad \gamma_2 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(aW+a_3)},\quad b \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{b_3}{a_3} a + \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} a^\perp,\quad a_3bW-b_3 aW \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu} a^\perp W. $$ This implies \begin{align*} &\frac{\mu^2 a_3^2}{4(\kappa^2-\mu)^2} \Big( \Big( \kappa^2\big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big)+2\kappa'\big(\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big)\Big)^2 + \Big( 2\kappa'\big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big)-2\kappa^2\big(\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big) \Big)^2 \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu^2 a_3^2 (\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2)}{4(\kappa^2-\mu)^2} \Big( \big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big)^2+ \big(\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big)^2\Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu^2 a_3^2}{\kappa^2-\mu} \Big( \big( \frac{a_3bW-b_3aW}{a_3(aW+a_3)}\big)^2+ \big( \frac{-\kappa^2aW + (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \big)^2\Big) \\ &= \frac{\big( \kappa\mu(a_3bW-b_3aW)\big)^2+ \big(-\kappa^2aW + (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3 \big)^2}{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ \kappa^2\mu(a^\perp W)^2 + \kappa^4(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ \kappa^2\mu |a|^2|W|^2 + (\kappa^4-\kappa^2\mu)(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{(aW)^2 +2a_3aW+ a_3^2}{(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= 1. \end{align*} Here we have used $\kappa^2|a|^2|W|^2=(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3^2$, see \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(i). It remains to check that $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi)$ satisfies the ODE~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. To this end, we first rewrite the formulas for $\sin(\phi),\cos(\phi)$ from \eqref{eq:formula_phi} in the following way: \begin{align*} \sin(\phi) &= \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \kappa^2\big( \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big) +2\kappa'\big( \frac{1}{\kappa(aW+a_3)}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big) \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \frac{\kappa^2( bW a_3-aW b_3)}{a_3(aW+a_3)} + \frac{2\kappa'( \mu a_3-\kappa^2 (aW+a_3))}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \frac{\kappa^2 a^\perp W}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} + \frac{2\kappa'( (\mu-\kappa^2) a_3- \kappa^2 aW)}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \Big) \\ &= \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu) a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}, \\ \cos(\phi) &= \frac{2\sqrt\mu \kappa' a^\perp W + \kappa^3 aW + \kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}. \end{align*} For the calculation of $\gamma_1',\gamma_2'$ we use the formula \begin{align*} W' = \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W + \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W^\perp \end{align*} from Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(ii),(iii). We obtain \begin{align*} \frac{\gamma_2'}{\gamma_2} &= - \frac{\kappa'}{\kappa} - \frac{aW'}{aW+a_3} \\ &= - \frac{\kappa'}{\kappa} - \frac{2\mu\kappa' aW - \sqrt\mu\kappa^3 a^\perp W }{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \frac{ \sqrt\mu \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \sin(\phi). \\ \intertext{Similarly, $|a|^2=a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2$ implies} \frac{\gamma_1'}{\gamma_2} &= \kappa(aW+a_3) \Big( \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}\Big)' \\ &= \kappa bW' -\kappa aW' \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3} \\ &= \kappa W' \big( -\frac{a^\perp W}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} a + \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3}a^\perp \big) \\ &= \frac{(2\sqrt\mu\kappa' W + \kappa^3 W^\perp) (- (a^\perp W) a + (aW+a_3)a^\perp)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^3 (a^\perp W)^2+\kappa^3 (aW)^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt\mu\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^3 |a|^2|W|^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt\mu\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{a_3\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu) + \kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt\mu\kappa' a^\perp W}{2(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \cos(\phi). \end{align*} Here, once again we used $\kappa^3|a|^2|W|^2 = \kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)$. So we see that the equations for $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ from \eqref{eq:ODE_solution} are satisfied and it remains to verify the ODE for $\phi$. Having defined $\phi$ in \eqref{eq:formula_phi} in such a way that \eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} holds, we may differentiate these equations in order to derive the formula for $\phi'$. Differentiating \eqref{eq:b3a3_1} and using $\gamma_1'=\gamma_2\cos(\phi)$ as well as \eqref{eq:b3a3_2} we find \begin{align*} 2\kappa'(\kappa-\phi')\sin(\phi) + (\kappa^2\phi'+2\kappa-\kappa^3)\cos(\phi) = 2\kappa\cos(\phi)+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)\cos(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos^2(\phi) \end{align*} Differentiating \eqref{eq:b3a3_2} and using $\gamma_2'=\gamma_2\sin(\phi)$ as well as \eqref{eq:b3a3_2} we get \begin{align*} -2\kappa'(\kappa-\phi')\cos(\phi) + (\kappa^2\phi'+2\kappa-\kappa^3)\sin(\phi) = -2\kappa'\cos(\phi)+2\kappa \sin(\phi) -\kappa^2\sin(\phi)\cos(\phi) \end{align*} Multiplying the first equation with $\sin(\phi)$, the second with $-\cos(\phi)$ and adding up the resulting equations we arrive at $2\kappa'(\kappa-\phi')=2\kappa'\cos(\phi)$ and thus $\phi'+\cos(\phi)=\kappa$. So $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi)$ is a solution to the the ODE \eqref{eq:ODE_solution} and hence an orbitlike elastica, which is all we had to prove.
nodes.statement_short: Verify that the formulas define an orbitlike elastica parametrized by arclength.

nodes.name: Define phi and check unit norm
nodes.statement: Motivated by the formulas~\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} derived in the ''only if''-part we define $\phi$ via \begin{equation} \vecII{\sin(\phi)}{\cos(\phi)} := \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}\matII{\kappa^2}{2\kappa'}{2\kappa'}{-\kappa^2} \vecII{\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}}{\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}}. \end{equation} We have to verify that such a definition makes sense by checking that the Euclidean norm of the vector on the right hand side is 1. We introduce the notation $$ aW:=a_1W_1+a_2W_2,\quad a^\perp W:=-a_2W_1+a_1W_2, \quad bW:= b_1W_1+b_2W_2 $$ so that we can use the following facts: $$ \gamma_1 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3},\quad \gamma_2 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(aW+a_3)},\quad b \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{b_3}{a_3} a + \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} a^\perp,\quad a_3bW-b_3 aW \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu} a^\perp W. $$ This implies \begin{align*} &\frac{\mu^2 a_3^2}{4(\kappa^2-\mu)^2} \Big( \Big( \kappa^2\big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big)+2\kappa'\big(\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big)\Big)^2 + \Big( 2\kappa'\big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big)-2\kappa^2\big(\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big) \Big)^2 \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu^2 a_3^2 (\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2)}{4(\kappa^2-\mu)^2} \Big( \big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big)^2+ \big(\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big)^2\Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu^2 a_3^2}{\kappa^2-\mu} \Big( \big( \frac{a_3bW-b_3aW}{a_3(aW+a_3)}\big)^2+ \big( \frac{-\kappa^2aW + (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \big)^2\Big) \\ &= \frac{\big( \kappa\mu(a_3bW-b_3aW)\big)^2+ \big(-\kappa^2aW + (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3 \big)^2}{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ \kappa^2\mu(a^\perp W)^2 + \kappa^4(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ \kappa^2\mu |a|^2|W|^2 + (\kappa^4-\kappa^2\mu)(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{(aW)^2 +2a_3aW+ a_3^2}{(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= 1. \end{align*} Here we have used $\kappa^2|a|^2|W|^2=(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3^2$, see \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(i).
nodes.statement_short: Define phi via (36) and verify the defining vector has norm one.

nodes.name: Definition of the angle phi in the sufficiency part
nodes.statement: \vecII{\sin(\phi)}{\cos(\phi)} := \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}\matII{\kappa^2}{2\kappa'}{2\kappa'}{-\kappa^2} \vecII{\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}}{\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}}.
nodes.label: eq:formula_phi

nodes.name: Remaining ODE check
nodes.statement: It remains to check that $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi)$ satisfies the ODE~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to check the ODE system.

nodes.name: Verify gamma_1', gamma_2'
nodes.statement: To this end, we first rewrite the formulas for $\sin(\phi),\cos(\phi)$ from \eqref{eq:formula_phi} in the following way: \begin{align*} \sin(\phi) &= \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \kappa^2\big( \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\big) +2\kappa'\big( \frac{1}{\kappa(aW+a_3)}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu a_3}\big) \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \frac{\kappa^2( bW a_3-aW b_3)}{a_3(aW+a_3)} + \frac{2\kappa'( \mu a_3-\kappa^2 (aW+a_3))}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu a_3}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \frac{\kappa^2 a^\perp W}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} + \frac{2\kappa'( (\mu-\kappa^2) a_3- \kappa^2 aW)}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \Big) \\ &= \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu) a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}, \\ \cos(\phi) &= \frac{2\sqrt\mu \kappa' a^\perp W + \kappa^3 aW + \kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}. \end{align*} For the calculation of $\gamma_1',\gamma_2'$ we use the formula \begin{align*} W' = \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W + \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W^\perp \end{align*} from Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(ii),(iii). We obtain \begin{align*} \frac{\gamma_2'}{\gamma_2} &= - \frac{\kappa'}{\kappa} - \frac{aW'}{aW+a_3} \\ &= - \frac{\kappa'}{\kappa} - \frac{2\mu\kappa' aW - \sqrt\mu\kappa^3 a^\perp W }{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \frac{ \sqrt\mu \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \sin(\phi). \\ \intertext{Similarly, $|a|^2=a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2$ implies} \frac{\gamma_1'}{\gamma_2} &= \kappa(aW+a_3) \Big( \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}\Big)' \\ &= \kappa bW' -\kappa aW' \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3} \\ &= \kappa W' \big( -\frac{a^\perp W}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} a + \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3}a^\perp \big) \\ &= \frac{(2\sqrt\mu\kappa' W + \kappa^3 W^\perp) (- (a^\perp W) a + (aW+a_3)a^\perp)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^3 (a^\perp W)^2+\kappa^3 (aW)^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt\mu\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^3 |a|^2|W|^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt\mu\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{a_3\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu) + \kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt\mu\kappa' a^\perp W}{2(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \cos(\phi). \end{align*} Here, once again we used $\kappa^3|a|^2|W|^2 = \kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite sin(phi), cos(phi) and verify gamma_2'/gamma_2=sin(phi), gamma_1'/gamma_2=cos(phi).

nodes.name: Verify phi equation
nodes.statement: So we see that the equations for $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ from \eqref{eq:ODE_solution} are satisfied and it remains to verify the ODE for $\phi$. Having defined $\phi$ in \eqref{eq:formula_phi} in such a way that \eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} holds, we may differentiate these equations in order to derive the formula for $\phi'$. Differentiating \eqref{eq:b3a3_1} and using $\gamma_1'=\gamma_2\cos(\phi)$ as well as \eqref{eq:b3a3_2} we find \begin{align*} 2\kappa'(\kappa-\phi')\sin(\phi) + (\kappa^2\phi'+2\kappa-\kappa^3)\cos(\phi) = 2\kappa\cos(\phi)+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)\cos(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos^2(\phi) \end{align*} Differentiating \eqref{eq:b3a3_2} and using $\gamma_2'=\gamma_2\sin(\phi)$ as well as \eqref{eq:b3a3_2} we get \begin{align*} -2\kappa'(\kappa-\phi')\cos(\phi) + (\kappa^2\phi'+2\kappa-\kappa^3)\sin(\phi) = -2\kappa'\cos(\phi)+2\kappa \sin(\phi) -\kappa^2\sin(\phi)\cos(\phi) \end{align*} Multiplying the first equation with $\sin(\phi)$, the second with $-\cos(\phi)$ and adding up the resulting equations we arrive at $2\kappa'(\kappa-\phi')=2\kappa'\cos(\phi)$ and thus $\phi'+\cos(\phi)=\kappa$. So $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi)$ is a solution to the the ODE \eqref{eq:ODE_solution} and hence an orbitlike elastica, which is all we had to prove.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the a_3/b_3 identities to get phi'+cos(phi)=kappa.

nodes.name: Orbitlike elastica determined by three coefficients
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} shows that an orbitlike elastica with curvature is determined by fixing the three coefficients $a_1,a_2,b_3$. This is not surprising given the fact that the solutions of~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution} are uniquely determined by fixing three initial conditions for $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi$.

nodes.name: Proof of the ball criterion for Z
nodes.statement: From the definition of $Z$ in \eqref{eq:def_Z} we deduce the following:
nodes.statement_short: Direct consequence of the definition of Z.

nodes.name: Ball criterion for Z
nodes.statement: The inequality $Z(s;P)\geq -1+\rho>0$ holds if and only if $\gamma$ lies outside the Euclidean ball with center $(P_1,\rho P_2)$ and radius $\sqrt{\rho^2-1}|P_2|$. The same way, we have $Z(s;P)\leq -1+\rho$ if and only if $\gamma$ lies inside this ball.
nodes.statement_short: Z(s;P) >= -1+rho iff gamma(s) lies outside the Euclidean ball with centre (P_1, rho P_2) and radius sqrt(rho^2-1)|P_2|.
conclusions: The inequality $Z(s;P)\geq -1+\rho>0$ holds if and only if $\gamma$ lies outside the Euclidean ball with center $(P_1,\rho P_2)$ and radius $\sqrt{\rho^2-1}|P_2|$.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic circles are Euclidean circles
nodes.statement: Notice moreover that the above reasoning shows that hyperbolic circles with center $P$ and radius $\mathrm{Arcosh}(\rho)$ are nothing but Euclidean balls with center $(P_1,\rho P_2)$ and radius $\sqrt{\rho^2-1}|P_2|$ since both are characterized by the identity $Z(s;P)\equiv -1+\rho$, see~\eqref{eq:metric}.
nodes.statement_short: Hyperbolic circles with centre P and radius Arcosh(rho) are Euclidean balls with centre (P_1, rho P_2) and radius sqrt(rho^2-1)|P_2|.

nodes.name: Special point P with A=B=0 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: For $P_1=\frac{b_3}{a_3},P_2=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3}$ we have for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ $$ Z(s;P) = -1 + \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt\mu}. $$
nodes.statement_short: For P=(b_3/a_3, 1/(sqrt(mu) a_3)) the distance function reduces to Z = -1 + kappa/sqrt(mu).
conclusions: we have for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ $$ Z(s;P) = -1 + \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt\mu}. $$
nodes.label: prop:choice_of_P

nodes.name: Proof of Special point P with A=B=0 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: We will use the notation introduced in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike}. For the above choice of $P_1,P_2$ we deduce from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} and from $\kappa^2|a|^2||W|^2=(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3^2$ \begin{align*} \big(\gamma_1-P_1\big)^2+\big(\gamma_1-P_2\big)^2 &= \Big(\frac{a_3bW-b_3aW}{a_3(aW+a_3)}\Big)^2 + \Big( \frac{(\sqrt\mu-\kappa)a_3-\kappa aW}{\sqrt\mu \kappa a_3(aW+a_3)}\Big)^2 \\ &= \frac{\kappa^2 (a^\perp W)^2 +(\kappa-\sqrt\mu)^2a_3^2 +2\kappa(\kappa-\sqrt\mu)a_3aW + \kappa^2(aW)^2 }{\mu\kappa^2 a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^2 |a|^2|W|^2 +2\kappa(\kappa-\sqrt\mu)a_3aW+(\kappa-\sqrt\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\mu\kappa^2 a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{2\kappa(\kappa-\sqrt\mu) a_3^2 +2\kappa a_3(\kappa-\sqrt\mu)a_3aW}{\mu\kappa^2 a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{2}{\sqrt\mu a_3 \kappa(aW+a_3)} \big(-1+\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt\mu}\big) \\ &= 2P_2\gamma_2\big(-1+\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt\mu}\big), \end{align*} which is all we had to show.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation from the explicit formulas of Theorem 4.

nodes.name: Orbitlike elasticae oscillate between two circles
nodes.statement: We have $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ where \begin{align*} Q_1 &= \Big( \frac{b_3}{a_3},\frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\mu a_3}\Big),\qquad R_1 = \frac{\sqrt{2-\mu+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\mu a_3}, \\ Q_2 &= \Big( \frac{b_3}{a_3},\frac{\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\mu a_3}\Big),\qquad R_2 = \frac{\sqrt{2-\mu-2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\mu a_3}. \end{align*} The curve $\gamma$ touches $\partial B_{R_1}(Q_1)$ exactly when $\kappa$ attains its maximum and it touches $\partial B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ precisely when $\kappa$ attains its minimum.
nodes.statement_short: An orbitlike elastica lies in an explicit closed disc minus an explicit open disc, touching the outer circle at curvature maxima and the inner one at minima.
conclusions: We have $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$
The curve $\gamma$ touches $\partial B_{R_1}(Q_1)$ exactly when $\kappa$ attains its maximum and it touches $\partial B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ precisely when $\kappa$ attains its minimum.
nodes.label: prop:enclosures

nodes.name: Proof of Orbitlike elasticae oscillate between two circles
nodes.statement: We recall $\mu=\frac{4(1-k^2)}{(2-k^2)^2}$ and hence $k^2=\frac{2}{\mu}+\frac{2\sqrt{1-\mu}}{\mu}$. Then, choosing $P=(P_1,P_2)$ as in Proposition \ref{prop:choice_of_P} we obtain the inequalities \begin{align*} Z(s;P) &\leq -1 + \frac{\max \kappa}{\sqrt{\mu}} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} -1 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt\mu} = -1 + \frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{\mu}} =:-1+\rho_1, \\ Z(s;P) &\geq -1 + \frac{\min \kappa}{\sqrt{\mu}} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} -1 + \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt\mu} = -1 + \frac{\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{\mu}} =: -1+\rho_2. \end{align*} Hence we deduce $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ for $$ Q_1:= (P_1,\rho_1 P_2),\quad Q_2:= (P_1,\rho_2 P_2),\quad R_1:= \sqrt{\rho_1^2-1}|P_2|,\quad R_2:= \sqrt{\rho_2^2-1}|P_2|, $$ which proves the result.
nodes.statement_short: Bound Z(.;P) for the special P between -1+min kappa/sqrt mu and -1+max kappa/sqrt mu and translate into Euclidean balls.

nodes.name: Recall mu
nodes.statement: We recall $\mu=\frac{4(1-k^2)}{(2-k^2)^2}$ and hence $k^2=\frac{2}{\mu}+\frac{2\sqrt{1-\mu}}{\mu}$.
nodes.statement_short: Express k^2 in terms of mu.

nodes.name: Bound Z
nodes.statement: Then, choosing $P=(P_1,P_2)$ as in Proposition \ref{prop:choice_of_P} we obtain the inequalities \begin{align*} Z(s;P) &\leq -1 + \frac{\max \kappa}{\sqrt{\mu}} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} -1 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt\mu} = -1 + \frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{\mu}} =:-1+\rho_1, \\ Z(s;P) &\geq -1 + \frac{\min \kappa}{\sqrt{\mu}} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} -1 + \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt\mu} = -1 + \frac{\sqrt{2-2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{\mu}} =: -1+\rho_2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound Z(.;P) above and below via max and min of kappa.

nodes.name: Conclude enclosure
nodes.statement: Hence we deduce $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ for $$ Q_1:= (P_1,\rho_1 P_2),\quad Q_2:= (P_1,\rho_2 P_2),\quad R_1:= \sqrt{\rho_1^2-1}|P_2|,\quad R_2:= \sqrt{\rho_2^2-1}|P_2|, $$ which proves the result.
nodes.statement_short: Translate the bounds into the ball enclosure.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the rotation Delta theta_k
nodes.statement: The function $k\mapsto \Delta\theta_k$ decreases on $(0,1)$ from its upper limit $\sqrt{2}\pi$ to its lower limit $\pi$.
nodes.origin_citation: Langer & Singer, The total squared curvature of closed curves, Proposition 5.3
nodes.statement_short: k -> Delta theta_k decreases on (0,1) from sqrt(2) pi to pi.
conclusions: The function $k\mapsto \Delta\theta_k$ decreases on $(0,1)$ from its upper limit $\sqrt{2}\pi$ to its lower limit $\pi$.
nodes.label: prop:rotation

nodes.name: Proof of Monotonicity of the rotation Delta theta_k
nodes.statement: We recall $$ \Delta\theta_k = \pi - \pi\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k)+2\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k). $$ The derivative of this function with respect to $k$ can be computed as follows. From the formulas \eqref{eq:derivative_EK},\eqref{eq:derivative_Heuman} we get \begin{align*} \frac{d}{d k} \big(\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k)\big) &= -\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-k^2}} \frac{2(E(k)-(k')^4K(k))}{\pi\sqrt{1-(k')^4}} + \frac{2(E(k)-K(k))k'}{\pi\sqrt{1-(k')^4}} \\ &= \frac{2}{\pi k'\sqrt{2k^2-k^4}}\big(-E(k)+(k')^4K(k)+(k')^2E(k)-(k')^2K(k)\big) \\ &= -\frac{2k}{\pi k'\sqrt{2-k^2}}(E(k)+(k')^2K(k)), \\ \frac{d}{d k} \big(\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) \big) &= -\frac{k\sqrt{2-k^2}}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}K(k) -\frac{k\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}K(k) \\ &\; + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2} \frac{E(k)-(k')^2K(k)}{k(k')^2} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{2-k^2}}{k\sqrt{1-k^2}}E(k) + \frac{k^4-2}{k\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}}K(k). \end{align*} From these identities we get $$ \frac{d}{d k} \big( \Delta\theta_k\big) = \frac{2(2E(k)+(k^2-2)K(k))}{k\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}}, $$ and we have to show that the numerator is negative. In fact, the function $g(k):=2E(k)+(k^2-2)K(k)$ satisfies $g(0)=0$ as well as $g'(k)=k (k')^{-2} (-E(k)+(k')^2K(k))<0$. Indeed, $h(k):=-E(k)+(k')^2K(k)$ satisfies $h(0)=0$ as well as $h'(k)=-kK(k)<0$, see \eqref{eq:derivative_EK} for the formulas for $E'(k),K'(k)$. This proves $h<0$, hence $g'<0,g<0$ on $(0,1)$ and thus the monotonicity of $k\mapsto \Delta\theta_k$. Finally, evaluating $\Delta\theta_k$ for $k=0,k=1$ and using $K(0)=\frac{\pi}{2},\lim_{k\to 1} K(k)\sqrt{1-k^2}=0$ from 112.01 as well as $\Lambda_0(0,1)=0,\Lambda_0(\frac{\pi}{2},0)=1$ from 151.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} we find the values $\sqrt 2 \pi$ respectively $\pi$ so that the claim is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate Delta theta_k in k using derivatives of E, K and Heuman's Lambda; show the numerator is negative by two monotonicity arguments; evaluate the limits.

nodes.name: Recall definition
nodes.statement: We recall $$ \Delta\theta_k = \pi - \pi\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k)+2\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k). $$
nodes.statement_short: Recall the formula for Delta theta_k.

nodes.name: Differentiate
nodes.statement: The derivative of this function with respect to $k$ can be computed as follows. From the formulas \eqref{eq:derivative_EK},\eqref{eq:derivative_Heuman} we get \begin{align*} \frac{d}{d k} \big(\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k)\big) &= -\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-k^2}} \frac{2(E(k)-(k')^4K(k))}{\pi\sqrt{1-(k')^4}} + \frac{2(E(k)-K(k))k'}{\pi\sqrt{1-(k')^4}} \\ &= \frac{2}{\pi k'\sqrt{2k^2-k^4}}\big(-E(k)+(k')^4K(k)+(k')^2E(k)-(k')^2K(k)\big) \\ &= -\frac{2k}{\pi k'\sqrt{2-k^2}}(E(k)+(k')^2K(k)), \\ \frac{d}{d k} \big(\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) \big) &= -\frac{k\sqrt{2-k^2}}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}K(k) -\frac{k\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}K(k) \\ &\; + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2} \frac{E(k)-(k')^2K(k)}{k(k')^2} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{2-k^2}}{k\sqrt{1-k^2}}E(k) + \frac{k^4-2}{k\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}}K(k). \end{align*} From these identities we get $$ \frac{d}{d k} \big( \Delta\theta_k\big) = \frac{2(2E(k)+(k^2-2)K(k))}{k\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}}, $$ and we have to show that the numerator is negative.
nodes.statement_short: Compute d/dk Delta theta_k from derivatives of E, K, Lambda_0.

nodes.name: Sign of numerator
nodes.statement: In fact, the function $g(k):=2E(k)+(k^2-2)K(k)$ satisfies $g(0)=0$ as well as $g'(k)=k (k')^{-2} (-E(k)+(k')^2K(k))<0$. Indeed, $h(k):=-E(k)+(k')^2K(k)$ satisfies $h(0)=0$ as well as $h'(k)=-kK(k)<0$, see \eqref{eq:derivative_EK} for the formulas for $E'(k),K'(k)$. This proves $h<0$, hence $g'<0,g<0$ on $(0,1)$ and thus the monotonicity of $k\mapsto \Delta\theta_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Show g(k)=2E+(k^2-2)K<0 via h<0.

nodes.name: Limits
nodes.statement: Finally, evaluating $\Delta\theta_k$ for $k=0,k=1$ and using $K(0)=\frac{\pi}{2},\lim_{k\to 1} K(k)\sqrt{1-k^2}=0$ from 112.01 as well as $\Lambda_0(0,1)=0,\Lambda_0(\frac{\pi}{2},0)=1$ from 151.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} we find the values $\sqrt 2 \pi$ respectively $\pi$ so that the claim is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the limits sqrt(2) pi and pi at k=0,1.

nodes.name: Parameter k_{m,n}
nodes.statement: Therefore we define $k_{m,n}\in (0,1)$ to be the unique solution of the equation \begin{equation} \Delta\theta_k = \frac{2\pi m}{n} \end{equation} where $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ are natural numbers such that $1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2$, see Proposition~\ref{prop:rotation}.

nodes.name: Closedness condition defining k_{m,n}
nodes.statement: \Delta\theta_k = \frac{2\pi m}{n}
nodes.label: eq:closednedd_condition

nodes.name: Closed orbitlike elastica gamma_{m,n}
nodes.statement: The associated elastica with initial conditions $\gamma_1(0)=0,\gamma_2(0)=1,\phi(0)=0$ and $s_*=0$, say, will be denoted by $\gamma_{m,n}$.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic length L_{m,n}
nodes.statement: We now prove that for $k=k_{m,n}$ the elastica is closed with hyperbolic length $$ \mathcal{L}_{m,n}:=2n\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}). $$

nodes.name: Closedness criterion and winding number of orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement: The elastica $\gamma$ is closed if and only if $k=k_{m,n}$ for (w.l.o.g.) coprime integers $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$. In this case $\gamma=\gamma_{m,n}$ closes up after $n$ periods of its curvature function and its winding number around $(P_1,P_2)=(\frac{b_3}{a_3},\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3})$ is $m$.
nodes.statement_short: An orbitlike elastica closes iff k=k_{m,n}; then it closes after n curvature periods with winding number m around P.
conclusions: The elastica $\gamma$ is closed if and only if $k=k_{m,n}$ for (w.l.o.g.) coprime integers $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$.
In this case $\gamma=\gamma_{m,n}$ closes up after $n$ periods of its curvature function and its winding number around $(P_1,P_2)=(\frac{b_3}{a_3},\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3})$ is $m$.
nodes.label: prop:closed_and_winding_number

nodes.name: Proof of Closedness criterion and winding number of orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement: We first assume that $\gamma$ is closed, i.e. we have $\gamma(s+T)=\gamma(s)$ for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and some $T>0$. From Proposition \ref{prop:choice_of_P} we get that $T$ must be a multiple of the period of the curvature function, i.e. $T=2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
