Additionally, Theorem \ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} implies $W_1(s)=W_1(s+T),W_2(s)=W_2(s+T)$ because of $$ \det\matII{a_1}{a_2}{b_1}{b_2} = a_1 b_2-b_1a_2 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{a_1^2+a_2^2}{\sqrt\mu a_3} > 0. $$ Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(v), we have $n\Delta\theta_k\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$. Since $\Delta\theta_k$ is positive we find an $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $n\Delta\theta_k=2\pi m$, i.e. $k=k_{m,n}$ and $T=\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ for some $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2$. This proves the necessity of these conditions. Vice versa, $k=k_{m,n}$ is also sufficient for $\gamma_{m,n}$ to be closed. Indeed, from \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(v) we get that $\kappa,W_1,W_2$ are $\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$-periodic. Hence, $\gamma$ is $\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$-periodic thanks to the explicit formulas from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike}. \medskip It remains to calculate the winding number of $\gamma:=\gamma_{m,n}$, set $k:=k_{m,n}$. To this end we use the homotopy invariance of the winding number and first calculate the winding number for a more convenient curve, namely (in complex notation) $$ \eta(s):= \gamma_1(s)-\frac{b_3}{a_3} + i\cdot \Big(\gamma_2(s)\frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt{\mu}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3}\Big). $$ From Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} we get, using the notation from the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike}, \begin{align*} \eta &= \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}-\frac{b_3}{a_3} + i \Big( \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu (aW+a_3)} - \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \Big) \\ &= \frac{bWa_3 - b_3aW}{a_3(aW+a_3)} - i \frac{aW}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{a^\perp W}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} - i \frac{aW}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta}}{=} \frac{a_2\sin(\vartheta)+a_1\cos(\vartheta)}{N} + i\cdot \frac{a_1\sin(\vartheta)-a_2\cos(\vartheta)}{N} \end{align*} where $N:= \frac{\sqrt\mu\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}} a_3(aW+a_3)$ is a positive and $2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$-periodic function. Hence, we get from Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(ii) \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_0^{2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \frac{\eta'(s)}{\eta(s)}\,ds &= \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_0^{2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \big( - \frac{N'(s)}{N(s)} + i\vartheta'(s)\big) \,ds\\ &= \frac{1}{2\pi} \big(\vartheta(2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(0)\big) \\ &= \frac{n}{2\pi} \Delta\theta_k, \\ &= m. \end{align*} We now define the homotopy $$ (t,s)\mapsto \gamma_1(s)-\frac{b_3}{a_3} + i\cdot \Big( \gamma_2(s)\big(t\cdot \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt\mu}+1-t\big)-\frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \Big) $$ that connects the curve $\eta$ (at $t=1$) and the curve $\gamma-P_1-iP_2$ (at $t=0$). We intend to show that this homotopy is admissible, i.e. it is zero-free. To this end we choose $s\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the real part vanishes at $s$ and deduce that the imaginary part is non-zero. For a zero $s\in\mathbb{R}$ of the real part we have $a_3 \gamma_1(s)=b_3$, hence \begin{align*} a^\perp W(s) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \sqrt\mu a_3 (a_3bW(s) - b_3aW(s)) \\ &= \sqrt\mu (a_3(bW(s)+b_3)-b_3(aW(s)+a_3)) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \sqrt\mu (aW(s)+a_3)(a_3\gamma_1(s)- b_3) \\ &= 0. \end{align*} Due to \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(i) this implies $aW(s)= \pm |a||W(s)|= \pm a_3 \sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}/\kappa(s)$ and thus $$ \gamma_2(s) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)(aW(s)+a_3)} = \frac{1}{a_3(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))}. $$ From this we deduce \begin{align*} \gamma_2(s)\big(t\cdot \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt\mu}+1-t\big)-\frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} &= \frac{t(\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu)+\sqrt\mu -(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))}{\sqrt\mu a_3(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu} \cdot \big( (t-1)\sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu}\mp \sqrt{\kappa(s)+\sqrt{\mu}} \big)}{\sqrt\mu a_3(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))} \\ &\neq 0 \end{align*} because of $|(t-1)\sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu}|\leq \sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu}<\sqrt{\kappa(s)+\sqrt\mu}$. Hence, the homotopy is admissible so that the winding number of $\gamma$ around $P$ is $m$.
nodes.statement_short: Periodicity of kappa and quasi-periodicity of W_1+iW_2 give closedness iff n Delta theta_k in 2 pi Z; the winding number is computed for an auxiliary curve and transferred by an admissible homotopy.

nodes.name: Necessity of k=k_{m,n}
nodes.statement: We first assume that $\gamma$ is closed, i.e. we have $\gamma(s+T)=\gamma(s)$ for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and some $T>0$. From Proposition \ref{prop:choice_of_P} we get that $T$ must be a multiple of the period of the curvature function, i.e. $T=2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Additionally, Theorem \ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} implies $W_1(s)=W_1(s+T),W_2(s)=W_2(s+T)$ because of $$ \det\matII{a_1}{a_2}{b_1}{b_2} = a_1 b_2-b_1a_2 \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{a_1^2+a_2^2}{\sqrt\mu a_3} > 0. $$ Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(v), we have $n\Delta\theta_k\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$. Since $\Delta\theta_k$ is positive we find an $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $n\Delta\theta_k=2\pi m$, i.e. $k=k_{m,n}$ and $T=\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ for some $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2$. This proves the necessity of these conditions.
nodes.statement_short: Closedness forces period multiple and n Delta theta_k in 2 pi Z.

nodes.name: Sufficiency
nodes.statement: Vice versa, $k=k_{m,n}$ is also sufficient for $\gamma_{m,n}$ to be closed. Indeed, from \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(v) we get that $\kappa,W_1,W_2$ are $\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$-periodic. Hence, $\gamma$ is $\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$-periodic thanks to the explicit formulas from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike}.
nodes.statement_short: For k=k_{m,n}, kappa, W_1, W_2 and hence gamma are L_{m,n}-periodic.

nodes.name: Winding number task
nodes.statement: It remains to calculate the winding number of $\gamma:=\gamma_{m,n}$, set $k:=k_{m,n}$.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to compute the winding number.

nodes.name: Winding of auxiliary curve
nodes.statement: To this end we use the homotopy invariance of the winding number and first calculate the winding number for a more convenient curve, namely (in complex notation) $$ \eta(s):= \gamma_1(s)-\frac{b_3}{a_3} + i\cdot \Big(\gamma_2(s)\frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt{\mu}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}a_3}\Big). $$ From Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} we get, using the notation from the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike}, \begin{align*} \eta &= \frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}-\frac{b_3}{a_3} + i \Big( \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu (aW+a_3)} - \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \Big) \\ &= \frac{bWa_3 - b_3aW}{a_3(aW+a_3)} - i \frac{aW}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{a^\perp W}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} - i \frac{aW}{\sqrt\mu a_3(aW+a_3)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta}}{=} \frac{a_2\sin(\vartheta)+a_1\cos(\vartheta)}{N} + i\cdot \frac{a_1\sin(\vartheta)-a_2\cos(\vartheta)}{N} \end{align*} where $N:= \frac{\sqrt\mu\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}} a_3(aW+a_3)$ is a positive and $2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$-periodic function. Hence, we get from Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(ii) \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_0^{2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \frac{\eta'(s)}{\eta(s)}\,ds &= \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_0^{2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \big( - \frac{N'(s)}{N(s)} + i\vartheta'(s)\big) \,ds\\ &= \frac{1}{2\pi} \big(\vartheta(2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(0)\big) \\ &= \frac{n}{2\pi} \Delta\theta_k, \\ &= m. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the winding number m of the auxiliary curve eta via vartheta.

nodes.name: Homotopy
nodes.statement: We now define the homotopy $$ (t,s)\mapsto \gamma_1(s)-\frac{b_3}{a_3} + i\cdot \Big( \gamma_2(s)\big(t\cdot \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt\mu}+1-t\big)-\frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \Big) $$ that connects the curve $\eta$ (at $t=1$) and the curve $\gamma-P_1-iP_2$ (at $t=0$). We intend to show that this homotopy is admissible, i.e. it is zero-free. To this end we choose $s\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the real part vanishes at $s$ and deduce that the imaginary part is non-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Define a homotopy from eta to gamma-P.

nodes.name: Admissibility
nodes.statement: For a zero $s\in\mathbb{R}$ of the real part we have $a_3 \gamma_1(s)=b_3$, hence \begin{align*} a^\perp W(s) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \sqrt\mu a_3 (a_3bW(s) - b_3aW(s)) \\ &= \sqrt\mu (a_3(bW(s)+b_3)-b_3(aW(s)+a_3)) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \sqrt\mu (aW(s)+a_3)(a_3\gamma_1(s)- b_3) \\ &= 0. \end{align*} Due to \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(i) this implies $aW(s)= \pm |a||W(s)|= \pm a_3 \sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}/\kappa(s)$ and thus $$ \gamma_2(s) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)(aW(s)+a_3)} = \frac{1}{a_3(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))}. $$ From this we deduce \begin{align*} \gamma_2(s)\big(t\cdot \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt\mu}+1-t\big)-\frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} &= \frac{t(\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu)+\sqrt\mu -(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))}{\sqrt\mu a_3(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu} \cdot \big( (t-1)\sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu}\mp \sqrt{\kappa(s)+\sqrt{\mu}} \big)}{\sqrt\mu a_3(\pm\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}+\kappa(s))} \\ &\neq 0 \end{align*} because of $|(t-1)\sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu}|\leq \sqrt{\kappa(s)-\sqrt\mu}<\sqrt{\kappa(s)+\sqrt\mu}$.
nodes.statement_short: Show the homotopy has no zeros.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, the homotopy is admissible so that the winding number of $\gamma$ around $P$ is $m$.
nodes.statement_short: Winding number of gamma around P is m.

nodes.name: Selfintersection
nodes.statement: Such a selfintersection occurs if there are $s,t$ with $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ and $\gamma_{m,n}(s)=\gamma_{m,n}(t)$.

nodes.name: Number of selfintersections
nodes.statement: The number of $s$, for which such $t\in (s,\mathcal{L}_{m,n})$ exist, is defined as the number of selfintersections.

nodes.name: Nonclosed orbitlike elasticae selfintersect infinitely often
nodes.statement: We remark that in the nonclosed case essentially the same proof shows that the elasticae selfintersect infinitely many times.

nodes.name: Number of selfintersections of gamma_{m,n}
nodes.statement: Let $m,n\in \mathbb{N}$ be coprime such that $1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2$. Then the closed orbitlike elastica $\gamma_{m,n}$ has precisely $n(m-1)$ points of selfintersection characterized by the unique solutions $0\leq s<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ of the $n(m-1)$ equations \begin{equation} \frac{\vartheta(s)}{\pi} =\frac{(l-1)m}{n}-p \end{equation} where $l,p\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy the following conditions: \begin{align} \begin{aligned} l\in\{1,\ldots,2n-1\},\qquad p\in \big\{1,\ldots, \Big\lceil \frac{\min\{l,2n-l\}m}{n}\Big\rceil -1 \big\}. \end{aligned} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The closed orbitlike elastica gamma_{m,n} has exactly n(m-1) simple selfintersections, given by explicit equations for vartheta.
conclusions: Then the closed orbitlike elastica $\gamma_{m,n}$ has precisely $n(m-1)$ points of selfintersection

nodes.name: Selfintersection equations
nodes.statement: \frac{\vartheta(s)}{\pi} =\frac{(l-1)m}{n}-p
nodes.label: eq:selfintersections

nodes.name: Index conditions for selfintersections
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} l\in\{1,\ldots,2n-1\},\qquad p\in \big\{1,\ldots, \Big\lceil \frac{\min\{l,2n-l\}m}{n}\Big\rceil -1 \big\}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions

nodes.name: Proof of Number of selfintersections of gamma_{m,n}
nodes.statement: The equality $\gamma(s)=\gamma(t)$ for $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ is equivalent to $Z(s;P)=Z(t;P)$ for all $P\in\mathbb{R}^2,P_2\neq 0$. Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_orbitlike} and Proposition~\ref{prop:choice_of_P} show that this is in turn equivalent to $\kappa(s)=\kappa(t),W_1(s)=W_1(t),W_2(s)=W_2(t)$. So our aim is to show that these equalities and $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ are equivalent to \eqref{eq:selfintersections},\eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}. The equation $\kappa(s)=\kappa(t)$ and the explicit form of the curvature function from~\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike} give $$ \text{(i)}\; s= t+2l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) \quad\text{or}\quad \text{(ii)}\; s =- t +2l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) $$ for some $l\in\mathbb{Z}$. In the case (i) we have by Proposition \ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(v) $$ W_1(s)+iW_2(s) = (W_1(t)+iW_2(t))e^{il\Delta\theta_{k_{m,n}}} = (W_1(s)+iW_2(s))e^{i\frac{2\pi lm}{n}}. $$ Since $m,n$ are coprime and $s<t$ this implies $l\in -n\mathbb{N}$ and hence $$ s = t + 2l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) \leq t - 2n\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) = t-\mathcal{L}_{m,n} < 0, $$ a contradiction. So this is impossible. In the case (ii) we get from Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(vi) \begin{align*} i|W(s)|e^{i\vartheta(s)} &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta}}{=} i(W_2(s)-iW_1(s)) \\ &= W_1(s)+iW_2(s) \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}.(vi)}{=} \big( -W_1(t) + i W_2(t)\big)e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_{k_{m,n}}}\\ &= \big( -W_1(s) + i W_2(s)\big)e^{i\frac{2\pi(l-1)m}{n}}\\ &= i\overline{\big( W_2(s) -i W_1(s)\big)}e^{i\frac{2\pi(l-1)m}{n}}\\ &= i |W(s)| e^{i(-\vartheta(s)+\frac{2\pi(l-1)m}{n})}. \end{align*} This shows that intersection points occur precisely at those $s\in [0,\mathcal{L}_{m,n})$ where \eqref{eq:selfintersections} holds for some $p\in\mathbb{Z}$. Notice that $\vartheta$ is increasing by Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike} so that a unique solution $s$ in $\mathbb{R}$ exists for any given $p\in\mathbb{Z}$. So it remains to show that the condition~\eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions} is equivalent to $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ and that these conditions are satisfied for precisely $n(m-1)$ distinct pairs $(l,p)$. To this end we use Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(i). Thanks to this result the condition $s\geq 0$ is equivalent to \begin{equation} \vartheta(s) \geq \vartheta(0) = -\frac{\Delta\theta_k}{2}=-\frac{\pi m}{n}. \end{equation} The condition $t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ is equivalent to $s>2(l-n)\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ and thus to \begin{equation} \vartheta(s) > \vartheta(2(l-n)\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n})) = \frac{2l-2n-1}{2}\Delta\theta_k = \frac{\pi(2l-2n-1)m}{n}. \end{equation} The last condition $s<t$ holds if and only if $s<l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ and thus precisely if \begin{equation} \vartheta(s)<\vartheta(l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}))= \frac{\pi(l-1)m}{n}. \end{equation} Altogether the conditions \eqref{eq:selfintersections1}--\eqref{eq:selfintersections3} and $\vartheta(s) = \frac{\pi(l-1)m}{n} - \pi p$ lead to the conditions $$ 0<p\leq \frac{lm}{n}\quad\text{and}\quad p< \frac{m(2n-l)}{n}. $$ Since $m,n$ are coprime these inequalities for integers $p,l\in\mathbb{Z}$ yield the conditions \eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}. Notice that the solutions are different from each other because $m$ and $n$ are coprime. Indeed, if $(l,p),(\tilde l,\tilde p)$ are two pairs satisfying \eqref{eq:selfintersections},\eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}, then $l-\tilde l$ is a multiple of $n$, say $l-\tilde l=qn$ for $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$. In the case $q\geq 2$ we get a contradiction due to $$ l = qn+\tilde l \geq 2n+\tilde l > 2n-1. $$ In the case $q=1$ we find $m=p-\tilde p$ and thus a contradiction results from $$ p = \tilde p+m \geq 1+m > \Big\lceil \frac{\min\{l,2n-l\}m}{n}\Big\rceil -1. $$ This proves that we have precisely as many intersection points as pairs $(l,p)$ satisfying \eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}. So it remains to show that the number of these pairs is $n(m-1)$. By \eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions} the number of equations is $$ \sum_{l=1}^{2n-1} \big( \big\lceil \frac{\min\{l,2n-l\}m}{n}\big\rceil -1 \big) = 2\sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil \frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil + m -(2n-1) $$ Since $m,n$ are coprime the sum can be computed as follows: \begin{align*} \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil &= \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil\frac{(n-l)m}{n}\big\rceil \;=\; \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big( m + \big\lceil -\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil \big) \\ &= m(n-1) + \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big(-\big\lceil\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil+1\big) \\ &= (m+1)(n-1) - \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil. \end{align*} Hence, the number of equations is $m-(2n-1)+(m+1)(n-1)=n(m-1)$, which is all we had to show.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce gamma(s)=gamma(t) to equality of kappa, W_1, W_2; split into translation and reflection cases, rule out the first, translate the second into equations for vartheta and count the admissible (l,p) pairs.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: The equality $\gamma(s)=\gamma(t)$ for $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ is equivalent to $Z(s;P)=Z(t;P)$ for all $P\in\mathbb{R}^2,P_2\neq 0$. Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_orbitlike} and Proposition~\ref{prop:choice_of_P} show that this is in turn equivalent to $\kappa(s)=\kappa(t),W_1(s)=W_1(t),W_2(s)=W_2(t)$. So our aim is to show that these equalities and $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ are equivalent to \eqref{eq:selfintersections},\eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}.
nodes.statement_short: Selfintersection iff kappa, W_1, W_2 agree at s and t.

nodes.name: Two cases from kappa
nodes.statement: The equation $\kappa(s)=\kappa(t)$ and the explicit form of the curvature function from~\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike} give $$ \text{(i)}\; s= t+2l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) \quad\text{or}\quad \text{(ii)}\; s =- t +2l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) $$ for some $l\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Equal curvature gives translation or reflection relation between s and t.

nodes.name: Case (i) impossible
nodes.statement: In the case (i) we have by Proposition \ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(v) $$ W_1(s)+iW_2(s) = (W_1(t)+iW_2(t))e^{il\Delta\theta_{k_{m,n}}} = (W_1(s)+iW_2(s))e^{i\frac{2\pi lm}{n}}. $$ Since $m,n$ are coprime and $s<t$ this implies $l\in -n\mathbb{N}$ and hence $$ s = t + 2l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) \leq t - 2n\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}) = t-\mathcal{L}_{m,n} < 0, $$ a contradiction. So this is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Translation case contradicts s<t.

nodes.name: Case (ii)
nodes.statement: In the case (ii) we get from Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(vi) \begin{align*} i|W(s)|e^{i\vartheta(s)} &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta}}{=} i(W_2(s)-iW_1(s)) \\ &= W_1(s)+iW_2(s) \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}.(vi)}{=} \big( -W_1(t) + i W_2(t)\big)e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_{k_{m,n}}}\\ &= \big( -W_1(s) + i W_2(s)\big)e^{i\frac{2\pi(l-1)m}{n}}\\ &= i\overline{\big( W_2(s) -i W_1(s)\big)}e^{i\frac{2\pi(l-1)m}{n}}\\ &= i |W(s)| e^{i(-\vartheta(s)+\frac{2\pi(l-1)m}{n})}. \end{align*} This shows that intersection points occur precisely at those $s\in [0,\mathcal{L}_{m,n})$ where \eqref{eq:selfintersections} holds for some $p\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reflection case yields the vartheta equations.

nodes.name: Unique solutions
nodes.statement: Notice that $\vartheta$ is increasing by Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike} so that a unique solution $s$ in $\mathbb{R}$ exists for any given $p\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: vartheta increasing gives unique s for each p.

nodes.name: Remaining conditions
nodes.statement: So it remains to show that the condition~\eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions} is equivalent to $0\leq s<t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ and that these conditions are satisfied for precisely $n(m-1)$ distinct pairs $(l,p)$.
nodes.statement_short: Remains to translate the range conditions and count pairs.

nodes.name: Range conditions
nodes.statement: To this end we use Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(i). Thanks to this result the condition $s\geq 0$ is equivalent to \begin{equation} \vartheta(s) \geq \vartheta(0) = -\frac{\Delta\theta_k}{2}=-\frac{\pi m}{n}. \end{equation} The condition $t<\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$ is equivalent to $s>2(l-n)\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ and thus to \begin{equation} \vartheta(s) > \vartheta(2(l-n)\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n})) = \frac{2l-2n-1}{2}\Delta\theta_k = \frac{\pi(2l-2n-1)m}{n}. \end{equation} The last condition $s<t$ holds if and only if $s<l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ and thus precisely if \begin{equation} \vartheta(s)<\vartheta(l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}))= \frac{\pi(l-1)m}{n}. \end{equation} Altogether the conditions \eqref{eq:selfintersections1}--\eqref{eq:selfintersections3} and $\vartheta(s) = \frac{\pi(l-1)m}{n} - \pi p$ lead to the conditions $$ 0<p\leq \frac{lm}{n}\quad\text{and}\quad p< \frac{m(2n-l)}{n}. $$ Since $m,n$ are coprime these inequalities for integers $p,l\in\mathbb{Z}$ yield the conditions \eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}.
nodes.statement_short: Translate s>=0, t<L, s<t into conditions on (l,p).

nodes.name: Condition s>=0
nodes.statement: \vartheta(s) \geq \vartheta(0) = -\frac{\Delta\theta_k}{2}=-\frac{\pi m}{n}.
nodes.label: eq:selfintersections1

nodes.name: Condition t<L_{m,n}
nodes.statement: \vartheta(s) > \vartheta(2(l-n)\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n})) = \frac{2l-2n-1}{2}\Delta\theta_k = \frac{\pi(2l-2n-1)m}{n}.
nodes.label: eq:selfintersections2

nodes.name: Condition s<t
nodes.statement: \vartheta(s)<\vartheta(l\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}K(k_{m,n}))= \frac{\pi(l-1)m}{n}.
nodes.label: eq:selfintersections3

nodes.name: Distinctness
nodes.statement: Notice that the solutions are different from each other because $m$ and $n$ are coprime. Indeed, if $(l,p),(\tilde l,\tilde p)$ are two pairs satisfying \eqref{eq:selfintersections},\eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}, then $l-\tilde l$ is a multiple of $n$, say $l-\tilde l=qn$ for $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$. In the case $q\geq 2$ we get a contradiction due to $$ l = qn+\tilde l \geq 2n+\tilde l > 2n-1. $$ In the case $q=1$ we find $m=p-\tilde p$ and thus a contradiction results from $$ p = \tilde p+m \geq 1+m > \Big\lceil \frac{\min\{l,2n-l\}m}{n}\Big\rceil -1. $$ This proves that we have precisely as many intersection points as pairs $(l,p)$ satisfying \eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions}.
nodes.statement_short: Distinct pairs give distinct intersection points.

nodes.name: Counting task
nodes.statement: So it remains to show that the number of these pairs is $n(m-1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Remains to count the pairs.

nodes.name: Count
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:selfintersection_lp_conditions} the number of equations is $$ \sum_{l=1}^{2n-1} \big( \big\lceil \frac{\min\{l,2n-l\}m}{n}\big\rceil -1 \big) = 2\sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil \frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil + m -(2n-1) $$ Since $m,n$ are coprime the sum can be computed as follows: \begin{align*} \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil &= \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil\frac{(n-l)m}{n}\big\rceil \;=\; \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big( m + \big\lceil -\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil \big) \\ &= m(n-1) + \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big(-\big\lceil\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil+1\big) \\ &= (m+1)(n-1) - \sum_{l=1}^{n-1} \big\lceil\frac{lm}{n}\big\rceil. \end{align*} Hence, the number of equations is $m-(2n-1)+(m+1)(n-1)=n(m-1)$, which is all we had to show.
nodes.statement_short: Sum of ceilings equals n(m-1) for coprime m,n.

nodes.name: Willmore energy W_{m,n} and selfintersection number S_{m,n}
nodes.statement: The table contains $k_{m,n}$, the hyperbolic length $\mathcal{L}_{m,n}$, the number of selfintersections $\mathcal{S}_{m,n}=n(m-1)$ and the Willmore energy \begin{align*} \mathcal{W}_{m,n} := \mathcal{W}(\Sigma_{\gamma_{m,n}}) = \frac{\pi}{2} \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} \kappa^2 \,ds = \frac{4n\pi E(k_{m,n})}{\sqrt{2-k_{m,n}^2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: W_{m,n} is the Willmore energy of the surface generated by gamma_{m,n}, equal to 4 n pi E(k_{m,n})/sqrt(2-k_{m,n}^2).

nodes.name: Second variation functional I_{m,n}
nodes.statement: As pointed out by Langer and Singer (see equation (1.4) in \cite{LanSing_the_total}) the stability of $\gamma_{m,n}$ is determined by the integral $$ I_{m,n}(\phi) := \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} 2\phi''(s)^2-(5\kappa(s)^2-4)\phi'(s)^2+ (6\kappa'(s)^2-\kappa(s)^4+3\kappa(s)^2 + 2)\phi(s)^2 \,ds. $$

nodes.name: Stability of gamma_{m,n}
nodes.statement: The elastica $\gamma_{m,n}$ is said to be stable if the above functional is nonnegative, otherwise we will say that it is unstable.
differentia: if the above functional is nonnegative

nodes.name: Instability criterion for gamma_{m,n}
nodes.statement: The curve $\gamma_{m,n}$ is unstable provided \begin{align*} n > \frac{A(k_{m,n})+\sqrt{A(k_{m,n})^2+4B(k_{m,n})C(k_{m,n})}}{2C(k_{m,n})} \end{align*} where \begin{align*} A(k) &:= \frac{\pi\sqrt{5E(k)-(2-k^2)K(k)}}{(2-k^2)K(k)^{3/2}},\\ B(k) &:= \frac{\pi^2}{(2-k^2)K(k)^2}, \\ C(k) &:= \frac{\sqrt{(16(1-k^2)K(k)^2-44(2-k^2)E(k)K(k)+75E(k)^2)_+}}{\sqrt{3}(2-k^2)K(k)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: gamma_{m,n} is unstable when n exceeds an explicit threshold built from elliptic integrals A(k),B(k),C(k).
conclusions: The curve $\gamma_{m,n}$ is unstable
nodes.label: lem:instability

nodes.name: Proof of Instability criterion for gamma_{m,n}
nodes.statement:
Set $k:=k_{m,n}, T:= \mathcal{L}_{m,n}/2\pi=n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)/\pi$. We define the Fourier coefficients $\alpha_j, eta_j$ via  egin{align*} 5\kappa(s)^2-4 = \sum_{j=0}^\infty \alpha_j \cos\Big(  rac{js}{T}\Big),\qquad 6\kappa'(s)^2-\kappa(s)^4+3\kappa(s)^2 + 2 = \sum_{j=0}^\infty  eta_j \cos\Big(  rac{js}{T}\Big). \end{align*} From 110.03 respectively ootnote{We remark that 361.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} contains a typo: $E(u)$ has to be replaced by $E(\mathrm{sn}(u,k),k)$ in our notation and by $E(\arcsin(\mathrm{sn} u),k)$ in the notation used in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}.} 361.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} we get  egin{align*} \int_0^{2\pi T} \kappa(s)^2\,ds &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=}  rac{4}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \int_0^{2nK(k)} \mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2\,ds \ &=  rac{8n}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \int_0^{K(k)} \mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2\,ds \ &=  rac{8n E(k)}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}, \ \int_0^{2\pi T} \kappa'(s)^2\,ds &=  rac{4k^4}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \int_0^{2nK(k)} \mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2\mathrm{cn}(s,k)^2\,ds \ &=  rac{8nk^4}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \int_0^{K(k)} \mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2\mathrm{cn}(s,k)^2\,ds \ &=  rac{8n ig((2-k^2)E(k)-2(1-k^2)K(k) ig)}{3(2-k^2)^{3/2}}. \end{align*} From these identities and $\kappa^4=4(\kappa^2-(\kappa')^2-\mu)$ we deduce  egin{align*} \alpha_0 &=  rac{1}{2\pi T} \int_0^{2\pi T} (5\kappa(s)^2-4)\,ds \;=\;  rac{20E(k)}{(2-k^2)K(k)}-4,\  eta_0 &=  rac{1}{2\pi T} \int_0^{2\pi T} (10\kappa'(s)^2-\kappa(s)^2 + 2+4\mu)\,ds \ &= 10\cdot  rac{2 ig( (2-k^2)E(k)-4(1-k^2)K(k) ig)}{3(2-k^2)^2K(k)} -  rac{4E(k)}{(2-k^2)K(k)} + 2+4\mu \ &=  rac{28(2-k^2)E(k)-80(1-k^2)K(k)}{3(2-k^2)^2K(k)} +  rac{24-24k^2+2k^4}{(2-k^2)^2} \ &=  rac{28(2-k^2)E(k)+2(3k^2-2)(k^2+2)K(k)}{3(2-k^2)^2K(k)}. \end{align*} Now we calculate $I_{m,n}(\phi)$ for the function $\phi(s):= \cos(js/T)$ with $2j
otin n\mathbb{N}_0$. Since $\alpha_j= eta_j=0$ for $j
otin n\mathbb{N}_0$ and $$ \phi(s)^2 =  rac{1}{2} ig(1+\cos(2js/T) ig),\quad \phi'(s)^2= rac{j^2}{2T^2} ig(1-\cos(2js/T) ig),\quad \phi''(s)^2 =  rac{j^4}{2T^4} ig(1+\cos(2js/T) ig) $$ we may evaluate the integrals as follows:  egin{align*} \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} 2\phi''(s)^2\,ds &=  rac{2\pi^4 j^4}{(\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k))^3}, \ \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} (5\kappa(s)^2-4)\phi'(s)^2\,ds &=  rac{\alpha_0 \pi^2 j^2 }{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}, \ \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} (6\kappa'(s)^2-\kappa(s)^4+3\kappa(s)^2 + 2)\phi(s)^2 \,ds &=  eta_0 \sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k) \end{align*} and thus $$ I_{m,n}(\phi) = 2\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k) \cdot \Big( \Big( ig( rac{\pi j}{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)} ig)^2-  rac{\alpha_0}{4}\Big)^2 +  rac{8 eta_0-\alpha_0^2}{16} \Big). $$ So the natural choice is $$ j= ig\lfloor  rac{\sqrt{\alpha_0}\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}{2\pi}  igfloor \quad	ext{or}\quad j= \lceil  rac{\sqrt{\alpha_0}\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}{2\pi} ceil\quad	ext{s.t. } 2j
otin n\mathbb{N}_0. $$ Since one of these $j$ in fact satisfies $2j
otin n\mathbb{N}_0$ (because of $n\geq 3$ due to $ rac{2m}{n}\in (1,\sqrt 2),m\in\mathbb{N}$) we obtain $I_{m,n}(\phi)<0$ provided $$ \Big( ig( rac{\sqrt\alpha_0}{2}+ rac{\pi}{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)} ig)^2-  rac{\alpha_0}{4}\Big)^2 +  rac{8 eta_0-\alpha_0^2}{16}, $$ which in turn is equivalent to $$  rac{\pi\sqrt{\alpha_0}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)} +  rac{\pi^2}{(2-k^2)n^2K(k)^2} <  rac{\sqrt{(\alpha_0^2-8 eta_0)_+}}{4}. $$ Since this inequality can be rewritten as $ rac{A(k)}{n} +  rac{B(k)}{n^2}<C(k)$ we get the result.
nodes.statement_short: Monochromatic test function cos(js/T) in the second variation: compute Fourier means alpha_0, beta_0 via elliptic integrals and choose j to make I_{m,n} negative.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients
nodes.statement: Set $k:=k_{m,n}, T:= \mathcal{L}_{m,n}/2\pi=n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)/\pi$. We define the Fourier coefficients $\alpha_j,\beta_j$ via \begin{align*} 5\kappa(s)^2-4 = \sum_{j=0}^\infty \alpha_j \cos\Big( \frac{js}{T}\Big),\qquad 6\kappa'(s)^2-\kappa(s)^4+3\kappa(s)^2 + 2 = \sum_{j=0}^\infty \beta_j \cos\Big( \frac{js}{T}\Big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Set T and define Fourier coefficients alpha_j, beta_j.

nodes.name: Integrals of kappa^2, kappa'^2
nodes.statement: From 110.03 respectively\footnote{We remark that 361.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} contains a typo: $E(u)$ has to be replaced by $E(\mathrm{sn}(u,k),k)$ in our notation and by $E(\arcsin(\mathrm{sn} u),k)$ in the notation used in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}.} 361.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} we get \begin{align*} \int_0^{2\pi T} \kappa(s)^2\,ds &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} \frac{4}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \int_0^{2nK(k)} \mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2\,ds \\ &= \frac{8n}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \int_0^{K(k)} \mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2\,ds \\ &= \frac{8n E(k)}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}, \\ \int_0^{2\pi T} \kappa'(s)^2\,ds &= \frac{4k^4}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \int_0^{2nK(k)} \mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2\mathrm{cn}(s,k)^2\,ds \\ &= \frac{8nk^4}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \int_0^{K(k)} \mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2\mathrm{cn}(s,k)^2\,ds \\ &= \frac{8n\big((2-k^2)E(k)-2(1-k^2)K(k)\big)}{3(2-k^2)^{3/2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate integrals via Byrd-Friedman formulas.

nodes.name: Mean coefficients
nodes.statement_short: Compute alpha_0 and beta_0.

nodes.name: Evaluate I
nodes.statement: Now we calculate $I_{m,n}(\phi)$ for the function $\phi(s):= \cos(js/T)$ with $2j\notin n\mathbb{N}_0$. Since $\alpha_j=\beta_j=0$ for $j\notin n\mathbb{N}_0$ and $$ \phi(s)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\big(1+\cos(2js/T)\big),\quad \phi'(s)^2=\frac{j^2}{2T^2}\big(1-\cos(2js/T)\big),\quad \phi''(s)^2 = \frac{j^4}{2T^4}\big(1+\cos(2js/T)\big) $$ we may evaluate the integrals as follows: \begin{align*} \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} 2\phi''(s)^2\,ds &= \frac{2\pi^4 j^4}{(\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k))^3}, \\ \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} (5\kappa(s)^2-4)\phi'(s)^2\,ds &= \frac{\alpha_0 \pi^2 j^2 }{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}, \\ \int_0^{\mathcal{L}_{m,n}} (6\kappa'(s)^2-\kappa(s)^4+3\kappa(s)^2 + 2)\phi(s)^2 \,ds &= \beta_0 \sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k) \end{align*} and thus $$ I_{m,n}(\phi) = 2\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k) \cdot \Big( \Big(\big(\frac{\pi j}{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}\big)^2- \frac{\alpha_0}{4}\Big)^2 + \frac{8\beta_0-\alpha_0^2}{16} \Big). $$
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate I_{m,n} on cos(js/T).

nodes.name: Choose j
nodes.statement: So the natural choice is $$ j=\big\lfloor \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_0}\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}{2\pi} \big\rfloor \quad\text{or}\quad j= \lceil \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_0}\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}{2\pi} \rceil\quad\text{s.t. } 2j\notin n\mathbb{N}_0. $$
nodes.statement_short: Choose j near sqrt(alpha_0) n K/(2 pi).

nodes.name: Negativity condition
nodes.statement: Since one of these $j$ in fact satisfies $2j\notin n\mathbb{N}_0$ (because of $n\geq 3$ due to $\frac{2m}{n}\in (1,\sqrt 2),m\in\mathbb{N}$) we obtain $I_{m,n}(\phi)<0$ provided $$ \Big(\big(\frac{\sqrt\alpha_0}{2}+\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)}\big)^2- \frac{\alpha_0}{4}\Big)^2 + \frac{8\beta_0-\alpha_0^2}{16}, $$ which in turn is equivalent to $$ \frac{\pi\sqrt{\alpha_0}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}nK(k)} + \frac{\pi^2}{(2-k^2)n^2K(k)^2} < \frac{\sqrt{(\alpha_0^2-8\beta_0)_+}}{4}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Derive the inequality ensuring I<0.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since this inequality can be rewritten as $\frac{A(k)}{n} + \frac{B(k)}{n^2}<C(k)$ we get the result.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite as A/n+B/n^2<C.

nodes.name: Scope of the instability criterion
nodes.statement: This criterion proves the instability of infinitely many of the $\gamma_{m,n}$ but also infinitely many of them are not covered. Only one of the curves $\gamma_{m,n}$ listed in Table \ref{table:elasticae} (namely for $n=17,m=12$) can be proved to be unstable via Lemma~\ref{lem:instability}. Notice that the above criterion only works for $C(k)>0$ and this is only the case for $0\leq k<0.6869145$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1 proves instability of infinitely many but not all gamma_{m,n}; it needs C(k)>0, i.e. k<0.6869145 (numerically).

nodes.name: Refined test function spaces for instability
nodes.statement: With more computational effort the instability of more curves $\gamma_{m,n}$ can be shown both analytically and numerically. For instance it is possible to analytically determine the constrained minimizer of $I$ in the set of functions $\phi$ given by $$ \phi(s)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_j \cos\Big( \frac{js}{T}\Big) + \sum_{j=1}^{n-1} b_j \sin\Big( \frac{js}{T}\Big). $$ A reasonable constraint is given by $a_0^2+b_0^2+\ldots+a_{n-1}^2+b_{n-1}^2=1$. The constrained minimizers are of the form $a_j \cos\big(\frac{js}{T}\big)+a_{n-j}\cos\big(\frac{(n-j)s}{T }\big)$ or $b_j \sin\big(\frac{js}{T}\big)+b_{n-j}\sin\big(\frac{(n-j)s}{T }\big)$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ so that there is a higher chance to find negative values for $I_{m,n}(\phi)$. However, the analytical expressions for these minima are much more complicated than the one from Lemma \ref{lem:instability} and we could not detect any substantial gain with respect to the monochromatic ansatz functions when applying the resulting criterion to elasticae with large $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Constrained minimization of I over trigonometric polynomials of degree < n gives two-mode minimizers, but no substantial gain for large k.

nodes.name: All closed orbitlike elasticae are unstable
nodes.statement: Numerically, one clearly obtains much better results by choosing sufficiently large test function spaces and the natural conjecture is that all closed orbitlike elasticae are unstable.
conclusions: all closed orbitlike elasticae are unstable

nodes.name: Gap theorem of Mondino and Nguyen
nodes.statement: By a gap theorem due to Mondino and Nguyen \cite{MonNgu_gap_theorem} one knows that the Clifford torus can not be approximated by Willmore tori with respect to the Willmore energy functional.
conclusions: the Clifford torus can not be approximated by Willmore tori with respect to the Willmore energy functional

nodes.name: Hausdorff convergence
nodes.statement: We will use the notion of Hausdorff convergence defined by $\Sigma_n\to\Sigma$ in the Hausdorff sense if and only if $d_H(\Sigma_n,\Sigma)\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ where $$ d_H(\Sigma',\Sigma) = \max \big\{ \sup_{z'\in\Sigma'}\inf_{z\in\Sigma} d_{\mathbb{H}}(z',z), \sup_{z\in\Sigma}\inf_{z'\in\Sigma'} d_{\mathbb{H}}(z',z)\big\} $$ and $\Sigma,\Sigma',\Sigma_n$ are subsets of the (metric) hyperbolic space $(\mathbb{H},d_{\mathbb{H}})$.

nodes.name: Approximation of the Clifford torus by orbitlike Willmore surfaces
nodes.statement: Let $(m_n)$ be a sequence such that $1<2m_n/n<\sqrt 2$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Then, as $n\to\infty$, the sequence $(\Sigma_{\gamma_{m_n,n}})$ diverges with respect to the Willmore energy and it converges (up to M\"obius transformations) to the Clifford torus in the Hausdorff sense if and only if $2m_n/n\to \sqrt{2}$. In this case, almost all of the Willmore surfaces are unstable.
nodes.statement_short: Surfaces from gamma_{m_n,n} have diverging Willmore energy and converge (Hausdorff, up to Moebius maps) to the Clifford torus iff 2m_n/n -> sqrt 2; then almost all are unstable.
assumptions: Let $(m_n)$ be a sequence such that $1<2m_n/n<\sqrt 2$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
conclusions: the sequence $(\Sigma_{\gamma_{m_n,n}})$ diverges with respect to the Willmore energy
it converges (up to M\"obius transformations) to the Clifford torus in the Hausdorff sense if and only if $2m_n/n\to \sqrt{2}$.
In this case, almost all of the Willmore surfaces are unstable.
nodes.label: lem:approximation_results

nodes.name: Proof of Approximation of the Clifford torus by orbitlike Willmore surfaces
nodes.statement: From $\mathcal{W}_{m,n}\geq \sqrt{2}n\pi^2\to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$ we immediately get the divergence property. Proposition~\ref{prop:enclosures} shows that the set $\Sigma_{\gamma_{m_n,n}}=\gamma_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})\subset\mathbb{H}$ converges to the circle in the Hausdorff sense if and only if $\mu=\mu_{k_{m,n}}\to 1$. Indeed, only in this cases the radii and the centers of the inner and outer circles from Proposition~\ref{prop:enclosures} converge to each other. Notice that applying suitable M\"obius transformations to $\Sigma_{\gamma_{m_n,n}}$ we can ensure that the $b_3,a_3$--parameters of $\gamma_{m_n,n}$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} are the same for all $n$. By $\mu_{k_{m,n}}=4(1-k_{m,n}^2)/(2-k_{m,n}^2)^2$ we observe that $\mu_{k_{m_n}}\to 1$ happens precisely when $k_{m_n}\to 0$ which, by Proposition~\ref{prop:rotation} and the definition of $k_{m,n}$, is equivalent to $2m_n/n\to \sqrt{2}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:instability} shows that almost all $\gamma_{m,n}$ are unstable elasticae which proves the result.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the energy lower bound, the enclosing circles of Proposition 7, monotonicity of Delta theta_k and the instability lemma.

nodes.name: Divergence and Hausdorff criterion
nodes.statement: From $\mathcal{W}_{m,n}\geq \sqrt{2}n\pi^2\to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$ we immediately get the divergence property. Proposition~\ref{prop:enclosures} shows that the set $\Sigma_{\gamma_{m_n,n}}=\gamma_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})\subset\mathbb{H}$ converges to the circle in the Hausdorff sense if and only if $\mu=\mu_{k_{m,n}}\to 1$. Indeed, only in this cases the radii and the centers of the inner and outer circles from Proposition~\ref{prop:enclosures} converge to each other.
nodes.statement_short: Energy diverges; Hausdorff convergence iff mu->1 by Proposition 7.

nodes.name: Equivalent limit
nodes.statement: Notice that applying suitable M\"obius transformations to $\Sigma_{\gamma_{m_n,n}}$ we can ensure that the $b_3,a_3$--parameters of $\gamma_{m_n,n}$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} are the same for all $n$. By $\mu_{k_{m,n}}=4(1-k_{m,n}^2)/(2-k_{m,n}^2)^2$ we observe that $\mu_{k_{m_n}}\to 1$ happens precisely when $k_{m_n}\to 0$ which, by Proposition~\ref{prop:rotation} and the definition of $k_{m,n}$, is equivalent to $2m_n/n\to \sqrt{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: mu->1 iff k->0 iff 2m_n/n -> sqrt 2.

nodes.name: Instability
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:instability} shows that almost all $\gamma_{m,n}$ are unstable elasticae which proves the result.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1 gives instability of almost all.

nodes.name: Approximation picture: Clifford torus and catenoid limits
nodes.statement: The consequence is that the Clifford torus may be well approximated by orbitlike surfaces of revolutions the shape of which, however, becomes more and more complicated as they approach the torus. Similarly, one can study the limit $2m_n/n\to 1$, which corresponds to $k_{m_n}\to 1$. In this case Proposition~\ref{prop:enclosures} tells us that there is no Hausdorff convergence at all, but the catenoid is, as a subset of $\mathbb{H}$, contained in the set of accumlation points of the curves $\gamma_{m_n,n}(\mathbb{R})$. The latter follows from the fact that the solution of the initial value problem~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution} converges locally (but not globally) uniformly towards the catenoid solution as the curvature functions approach $\sqrt 2 \mathrm{sech}(s)$ locally uniformly.
nodes.statement_short: The Clifford torus is approximated by increasingly complicated orbitlike surfaces; in the limit 2m_n/n -> 1 there is no Hausdorff convergence but the catenoid lies among the accumulation points.

nodes.name: Wavelike elastica with curvature parameters k, s_*
nodes.statement: In this section we consider wavelike elasticae associated with curvature functions \begin{equation} \kappa(s) = \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}} \mathrm{cn}\Big( \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}},k\Big),\qquad\text{where } \frac{1}{\sqrt 2}<k<1,\;s_*\in\mathbb{R}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Wavelike curvature function
nodes.statement: \kappa(s) = \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}} \mathrm{cn}\Big( \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}},k\Big),\qquad\text{where } \frac{1}{\sqrt 2}<k<1,\;s_*\in\mathbb{R}.
nodes.label: eq:def_kappa_wavelike

nodes.name: Parameter mu for wavelike elasticae
nodes.statement: The functions $\phi$ and $Z(\cdot,P)$ are defined as before and we set $$ \mu:= -(\kappa')^2+\kappa^2-\frac{1}{4}\kappa^4 = -\frac{4k^2(1-k^2)}{(2k^2-1)^2}. $$

nodes.name: Fundamental system for the wavelike Lame-type equation
nodes.statement: For all $k\in (0,1)$ the ordinary differential equation $w''- \frac{2(1-k^2)}{\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)}w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$ such that the following holds: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $w_1$ is odd about 0, $w_2$ is even about 0, $w_2(0)>0>w_1'(0)$, \item[(ii)] $\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)(w_2(s)^2 - w_1(s)^2) = 1-k^2+(2k^2-1)\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(iii)] $\mathrm{cn}^3(s,k)(w_2(s)w_2'(s) - w_1(s)w_1'(s)) = (1-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(iv)] $w_2(s)w_1'(s)-w_1(s)w_2'(s)= -k\sqrt{(1-k^2)(2k^2-1)}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(v)] The functions $\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)w_1,\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)w_2$ have unique smooth extensions $\hat w_1,\hat w_2:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that the functions $w_1:=\frac{\hat w_1}{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)},w_2:=\frac{\hat w_2}{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)}$ build a fundamental system on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$. Moreover, $\hat w_2$ is positive on $\mathbb{R}$, $s\hat w_1(s)$ is negative on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ and, as $s\to\pm\infty$, we have $\hat w_1(s)\to \mp\infty,\hat w_2(s)\to\infty$ exponentially and $\hat w_1(s)/\hat w_2(s)\to \mp 1$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: w''-2(1-k^2)cn^{-2} w=0 has a fundamental system with explicit hyperbolic-type identities and smooth extensions cn*w_j with exponential growth.
conclusions: the ordinary differential equation $w''- \frac{2(1-k^2)}{\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)}w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$ such that the following holds:
nodes.label: prop:w1w2_wavelike

nodes.name: W_j and hat W_j (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Similarly to the orbitlike case we define \begin{align} W_j(s) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}}w_j\big( \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}}\big),\quad \hat W_j(s) := \frac{2k}{2k^2-1} \hat w_j\big( \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}}\big). \qquad (j=1,2) \end{align} Notice that Part (v) of the previous proposition ensures that $W_1,W_2$ are well-defined and smooth on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$ whereas $\hat W_1,\hat W_2$ are well-defined and smooth on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\hat W_j(s)=\kappa(s)W_j(s)$ whenever $\kappa(s)\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Definition of W_j and hat W_j (wavelike)
nodes.statement: W_j(s) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}}w_j\big( \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}}\big),\quad \hat W_j(s) := \frac{2k}{2k^2-1} \hat w_j\big( \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}}\big). \qquad (j=1,2)
nodes.label: eq:def_Wj_wavelike

nodes.name: Identities for W_1, W_2 (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa$ be given by \eqref{eq:def_kappa_wavelike}. Then on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ the functions $W_1,W_2$ build a fundamental system of $W''+2\mu\kappa^{-2}W=0$ such that the following identities hold: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $W_2^2-W_1^2 = \frac{\kappa^2-\mu}{\kappa^2}$, \item[(ii)] $W_1'= \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_1 - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_2$, \item[(iii)] $W_2'= - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_1+ \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_2$, \item[(iv)] $W_2W_1'-W_1W_2' = - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}}{2}$. \end{itemize} Moreover, $\hat W_2$ is positive on $\mathbb{R}$ and we have $\hat W_1(s)/\hat W_2(s) \to \mp 1$ as $s\to\pm\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Wavelike analogue: W_1,W_2 solve W''+2 mu kappa^{-2}W=0 with hyperbolic modulus, derivative and Wronskian identities; hat W_1/hat W_2 -> -+1.
conclusions: Then on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ the functions $W_1,W_2$ build a fundamental system of $W''+2\mu\kappa^{-2}W=0$ such that the following identities hold:
nodes.label: prop:W1W2_wavelike

nodes.name: Angle function vartheta (wavelike)
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}~(i) and~\eqref{eq:def_Wj_wavelike} there is a smooth function $\vartheta$ such that \begin{align} \hat W_2(s)-i\hat W_1(s) = \sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu} \big( \cosh(\vartheta(s))+i \sinh(\vartheta(s)) \big). \end{align} Again $\vartheta$ is thus defined only up to additive multiples of $2\pi$ so that we may require $\vartheta$ to satisfy the inequality $-2\pi<\vartheta(-s_*)\leq 0$.

nodes.name: Angle function vartheta (wavelike)
nodes.statement: \hat W_2(s)-i\hat W_1(s) = \sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu} \big( \cosh(\vartheta(s))+i \sinh(\vartheta(s)) \big).
nodes.label: eq:def_theta_wavelike

nodes.name: Properties of the angle function vartheta (wavelike)
nodes.statement: For $W_1,W_2,\vartheta$ as above the following identities hold on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$: $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\quad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. $$
nodes.statement_short: vartheta' = sqrt|mu| kappa^2/(2(kappa^2-mu)) and the matrix of W_1,W_2 is a hyperbolic rotation by vartheta.
nodes.label: prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike

nodes.name: Formula for Z in terms of hat W_1, hat W_2 (wavelike)
nodes.statement: For $P\in\mathbb{C}^2,P_2\neq 0$ we have \begin{equation} Z(s;P) = -1 + A \hat W_1(s) + B\hat W_2(s) + C\kappa(s) \end{equation} where $A,B,C\in\mathbb{C}$ are given by \eqref{eq:formula_AB},\eqref{eq:def_C} whenever $\kappa(s_0)\neq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: For complex P, Z(s;P) = -1 + A hat W_1 + B hat W_2 + C kappa with the same coefficient formulas as in the orbitlike case.
conclusions: where $A,B,C\in\mathbb{C}$ are given by \eqref{eq:formula_AB},\eqref{eq:def_C} whenever $\kappa(s_0)\neq 0$.
nodes.label: prop:formula_Z_wavelike

nodes.name: Formula for Z (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Z(s;P) = -1 + A \hat W_1(s) + B\hat W_2(s) + C\kappa(s)
nodes.label: eq:formula_Z_wavelike

nodes.name: Proof of Formula for Z in terms of hat W_1, hat W_2 (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Defining $W(s) := \frac{Z(s;P)+1}{\kappa(s)}-C$ one finds as in Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_orbitlike} $W''(s)+\frac{2\mu}{\kappa(s)^2}W(s)=0$ whenever $s+s_*\in ((2j-1)K(k),(2j+1)K(k))$ for some $j\in\mathbb{Z}$. With Proposition \ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike} we get \eqref{eq:formula_Z_wavelike} so that the formula for $Z,A,B$ follows as in the orbitlike case. Notice that the smoothness of $Z,\hat W_1,\hat W_2$ guarantees that the coefficients $A,B,C$ are the same on all intervals.
nodes.statement_short: As in the orbitlike case on each interval between zeros of kappa; smoothness makes the coefficients interval-independent.

nodes.name: ODE for W
nodes.statement: Defining $W(s) := \frac{Z(s;P)+1}{\kappa(s)}-C$ one finds as in Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_orbitlike} $W''(s)+\frac{2\mu}{\kappa(s)^2}W(s)=0$ whenever $s+s_*\in ((2j-1)K(k),(2j+1)K(k))$ for some $j\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: W satisfies the same ODE on intervals between zeros of kappa.

nodes.name: Expand
nodes.statement: With Proposition \ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike} we get \eqref{eq:formula_Z_wavelike} so that the formula for $Z,A,B$ follows as in the orbitlike case.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 12 gives the formula for Z.

nodes.name: Global coefficients
nodes.statement: Notice that the smoothness of $Z,\hat W_1,\hat W_2$ guarantees that the coefficients $A,B,C$ are the same on all intervals.
nodes.statement_short: Smoothness makes A,B,C the same on all intervals.

nodes.name: Explicit formulas for wavelike elasticae
nodes.statement: A curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{H}$ is a wavelike elastica parametrized by hyperbolic arclength if and only if we have \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \gamma_1(s) &=\frac{b_1 \hat W_1(s)+b_2 \hat W_2(s)+b_3 \kappa(s)}{a_1 \hat W_1(s)+a_2 \hat W_2(s)+a_3\kappa(s)}, \\ \gamma_2(s) &=\frac{1}{a_1 \hat W_1(s)+a_2\hat W_2(s) + a_3\kappa(s)}. \end{aligned} \end{align} for $a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3\in\mathbb{R}$ such that \begin{align} \begin{aligned} &\text{either}\qquad a_3\neq 0, \;\; a_2=\sqrt{a_1^2+a_3^2},\; \; \vecII{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{b_3}{a_3} \vecII{a_1}{a_2} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \vecII{a_2}{a_1} \\ &\text{or }\qquad\quad\, a_3=0,\;\; a_2=|a_1|,\;\; b_1=\mathrm{sign}(a_1)b_2,\;\; |b_3| = \frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{aligned} \end{align} In this case the identities \eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2} hold on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$ and for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ we have \begin{align} a_3\gamma_1(s) &= b_3 +\frac{1}{2\mu}\big(\kappa(s)^2\sin(\phi(s))+2\kappa'(s)\cos(\phi(s))\big), \\ a_3\gamma_2(s) &= \frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu} + \frac{1}{2\mu}\big(2\kappa'(s)\sin(\phi(s))-\kappa(s)^2\cos(\phi(s))\big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A curve is a wavelike elastica in arclength iff gamma_1, gamma_2 are explicit quotients of hat W_1, hat W_2, kappa with coefficients satisfying one of two hyperbolic-type relations.
conclusions: A curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{H}$ is a wavelike elastica parametrized by hyperbolic arclength if and only if we have
nodes.label: thm:explicit_formula_wavelike

nodes.name: Explicit formulas for gamma_1, gamma_2 (wavelike)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \gamma_1(s) &=\frac{b_1 \hat W_1(s)+b_2 \hat W_2(s)+b_3 \kappa(s)}{a_1 \hat W_1(s)+a_2 \hat W_2(s)+a_3\kappa(s)}, \\ \gamma_2(s) &=\frac{1}{a_1 \hat W_1(s)+a_2\hat W_2(s) + a_3\kappa(s)}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:explicit_formula_wavelike

nodes.name: Coefficient relations (wavelike)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\text{either}\qquad a_3\neq 0, \;\; a_2=\sqrt{a_1^2+a_3^2},\; \; \vecII{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{b_3}{a_3} \vecII{a_1}{a_2} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \vecII{a_2}{a_1} \\ &\text{or }\qquad\quad\, a_3=0,\;\; a_2=|a_1|,\;\; b_1=\mathrm{sign}(a_1)b_2,\;\; |b_3| = \frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3

nodes.name: Identities for a_3 gamma (wavelike)
nodes.statement: a_3\gamma_1(s) &= b_3 +\frac{1}{2\mu}\big(\kappa(s)^2\sin(\phi(s))+2\kappa'(s)\cos(\phi(s))\big), \\ a_3\gamma_2(s) &= \frac{\kappa(s)}{\mu} + \frac{1}{2\mu}\big(2\kappa'(s)\sin(\phi(s))-\kappa(s)^2\cos(\phi(s))\big).
nodes.label: eq:wavelike_b3a3_1

nodes.name: Proof of Explicit formulas for wavelike elasticae
nodes.statement: The proof follows the same lines as in the orbitlike case, so we only sketch the main differences. Assuming first that $\gamma$ is a wavelike elastica in $\mathbb{H}$ we get from Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_wavelike} \begin{align*} (\gamma_1(s)-P_1)^2+\gamma_2(s)^2+P_2^2 = 2\gamma_2(s)P_2\big( A \hat W_1(s) + B \hat W_2(s) + C\kappa(s)\big) \end{align*} for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and $A,B,C$ given by \eqref{eq:formula_AB},\eqref{eq:def_C}. As in the orbitlike case this leads to \begin{align*} 1 = \gamma_2(s)\big(a_1 \hat W_1(s)+a_2\hat W_2(s)+a_3\kappa(s)\big),\quad \gamma_1(s) &= \gamma_2(s)\big(b_1\hat W_1(s)+b_2\hat W_2(s)+b_3\kappa(s)\big) \end{align*} where the constants $a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3$ satisfy \eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2},\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$. The latter two equations imply \eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_2} for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$. It remains to prove \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} to finish the ''only if''-part. \medskip To this end we introduce the matrices \begin{align*} \mathcal{W}:=\matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'},\qquad \mathcal{R}_h(\vartheta):=\matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. \end{align*} From Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike} we get \begin{align*} \mathcal{W} &= \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{\frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \mathcal{R}_h(\vartheta), \qquad \mathcal{W}^{-1} = \mathcal{R}_h(-\vartheta) \matII{-\frac{2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{-\frac{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}} {\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{0}, \\ \intertext{and combining these formulas with the ones for $\xi^1,\xi^3$ from \eqref{eq:formula_xi} we get} \xi^1 &= \mathcal{R}_h(-\vartheta) \vecII{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{|\mu|(\kappa^2-\mu)}}(2\kappa'\cos(\phi)+\kappa^2\sin(\phi))}{ \frac{1}{2\mu\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}(2\mu-2\kappa^2-2\kappa\kappa'\sin(\phi)+\kappa^3\cos(\phi)) }, \\ \xi^3 &= \mathcal{R}_h(-\vartheta) \vecII{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{|\mu|(\kappa^2-\mu)}}(2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))}{ \frac{\kappa}{2\mu\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi)) }. \intertext{ Writing $\skp{\cdot}{\cdot}_h$ for the inner product in $\mathbb{H}$ and $(w_1,w_2)^\perp=(w_2,w_1)$ we get from $(\kappa')^2=\kappa^2-\frac{\kappa^4}{4}-\mu$ and the fact that the rotation matrices $\mathcal{R}_h(\vartheta)$ are hyperbolic isometries} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1}_h &= -\frac{(2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))^2 }{4\mu^2} = - a_3^2\gamma_2^2,\\ \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^3}_h &= \frac{(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi))(2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))}{4\mu^2} = \gamma_2 a_3(a_3\gamma_1-b_3), \\ \skp{(\xi^1)^\perp}{\xi^3}_h &= -\frac{2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi)}{2\mu\sqrt{|\mu|}} = -\frac{a_3\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{align*} This implies \begin{align*} a_1^2-a_2^2 &= \skp{a}{a}_h \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1}}{=} \frac{1}{\gamma_2^2} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1}_h = -a_3^2, \\ a_1b_1-a_2b_2 &= \skp{a}{b}_h \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2}}{=} \frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_2^2} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1}_h + \frac{1}{\gamma_2} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^3}_h = -b_3a_3, \\ a_2b_1-a_1b_2 &= \skp{a^\perp}{b}_h \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\gamma_2}\skp{(\xi^1)^\perp}{\xi^3}_h = -\frac{a_3}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{align*} Moreover, we have $a_2\geq |a_1|$ because, by Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}, $\hat W_2$ is positive and thus $$ 0 \leq \limsup_{s\to\pm\infty} \gamma_2(s)\hat W_2(s) = \limsup_{s\to\pm\infty} \frac{1}{a_1 \frac{\hat W_1(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}+a_2+\frac{a_3\kappa(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}} = \frac{1}{\mp a_1+a_2}. $$ Hence, in the case $a_3\neq 0$ we obtain the conditions from \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}. In the case $a_3=0$ the above equations imply $a_2=|a_1|,b_1=\mathrm{sign}(a_1)b_2$ and \eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_2} yield \begin{align*} b_3^2 &= \frac{(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi))^2}{4\mu^2} = \frac{\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2-(2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2-4\kappa^2}{4\mu^2} = \frac{1}{|\mu|}. \end{align*} So \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} is entirely proved. \medskip Now let $a_1,\ldots,b_3$ be given as in \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ the associated elastica. In analogy to \eqref{eq:formula_phi} the angle function $\phi$ is defined via \begin{equation*} \vecII{\sin(\phi)}{\cos(\phi)} := \frac{\mu}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}\matII{\kappa^2}{2\kappa'}{2\kappa'}{-\kappa^2} \vecII{a_3\gamma_1- b_3}{a_3\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}}, \end{equation*} Such a definition is possible because of $\kappa^2((aW)^2-(a^\perp W)^2)= \kappa^2(a_1^2-a_2^2)(W_1^2-W_2^2)=(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3^2$ \begin{align*} &\frac{\mu^2}{4(\kappa^2-\mu)^2} \Big( \Big( \kappa^2\big(a_3\gamma_1- b_3\big)+2\kappa'\big(a_3\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu }\big)\Big)^2 + \Big( 2\kappa'\big(a_3\gamma_1- b_3\big)-2\kappa^2\big(a_3\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}\big) \Big)^2 \Big) \\ &= \frac{\big( \kappa|\mu|(a_3bW-b_3aW)\big)^2+ \big(-\kappa^2aW + (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3 \big)^2}{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ |\mu|\kappa^2(a^\perp W)^2 + \kappa^4(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ \kappa^2\mu |a|_h^2|W|_h^2 + (\kappa^4-\kappa^2\mu)(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{(aW)^2 +2a_3aW+ a_3^2}{(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= 1. \end{align*} It therefore remains to check that $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi)$ satisfies the ODE~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. We have \begin{align*} \sin(\phi) &= \frac{\mu}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \kappa^2\big( a_3\frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}-b_3\big) +2\kappa'\big( \frac{a_3}{\kappa(aW+a_3)}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}\big) \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( -\frac{\kappa^2 a^\perp W}{\sqrt{|\mu|} (aW+a_3)} + \frac{2\kappa'( (\mu-\kappa^2) a_3- \kappa^2 aW)}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \Big) \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu) a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}, \\ \cos(\phi) &= \frac{2\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa' a^\perp W + \kappa^3 aW + \kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}. \end{align*} Next we use \begin{align*} W' = \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W^\perp \end{align*} from Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}. We obtain \begin{align*} \frac{\gamma_2'}{\gamma_2} &= - \frac{\kappa'}{\kappa} - \frac{2\mu\kappa' aW + \sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^3 a^\perp W }{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \frac{-\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \sin(\phi), \\ \frac{\gamma_1'}{\gamma_2} &= \kappa W' \frac{b(aW+a_3)-a(bW+b_3)}{aW+a_3} \\ &= \kappa W' \frac{ (a^\perp W) a -(aW+a_3)a^\perp}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \frac{(-2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' W - \kappa^3 W^\perp) ( (a^\perp W) a - (aW+a_3)a^\perp)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{-\kappa^3 (a^\perp W)^2+\kappa^3 (aW)^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^3 |a|_h^2|W|_h^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{a_3\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu) + \kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' a^\perp W}{2(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \cos(\phi). \end{align*} The verification of $\phi'+\cos(\phi)=\kappa$ is the same as in the orbitlike case so that $\gamma$ is indeed a wavelike elastica.
nodes.statement_short: Same lines as the orbitlike case with hyperbolic rotations replacing rotations; extra case a_3=0 handled via asymptotics of hat W_j.

nodes.name: Analogy
nodes.statement: The proof follows the same lines as in the orbitlike case, so we only sketch the main differences.
nodes.statement_short: Proof follows the orbitlike case.

nodes.name: Necessity formulas
nodes.statement: Assuming first that $\gamma$ is a wavelike elastica in $\mathbb{H}$ we get from Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_Z_wavelike} \begin{align*} (\gamma_1(s)-P_1)^2+\gamma_2(s)^2+P_2^2 = 2\gamma_2(s)P_2\big( A \hat W_1(s) + B \hat W_2(s) + C\kappa(s)\big) \end{align*} for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and $A,B,C$ given by \eqref{eq:formula_AB},\eqref{eq:def_C}. As in the orbitlike case this leads to \begin{align*} 1 = \gamma_2(s)\big(a_1 \hat W_1(s)+a_2\hat W_2(s)+a_3\kappa(s)\big),\quad \gamma_1(s) &= \gamma_2(s)\big(b_1\hat W_1(s)+b_2\hat W_2(s)+b_3\kappa(s)\big) \end{align*} where the constants $a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3$ satisfy \eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2},\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$. The latter two equations imply \eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_2} for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: Derive the explicit formulas from Proposition 14.

nodes.name: Remaining relations
nodes.statement: It remains to prove \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} to finish the ''only if''-part.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to prove the coefficient relations.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic rotation form
nodes.statement: To this end we introduce the matrices \begin{align*} \mathcal{W}:=\matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'},\qquad \mathcal{R}_h(\vartheta):=\matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. \end{align*} From Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike} we get \begin{align*} \mathcal{W} &= \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{\frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \mathcal{R}_h(\vartheta), \qquad \mathcal{W}^{-1} = \mathcal{R}_h(-\vartheta) \matII{-\frac{2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{-\frac{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}} {\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{0}, \\ \intertext{and combining these formulas with the ones for $\xi^1,\xi^3$ from \eqref{eq:formula_xi} we get} \xi^1 &= \mathcal{R}_h(-\vartheta) \vecII{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{|\mu|(\kappa^2-\mu)}}(2\kappa'\cos(\phi)+\kappa^2\sin(\phi))}{ \frac{1}{2\mu\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}(2\mu-2\kappa^2-2\kappa\kappa'\sin(\phi)+\kappa^3\cos(\phi)) }, \\ \xi^3 &= \mathcal{R}_h(-\vartheta) \vecII{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{|\mu|(\kappa^2-\mu)}}(2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))}{ \frac{\kappa}{2\mu\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi)) }. \intertext{ Writing $\skp{\cdot}{\cdot}_h$ for the inner product in $\mathbb{H}$ and $(w_1,w_2)^\perp=(w_2,w_1)$ we get from $(\kappa')^2=\kappa^2-\frac{\kappa^4}{4}-\mu$ and the fact that the rotation matrices $\mathcal{R}_h(\vartheta)$ are hyperbolic isometries} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1}_h &= -\frac{(2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))^2 }{4\mu^2} = - a_3^2\gamma_2^2,\\ \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^3}_h &= \frac{(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi))(2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))}{4\mu^2} = \gamma_2 a_3(a_3\gamma_1-b_3), \\ \skp{(\xi^1)^\perp}{\xi^3}_h &= -\frac{2\kappa+2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi)}{2\mu\sqrt{|\mu|}} = -\frac{a_3\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express W and xi^1,xi^3 via hyperbolic rotations; compute hyperbolic inner products.

nodes.name: Coefficient identities
nodes.statement: This implies \begin{align*} a_1^2-a_2^2 &= \skp{a}{a}_h \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1}}{=} \frac{1}{\gamma_2^2} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1}_h = -a_3^2, \\ a_1b_1-a_2b_2 &= \skp{a}{b}_h \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2}}{=} \frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_2^2} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^1}_h + \frac{1}{\gamma_2} \skp{\xi^1}{\xi^3}_h = -b_3a_3, \\ a_2b_1-a_1b_2 &= \skp{a^\perp}{b}_h \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_1},\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\gamma_2}\skp{(\xi^1)^\perp}{\xi^3}_h = -\frac{a_3}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Deduce a_1^2-a_2^2=-a_3^2 and b relations.

nodes.name: Case a_3 nonzero
nodes.statement: Moreover, we have $a_2\geq |a_1|$ because, by Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}, $\hat W_2$ is positive and thus $$ 0 \leq \limsup_{s\to\pm\infty} \gamma_2(s)\hat W_2(s) = \limsup_{s\to\pm\infty} \frac{1}{a_1 \frac{\hat W_1(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}+a_2+\frac{a_3\kappa(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}} = \frac{1}{\mp a_1+a_2}. $$ Hence, in the case $a_3\neq 0$ we obtain the conditions from \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}.
nodes.statement_short: a_2>=|a_1| from positivity of hat W_2 gives the first alternative.

nodes.name: Case a_3=0
nodes.statement: In the case $a_3=0$ the above equations imply $a_2=|a_1|,b_1=\mathrm{sign}(a_1)b_2$ and \eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:wavelike_b3a3_2} yield \begin{align*} b_3^2 &= \frac{(\kappa^2\sin(\phi)+2\kappa'\cos(\phi))^2}{4\mu^2} = \frac{\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2-(2\kappa'\sin(\phi)-\kappa^2\cos(\phi))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2-4\kappa^2}{4\mu^2} = \frac{1}{|\mu|}. \end{align*} So \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} is entirely proved.
nodes.statement_short: Derive a_2=|a_1|, b_1=sign(a_1)b_2, |b_3|=1/sqrt|mu|.

nodes.name: Define phi
nodes.statement: Now let $a_1,\ldots,b_3$ be given as in \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ the associated elastica. In analogy to \eqref{eq:formula_phi} the angle function $\phi$ is defined via \begin{equation*} \vecII{\sin(\phi)}{\cos(\phi)} := \frac{\mu}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}\matII{\kappa^2}{2\kappa'}{2\kappa'}{-\kappa^2} \vecII{a_3\gamma_1- b_3}{a_3\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}}, \end{equation*} Such a definition is possible because of $\kappa^2((aW)^2-(a^\perp W)^2)= \kappa^2(a_1^2-a_2^2)(W_1^2-W_2^2)=(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3^2$ \begin{align*} &\frac{\mu^2}{4(\kappa^2-\mu)^2} \Big( \Big( \kappa^2\big(a_3\gamma_1- b_3\big)+2\kappa'\big(a_3\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu }\big)\Big)^2 + \Big( 2\kappa'\big(a_3\gamma_1- b_3\big)-2\kappa^2\big(a_3\gamma_2-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}\big) \Big)^2 \Big) \\ &= \frac{\big( \kappa|\mu|(a_3bW-b_3aW)\big)^2+ \big(-\kappa^2aW + (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3 \big)^2}{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ |\mu|\kappa^2(a^\perp W)^2 + \kappa^4(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{ \kappa^2\mu |a|_h^2|W|_h^2 + (\kappa^4-\kappa^2\mu)(aW)^2 +2\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3aW+ (\kappa^2-\mu)^2a_3^2 }{\kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= \frac{(aW)^2 +2a_3aW+ a_3^2}{(aW+a_3)^2} \\ &= 1. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define phi and check the unit norm.

nodes.name: Verify gamma',
nodes.statement: It therefore remains to check that $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\phi)$ satisfies the ODE~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. We have \begin{align*} \sin(\phi) &= \frac{\mu}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( \kappa^2\big( a_3\frac{bW+b_3}{aW+a_3}-b_3\big) +2\kappa'\big( \frac{a_3}{\kappa(aW+a_3)}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}\big) \Big) \\ &= \frac{\mu}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)} \Big( -\frac{\kappa^2 a^\perp W}{\sqrt{|\mu|} (aW+a_3)} + \frac{2\kappa'( (\mu-\kappa^2) a_3- \kappa^2 aW)}{\mu\kappa a_3(aW+a_3)} \Big) \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu) a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}, \\ \cos(\phi) &= \frac{2\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa' a^\perp W + \kappa^3 aW + \kappa^2(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)}. \end{align*} Next we use \begin{align*} W' = \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W^\perp \end{align*} from Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}. We obtain \begin{align*} \frac{\gamma_2'}{\gamma_2} &= - \frac{\kappa'}{\kappa} - \frac{2\mu\kappa' aW + \sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^3 a^\perp W }{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \frac{-\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^3 a^\perp W - 2\kappa^2\kappa' aW - 2\kappa'(\kappa^2-\mu)a_3}{2\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \sin(\phi), \\ \frac{\gamma_1'}{\gamma_2} &= \kappa W' \frac{b(aW+a_3)-a(bW+b_3)}{aW+a_3} \\ &= \kappa W' \frac{ (a^\perp W) a -(aW+a_3)a^\perp}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3(aW+a_3)} \\ &= \frac{(-2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' W - \kappa^3 W^\perp) ( (a^\perp W) a - (aW+a_3)a^\perp)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{-\kappa^3 (a^\perp W)^2+\kappa^3 (aW)^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^3 |a|_h^2|W|_h^2 + a_3(\kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' a^\perp W)}{2a_3(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \frac{a_3\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu) + \kappa^3 aW + 2\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa' a^\perp W}{2(aW+a_3)(\kappa^2-\mu)} \\ &= \cos(\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Verify gamma_2'/gamma_2=sin(phi), gamma_1'/gamma_2=cos(phi).

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The verification of $\phi'+\cos(\phi)=\kappa$ is the same as in the orbitlike case so that $\gamma$ is indeed a wavelike elastica.
nodes.statement_short: phi equation as in the orbitlike case.

nodes.name: Special complex point P (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Assume $a_3\neq 0$. For $P=(\frac{b_3}{a_3},\pm \frac{i}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3})$ we have $$ Z(s;P) = -1 \pm i \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: For the complex point P=(b_3/a_3, +-i/(sqrt|mu| a_3)), Z = -1 +- i kappa/sqrt|mu|.
conclusions: we have $$ Z(s;P) = -1 \pm i \frac{\kappa(s)}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. $$
nodes.label: prop:choice_of_P_wavelike

nodes.name: Proof of Special complex point P (wavelike)
nodes.statement: As in the proof of the previous theorem we use $\kappa^2((a^\perp W)^2-(aW)^2 ) = (\mu-\kappa^2)a_3^2$ by \eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}~(i). Then the assertion follows from \begin{align*} &\Big(\gamma_1-\frac{b_3}{a_3}\Big)^2+\Big(\gamma_2\mp \frac{i}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3}\Big)^2 \\ &= \frac{(a^\perp W)^2}{|\mu|a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} + \frac{|\mu|a_3^2-\kappa^2(aW+a_3)^2}{\kappa^2|\mu|a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} \mp \frac{2i\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \\ &= \frac{\kappa^2((a^\perp W)^2-(aW)^2) - \mu a_3^2-2\kappa^2 a_3aW - \kappa^2a_3^2}{\kappa^2|\mu|a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} \mp \frac{2i\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \\ &= -\frac{2\kappa^2a_3^2-2\kappa^2 a_3aW}{\kappa^2|\mu|a_3^2(aW+a_3)^2} \mp \frac{2i\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \\ &= -\frac{2}{|\mu|a_3(aW+a_3)} \mp \frac{2i\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} -\frac{2\kappa\gamma_2}{|\mu|a_3} \mp \frac{2i\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \\ &= \pm \frac{2i\gamma_2}{\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3} \big( -1 \pm i \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{|\mu|}} \big) \\ &=2P_2\gamma_2\big( -1 \pm i \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{|\mu|}} \big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation using the coefficient relations of Theorem 5.

nodes.name: Wavelike elasticae oscillate between two circles
nodes.statement: Assume $a_3\neq 0$. Then we have $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ where \begin{align*} Q_1 &= \Big(\frac{b_3}{a_3},~~~\frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{|\mu| |a_3|}\Big),\qquad R_1 = \frac{\sqrt{2-\mu+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{|\mu| |a_3|}, \\ Q_2 &= \Big( \frac{b_3}{a_3},-\frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{|\mu| |a_3|}\Big),\qquad R_2 = \frac{\sqrt{2-\mu+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{|\mu| |a_3|}. \end{align*} The curve $\gamma$ touches $\partial B_{R_1}(Q_1)$ exactly when $\kappa$ attains its maximum and it touches $\partial B_{R_2}(Q_2)$ precisely when $\kappa$ attains its minimum. Moreover, we have \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \Big\{\lim_{s\to\infty} \gamma(s), \lim_{s\to -\infty} \gamma(s)\Big\} &= \partial B_{R_1}(Q_1) \cap \partial B_{R_2}(Q_2) \\ &= \Big\{ \Big(\frac{b_3}{a_3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3},0\Big), \Big(\frac{b_3}{a_3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3},0 \Big) \Big\}. \end{aligned} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For a_3 nonzero a wavelike elastica lies between two equal circles centred symmetrically about the axis and converges at both ends to their intersection points.
conclusions: Then we have $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$
nodes.label: prop:oscillations_wavelike

nodes.name: Limits of wavelike elasticae
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \Big\{\lim_{s\to\infty} \gamma(s), \lim_{s\to -\infty} \gamma(s)\Big\} &= \partial B_{R_1}(Q_1) \cap \partial B_{R_2}(Q_2) \\ &= \Big\{ \Big(\frac{b_3}{a_3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3},0\Big), \Big(\frac{b_3}{a_3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3},0 \Big) \Big\}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:limits_wavelike

nodes.name: Proof of Wavelike elasticae oscillate between two circles
nodes.statement: Let $P=(P_1,P_2)$ be given as in Proposition \ref{prop:choice_of_P_wavelike}. By definition of $Z(\cdot;P)$ and $P_2^2=-|P_2|^2$ we find $(\gamma_1-P_1)^2+\gamma_2^2-|P_2|^2=2\gamma_2|P_2|\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}$ and thus \begin{align*} (\gamma_1-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2+\rho|P_2|)^2 &\geq |P_2|^2(1+\rho^2), \\ (\gamma_1-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2-\rho|P_2|)^2 &\leq |P_2|^2(1+\rho^2),\\ \text{where }\quad \rho:= \frac{\max |\kappa|}{\sqrt{|\mu|}} &= \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}\sqrt{|\mu|}} = \frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{align*} Here equality holds if and only if $\kappa$ attains its minimum/maximum, respectively. So if we set $$ Q_1:=(P_1,\rho|P_2|),\quad Q_2:=(P_1,-\rho|P_2|),\quad R_1:=R_2:=|P_2|\sqrt{1+\rho^2} $$ then $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$, which is the first statement of the theorem. From the explicit formulas from Theorem \ref{thm:explicit_formula_wavelike} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike} we infer $\gamma_2(s) \to 0$ as $s\to \pm\infty$ and \begin{align*} \lim_{s\to\pm\infty} \gamma_1(s) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_wavelike}}{=} \lim_{s\to\pm\infty} \frac{b_1 \frac{\hat W_1(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}+b_2+b_3 \frac{\kappa(s)}{\hat W_2(s)} }{a_1 \frac{\hat W_1(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}+a_2+a_3 \frac{\kappa(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}} = \frac{\mp b_1 +b_2}{\mp a_1 +a_2} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{b_3}{a_3} \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Z for the complex point P to derive circle inequalities; limits from asymptotics of hat W_1/hat W_2.

nodes.name: Circle inequalities
nodes.statement: Let $P=(P_1,P_2)$ be given as in Proposition \ref{prop:choice_of_P_wavelike}. By definition of $Z(\cdot;P)$ and $P_2^2=-|P_2|^2$ we find $(\gamma_1-P_1)^2+\gamma_2^2-|P_2|^2=2\gamma_2|P_2|\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}$ and thus \begin{align*} (\gamma_1-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2+\rho|P_2|)^2 &\geq |P_2|^2(1+\rho^2), \\ (\gamma_1-P_1)^2+(\gamma_2-\rho|P_2|)^2 &\leq |P_2|^2(1+\rho^2),\\ \text{where }\quad \rho:= \frac{\max |\kappa|}{\sqrt{|\mu|}} &= \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}\sqrt{|\mu|}} = \frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. \end{align*} Here equality holds if and only if $\kappa$ attains its minimum/maximum, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Use Z for complex P to get two circle inequalities.

nodes.name: Enclosure
nodes.statement: So if we set $$ Q_1:=(P_1,\rho|P_2|),\quad Q_2:=(P_1,-\rho|P_2|),\quad R_1:=R_2:=|P_2|\sqrt{1+\rho^2} $$ then $\gamma(\mathbb{R})\subset \overline{B_{R_1}(Q_1)}\setminus B_{R_2}(Q_2)$, which is the first statement of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Define Q_i, R_i to obtain the enclosure.

nodes.name: Limits
nodes.statement: From the explicit formulas from Theorem \ref{thm:explicit_formula_wavelike} and Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike} we infer $\gamma_2(s) \to 0$ as $s\to \pm\infty$ and \begin{align*} \lim_{s\to\pm\infty} \gamma_1(s) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_wavelike}}{=} \lim_{s\to\pm\infty} \frac{b_1 \frac{\hat W_1(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}+b_2+b_3 \frac{\kappa(s)}{\hat W_2(s)} }{a_1 \frac{\hat W_1(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}+a_2+a_3 \frac{\kappa(s)}{\hat W_2(s)}} = \frac{\mp b_1 +b_2}{\mp a_1 +a_2} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{b_3}{a_3} \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mu|} a_3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute limits of gamma at +-infinity.

nodes.name: Wavelike elasticae oscillate around a half circle
nodes.statement: So we conclude as in \cite{LanSing_the_total} that wavelike elasticae with $a_3\neq 0$ oscillate around the halfcircle around $(b_3/a_3,0)$ with radius $1/(\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3)$.
conclusions: oscillate around the halfcircle around $(b_3/a_3,0)$ with radius $1/(\sqrt{|\mu|}a_3)$

nodes.name: Wavelike elasticae with a_3=0 lie in a cone
nodes.statement: Assume $a_3=0$. Then the elastica $\gamma$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_wavelike} satisfies $$ \gamma(\mathbb{R}) \subset \mathcal{C}:= \Big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb{H} : \frac{\big|x-\frac{b_1}{a_1}\big|}{y} \leq \frac{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}}}{\sqrt{|\mu|}} \Big\}. $$ It touches the boundary of the cone $\mathcal{C}$ at points where $\kappa$ attains its maximum or minimum. Moreover, we have $$ \big\{\lim_{s\to\infty} \gamma_2(s), \lim_{s\to -\infty} \gamma_2(s)\big\} = \{0,\infty\}. $$
nodes.statement_short: For a_3=0 the wavelike elastica lies in an explicit cone, touches its boundary at curvature extrema, and gamma_2 tends to 0 and infinity at the two ends.
conclusions: Then the elastica $\gamma$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_wavelike} satisfies
nodes.label: prop:wavelike_a30

nodes.name: Proof of Wavelike elasticae with a_3=0 lie in a cone
nodes.statement: The conditions~\eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_wavelike} imply $$ \gamma_1(s) = \frac{b_1(\hat W_1(s)+\mathrm{sign}(a_1) \hat W_2(s))+b_3 \kappa(s)}{a_1 \hat W_1(s)+|a_1| \hat W_2(s)} = \frac{b_1}{a_1} + \frac{\mathrm{sign}(b_3)\kappa(s) \gamma_2(s)}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. $$ This identity and $$ - \min_\mathbb{R} \kappa = \max_\mathbb{R} \kappa = \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}} = \sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}} $$ proves the first two assertions. Additionally, Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike} implies $\hat W_2(s)\to\infty$ as $s\to\pm\infty$ so that the claim follows from $$ \gamma_2(s)\hat W_2(s) = \frac{\hat W_2(s)}{a_1\hat W_1(s)+|a_1|\hat W_2(s)} \to \frac{1}{\mp a_1+|a_1|} \quad\text{as }s\to\pm\infty. $$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite gamma_1 via the a_3=0 relations as b_1/a_1 + sign(b_3) kappa gamma_2/sqrt|mu| and use bounds on kappa and growth of hat W_2.

nodes.name: Rewrite gamma_1
nodes.statement: The conditions~\eqref{eq:wavelike_a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_wavelike} imply $$ \gamma_1(s) = \frac{b_1(\hat W_1(s)+\mathrm{sign}(a_1) \hat W_2(s))+b_3 \kappa(s)}{a_1 \hat W_1(s)+|a_1| \hat W_2(s)} = \frac{b_1}{a_1} + \frac{\mathrm{sign}(b_3)\kappa(s) \gamma_2(s)}{\sqrt{|\mu|}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Express gamma_1 = b_1/a_1 + sign(b_3) kappa gamma_2/sqrt|mu|.

nodes.name: Cone
nodes.statement: This identity and $$ - \min_\mathbb{R} \kappa = \max_\mathbb{R} \kappa = \frac{2k}{\sqrt{2k^2-1}} = \sqrt{2+2\sqrt{1-\mu}} $$ proves the first two assertions.
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on kappa give the cone and touching points.

nodes.name: Limits of gamma_2
nodes.statement: Additionally, Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike} implies $\hat W_2(s)\to\infty$ as $s\to\pm\infty$ so that the claim follows from $$ \gamma_2(s)\hat W_2(s) = \frac{\hat W_2(s)}{a_1\hat W_1(s)+|a_1|\hat W_2(s)} \to \frac{1}{\mp a_1+|a_1|} \quad\text{as }s\to\pm\infty. $$
nodes.statement_short: Growth of hat W_2 gives limits 0 and infinity.

nodes.name: Reduction of the Dirichlet problem for orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement: Let $(A_1,A_2),(B_1,B_2)\in\mathbb{H},\phi_A,\phi_B\in\mathbb{R}$ be given. For $s_*\in\mathbb{R},k\in (0,1)$ let the functions $\kappa,\vartheta$ be defined by \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike},\eqref{eq:def_theta}. Then the elastica given by \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1},\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2} solves the Dirichlet problem \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP2} if and only if there is an $l\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that \begin{align} &a_3 = \frac{2\kappa(0)+2\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)-\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A)}{2\mu A_2}, \\ &b_3 = a_3 A_1 - \frac{\kappa(0)^2\sin(\phi_A)+2\kappa'(0)\cos(\phi_A)}{2\mu}, \\ & a_1+ia_2 = a_3 \frac{\sigma_2+i\sigma_1}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}}e^{i\vartheta(0)}, \\ &b_1+ib_2 = \big( \frac{b_3}{a_3}+\frac{i}{\sqrt\mu a_3}\big)(a_1+ia_2) \\ &L= -s_*+\sqrt{2-k^2}\Big( 2lK(k)-\sigma\mathrm{dn}^{-1}\Big(\frac{\sqrt{2-k^2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1+\mu(B_2^2a_3^2+(a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3} ,k\Big)\Big) \intertext{for $\sigma:= \mathrm{sign}\Big(\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_B) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3} \sin(\phi_B)\Big)$ and $s_*,k$ satisfy the equations} &\Big(\frac{1+\mu(B_2^2a_3^2+(a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3}\Big)^2 = 2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_B) \notag \\ &\hspace{6.2cm} + \frac{1+\mu(-B_2^2a_3^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3}\cos(\phi_B), \\ &e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))} = \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{ \sqrt{(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)(\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2)}}. \end{align}
