nodes.name: Proof of Reduction of the Dirichlet problem for orbitlike elasticae
nodes.statement: In a first step we prove that every solution of \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP2} satisfies \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3}--\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} for some $l\in\mathbb{Z}$. In the second step we show that these conditions indeed provide solutions of the Dirichlet problem. So let $\gamma$ be a solution of the Dirichlet problem with angle function $\phi$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} the formulas \eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} and $e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}$ yield \begin{align*} a_3 &= \frac{2\kappa(0)+2\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)-\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A)}{2\mu A_2}, \\ a_3 &= \frac{2\kappa(L)+2\kappa'(L)\sin(\phi_B)-\kappa(L)^2\cos(\phi_B)}{2\mu B_2}, \\ b_3 &= a_3 A_1 - \frac{\kappa(0)^2\sin(\phi_A)+2\kappa'(0)\cos(\phi_A)}{2\mu}, \\ b_3 &= a_3 B_1 - \frac{\kappa(L)^2\sin(\phi_B)+2\kappa'(L)\cos(\phi_B)}{2\mu}. \end{align*} These equations imply \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b3} as well as \begin{align} \matII{\cos(\phi_A)}{-\sin(\phi_A)}{\sin(\phi_A)}{\cos(\phi_A)}\vecII{\kappa(0)^2}{2\kappa'(0)} &= \vecII{2\kappa(0)-2\mu A_2 a_3}{2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)}, \\ \matII{\cos(\phi_B)}{-\sin(\phi_B)}{\sin(\phi_B)}{\cos(\phi_B)}\vecII{\kappa(L)^2}{2\kappa'(L)} &= \vecII{2\kappa(L)-2\mu B_2 a_3}{2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)}. \end{align} Taking the modulus on each side and using $\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2=4(\kappa^2-\mu)$ we find that the quadratic term $4\kappa(0)^2,4\kappa(L)^2$ cancels and we get \begin{align} \kappa(0) &= \frac{1+\mu(a_3^2A_2^2+(a_3A_1-b_3)^2)}{2A_2a_3}, \\ \kappa(L) &= \frac{1+\mu(a_3^2B_2^2+(a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3}. \end{align} Plugging these formulas into \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula1a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula1b} we may solve for $\kappa(0)^2,2\kappa'(0),\kappa(L)^2,2\kappa'(L)$ and find \begin{align} \kappa(0)^2 &= 2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_A)+ \frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2A_2^2+ (a_3A_1-b_3)^2)}{A_2a_3}\cos(\phi_A), \\ \kappa(L)^2 &= 2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_B)+ \frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3}\cos(\phi_B), \\ 2\kappa'(0) &= 2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_A) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2A_2^2+ (a_3A_1-b_3)^2)}{A_2a_3} \sin(\phi_A), \\ 2\kappa'(L) &= 2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_B) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3} \sin(\phi_B). \end{align} Since the values for $\kappa(L)^2$ given by \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} have to coincide, we get \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I} as a necessary condition. Moreover, using the explicit formula for $\kappa$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1} as well as \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} we obtain the formula for the hyperbolic length $L$ from \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_III}. \medskip It remains to derive \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b1b2},\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II}. The equation \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b1b2} is a direct consequence of \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}. From $\gamma(0)=(A_1,A_2)$ and $\gamma(L)=(B_1,B_2)$ and the explicit formulas for $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} and in particular the relation $b=\frac{b_3}{a_3}a+\frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3}a^\perp$ from \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} imply \begin{align*} \matII{a_1}{a_2}{-a_2}{a_1}\vecII{W_1(0)}{W_2(0)} = \frac{1}{A_2\kappa(0)} \vecII{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}, \qquad \matII{a_1}{a_2}{-a_2}{a_1}\vecII{W_1(L)}{W_2(L)} = \frac{1}{B_2\kappa(L)}\vecII{\sigma_3}{\sigma_4}. \end{align*} Notice that we used here $\sigma_1=1-a_3A_2\kappa(0),\sigma_2=1-a_3A_2\kappa(L)$, see \eqref{eq:sigmas} and \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b}. Using $a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2$ from~\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} we may solve this linear problem and arrive at \begin{align} \vecII{W_1(0)}{W_2(0)} = \frac{1}{a_3^2A_2\kappa(0)}\vecII{ a_1\sigma_1 - a_2\sigma_2}{ a_2\sigma_1 + a_1\sigma_2}, \qquad \vecII{W_1(L)}{W_2(L)} = \frac{1}{a_3^2B_2\kappa(L)} \vecII{ a_1\sigma_3 - a_2\sigma_4}{ a_2\sigma_3 + a_1\sigma_4}. \end{align} From \eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1} and \eqref{eq:DirProblem_equationsforW_1W_2} we get \begin{align*} e^{i\vartheta(0)} = \frac{a_2\sigma_1+a_1\sigma_2+i(a_2\sigma_2-a_1\sigma_1)}{ \sqrt{(a_1^2+a_2^2)(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)}}, \qquad e^{i\vartheta(L)} = \frac{a_2\sigma_3+a_1\sigma_4+i(a_2\sigma_4-a_1\sigma_3)}{ \sqrt{(a_1^2+a_2^2)(\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2)}}. \end{align*} The first equation and $a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2$ imply \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2}. Dividing both equations we finally end up with \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II}. This finishes the ''only if''-part of our statement. \medskip Now we assume the conditions \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3}--\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} to hold and define $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ by the formulas \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1},\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}. Then, by definition of $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$, the conditions \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} hold so that $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ is an orbitlike elastica by Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} with angle function $\phi$ that satisfies \eqref{eq:formula_phi}. Exploiting the identities~\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} we have \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2 &= (1-A_2a_3\kappa(0))^2 + \mu(A_1a_3-b_3)^2 \\ &= \frac{(2\mu-2\kappa(0)^2-2\kappa(0)\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)+\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &+ \frac{\mu(\kappa(0)^2\sin(\phi_A)+2\kappa'(0)\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2}\\ &= \frac{(\kappa(0)^2-\mu)(2\kappa(0)+2\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)-\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &= (\kappa(0)^2-\mu)A_2^2a_3^2, \end{aligned} \end{align} where we used once again $4(\kappa')^2=4\kappa^2-\kappa^4-4\mu$. This entails \begin{align} \begin{aligned} &\;aW(0)+ia^\perp W(0) \\ &= (W_2(0)-iW_1(0))(a_2+ia_1) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2}}{=} \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(0)}e^{i\vartheta(0)}\cdot a_3 \frac{\sigma_1+i\sigma_2}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}}e^{-i\vartheta(0)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:sigma12_sq}}{=} \frac{\sigma_1+i\sigma_2}{\kappa(0)A_2}. \end{aligned} \end{align} From this identity and $\sigma_1=1-a_3A_2\kappa(0),\sigma_2= \sqrt\mu (A_1a_3-b_3)$ we deduce \begin{align*} \gamma_2(0) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(0)(aW(0)+a_3)} = \frac{1}{\kappa(0)(\frac{\sigma_1}{\kappa(0)A_2}+a_3)} = A_2, \\ \gamma_1(0) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \frac{bW(0)+b_3}{aW(0)+a_3} \\ &= A_2\kappa(0)(bW(0)+b_3) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b1b2}}{=} A_2\kappa(0) \Big( \frac{b_3}{a_3} aW(0)+ \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} a^\perp W(0)+b_3\Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:aW(0)}}{=} \frac{b_3}{a_3} \sigma_1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \sigma_2 + b_3A_2\kappa(0) \\ &= A_1. \end{align*} The same way we find $\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2 = (\kappa(L)^2-\mu)B_2^2a_3^2$ and deduce \begin{align*} aW(L)+ia^\perp W(L) &= (a_2+ia_1)(W_2(L)-iW_1(L)) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1}}{=} (a_2+ia_1)(W_2(0)-iW_1(0)) \frac{\kappa(0)\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(L)\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}} e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II}}{=} \big(aW(0)+ia^\perp W(0)\big) \frac{\kappa(0)\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}}{\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}\kappa(L)} \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}\sqrt{\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2}} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:aW(0)}}{=} \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}(\sigma_1+i\sigma_2)}{A_2\kappa(L)\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}} \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}\sqrt{\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2}} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}}{A_2\kappa(L)\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}} \frac{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{\sqrt{\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2}} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:sigma12_sq}}{=} \frac{\sigma_3+i\sigma_4}{B_2\kappa(L)}. \end{align*} As above we deduce $\gamma_1(L)=B_1,\gamma_2(L)=B_2$ so that it remains to show $e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}$. To this end we prove the formulas \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a}--\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} for $\kappa(0),\ldots,2\kappa'(L)$ from the ''only if''-part. First we note that the formula for $\kappa(L)$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b} holds by our definition of $L$ from \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_III}. Then the formula for $\kappa(L)^2$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} is a direct consequence of assumption \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I} and the formula for $2\kappa'(L)$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} follows from $\mathrm{sign}(\kappa'(L))=\sigma$ and \begin{align*} 4\kappa'(L)^2 &= 4\kappa(L)^2-4\mu -\kappa(L)^4 \\ &= 4\cdot \frac{1+\mu(B_2^2a_3^2+(a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3}-4\mu \\ &\;- \Big(2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_B)+ \frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3}\cos(\phi_B)\Big)^2 \\ &= 4\Big(\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_B) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3} \sin(\phi_B)\Big)^2. \end{align*} The formulas for $\kappa(0),\kappa(0)^2,2\kappa'(0)$ follow from the definition of $a_3,b_3$ and $4(\kappa')^2=4\kappa^2-\kappa^4-4\mu$. With these formulas we deduce $e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}$ from~\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2}, which is all what remained to be shown.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Necessity: boundary values of the a_3,b_3 formulas give kappa(0),kappa(L), their derivatives and the vartheta condition; sufficiency: verify boundary positions and angles from the explicit formulas.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: In a first step we prove that every solution of \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP2} satisfies \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3}--\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} for some $l\in\mathbb{Z}$. In the second step we show that these conditions indeed provide solutions of the Dirichlet problem.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Necessity then sufficiency.

nodes.name: Boundary relations
nodes.statement: So let $\gamma$ be a solution of the Dirichlet problem with angle function $\phi$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} the formulas \eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} and $e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}$ yield \begin{align*} a_3 &= \frac{2\kappa(0)+2\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)-\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A)}{2\mu A_2}, \\ a_3 &= \frac{2\kappa(L)+2\kappa'(L)\sin(\phi_B)-\kappa(L)^2\cos(\phi_B)}{2\mu B_2}, \\ b_3 &= a_3 A_1 - \frac{\kappa(0)^2\sin(\phi_A)+2\kappa'(0)\cos(\phi_A)}{2\mu}, \\ b_3 &= a_3 B_1 - \frac{\kappa(L)^2\sin(\phi_B)+2\kappa'(L)\cos(\phi_B)}{2\mu}. \end{align*} These equations imply \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b3} as well as \begin{align} \matII{\cos(\phi_A)}{-\sin(\phi_A)}{\sin(\phi_A)}{\cos(\phi_A)}\vecII{\kappa(0)^2}{2\kappa'(0)} &= \vecII{2\kappa(0)-2\mu A_2 a_3}{2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)}, \\ \matII{\cos(\phi_B)}{-\sin(\phi_B)}{\sin(\phi_B)}{\cos(\phi_B)}\vecII{\kappa(L)^2}{2\kappa'(L)} &= \vecII{2\kappa(L)-2\mu B_2 a_3}{2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the a_3,b_3 formulas at 0 and L.

nodes.name: Rotated boundary curvature relations
nodes.statement: \matII{\cos(\phi_A)}{-\sin(\phi_A)}{\sin(\phi_A)}{\cos(\phi_A)}\vecII{\kappa(0)^2}{2\kappa'(0)} &= \vecII{2\kappa(0)-2\mu A_2 a_3}{2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)}, \\ \matII{\cos(\phi_B)}{-\sin(\phi_B)}{\sin(\phi_B)}{\cos(\phi_B)}\vecII{\kappa(L)^2}{2\kappa'(L)} &= \vecII{2\kappa(L)-2\mu B_2 a_3}{2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)}.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:DirProblem_Formula1a

nodes.name: kappa at endpoints
nodes.statement: Taking the modulus on each side and using $\kappa^4+4(\kappa')^2=4(\kappa^2-\mu)$ we find that the quadratic term $4\kappa(0)^2,4\kappa(L)^2$ cancels and we get \begin{align} \kappa(0) &= \frac{1+\mu(a_3^2A_2^2+(a_3A_1-b_3)^2)}{2A_2a_3}, \\ \kappa(L) &= \frac{1+\mu(a_3^2B_2^2+(a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Take moduli to obtain kappa(0), kappa(L).

nodes.name: Boundary curvature values
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:DirProblem_Formula2a

nodes.name: kappa^2, kappa' at endpoints
nodes.statement: Plugging these formulas into \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula1a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula1b} we may solve for $\kappa(0)^2,2\kappa'(0),\kappa(L)^2,2\kappa'(L)$ and find \begin{align} \kappa(0)^2 &= 2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_A)+ \frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2A_2^2+ (a_3A_1-b_3)^2)}{A_2a_3}\cos(\phi_A), \\ \kappa(L)^2 &= 2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_B)+ \frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3}\cos(\phi_B), \\ 2\kappa'(0) &= 2\mu(a_3A_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_A) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2A_2^2+ (a_3A_1-b_3)^2)}{A_2a_3} \sin(\phi_A), \\ 2\kappa'(L) &= 2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_B) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3} \sin(\phi_B). \end{align}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Solve for kappa^2 and 2kappa' at both ends.

nodes.name: Boundary values of kappa^2 and 2kappa'
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:DirProblem_Formula3a

nodes.name: First equation and L
nodes.statement: Since the values for $\kappa(L)^2$ given by \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} have to coincide, we get \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I} as a necessary condition. Moreover, using the explicit formula for $\kappa$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1} as well as \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} we obtain the formula for the hyperbolic length $L$ from \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_III}.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Consistency gives equation (59); kappa(L) formula gives L.

nodes.name: Remaining
nodes.statement: It remains to derive \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b1b2},\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II}.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: It remains to derive the a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2 formulas and (60).

nodes.name: W at endpoints
nodes.statement: The equation \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b1b2} is a direct consequence of \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}. From $\gamma(0)=(A_1,A_2)$ and $\gamma(L)=(B_1,B_2)$ and the explicit formulas for $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} and in particular the relation $b=\frac{b_3}{a_3}a+\frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3}a^\perp$ from \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} imply \begin{align*} \matII{a_1}{a_2}{-a_2}{a_1}\vecII{W_1(0)}{W_2(0)} = \frac{1}{A_2\kappa(0)} \vecII{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}, \qquad \matII{a_1}{a_2}{-a_2}{a_1}\vecII{W_1(L)}{W_2(L)} = \frac{1}{B_2\kappa(L)}\vecII{\sigma_3}{\sigma_4}. \end{align*} Notice that we used here $\sigma_1=1-a_3A_2\kappa(0),\sigma_2=1-a_3A_2\kappa(L)$, see \eqref{eq:sigmas} and \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b}. Using $a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2$ from~\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} we may solve this linear problem and arrive at \begin{align} \vecII{W_1(0)}{W_2(0)} = \frac{1}{a_3^2A_2\kappa(0)}\vecII{ a_1\sigma_1 - a_2\sigma_2}{ a_2\sigma_1 + a_1\sigma_2}, \qquad \vecII{W_1(L)}{W_2(L)} = \frac{1}{a_3^2B_2\kappa(L)} \vecII{ a_1\sigma_3 - a_2\sigma_4}{ a_2\sigma_3 + a_1\sigma_4}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Solve for W(0), W(L) from boundary positions.

nodes.name: Boundary values of W_1, W_2
nodes.statement: \vecII{W_1(0)}{W_2(0)} = \frac{1}{a_3^2A_2\kappa(0)}\vecII{ a_1\sigma_1 - a_2\sigma_2}{ a_2\sigma_1 + a_1\sigma_2}, \qquad \vecII{W_1(L)}{W_2(L)} = \frac{1}{a_3^2B_2\kappa(L)} \vecII{ a_1\sigma_3 - a_2\sigma_4}{ a_2\sigma_3 + a_1\sigma_4}.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:DirProblem_equationsforW_1W_2

nodes.name: Angle equation
nodes.statement: From \eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1} and \eqref{eq:DirProblem_equationsforW_1W_2} we get \begin{align*} e^{i\vartheta(0)} = \frac{a_2\sigma_1+a_1\sigma_2+i(a_2\sigma_2-a_1\sigma_1)}{ \sqrt{(a_1^2+a_2^2)(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2)}}, \qquad e^{i\vartheta(L)} = \frac{a_2\sigma_3+a_1\sigma_4+i(a_2\sigma_4-a_1\sigma_3)}{ \sqrt{(a_1^2+a_2^2)(\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2)}}. \end{align*} The first equation and $a_1^2+a_2^2=a_3^2$ imply \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2}. Dividing both equations we finally end up with \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II}. This finishes the ''only if''-part of our statement.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Obtain e^{i vartheta(0)}, e^{i vartheta(L)} and the second equation.

nodes.name: Sufficiency setup
nodes.statement: Now we assume the conditions \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3}--\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} to hold and define $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ by the formulas \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1},\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}. Then, by definition of $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$, the conditions \eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3} hold so that $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ is an orbitlike elastica by Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_formula_orbitlike} with angle function $\phi$ that satisfies \eqref{eq:formula_phi}. Exploiting the identities~\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2} we have \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2 &= (1-A_2a_3\kappa(0))^2 + \mu(A_1a_3-b_3)^2 \\ &= \frac{(2\mu-2\kappa(0)^2-2\kappa(0)\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)+\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &+ \frac{\mu(\kappa(0)^2\sin(\phi_A)+2\kappa'(0)\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2}\\ &= \frac{(\kappa(0)^2-\mu)(2\kappa(0)+2\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)-\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &= (\kappa(0)^2-\mu)A_2^2a_3^2, \end{aligned} \end{align} where we used once again $4(\kappa')^2=4\kappa^2-\kappa^4-4\mu$.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Assume the conditions; compute sigma_1^2+sigma_2^2.

nodes.name: sigma_1^2+sigma_2^2 identity
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2 &= (1-A_2a_3\kappa(0))^2 + \mu(A_1a_3-b_3)^2 \\ &= \frac{(2\mu-2\kappa(0)^2-2\kappa(0)\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)+\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &+ \frac{\mu(\kappa(0)^2\sin(\phi_A)+2\kappa'(0)\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2}\\ &= \frac{(\kappa(0)^2-\mu)(2\kappa(0)+2\kappa'(0)\sin(\phi_A)-\kappa(0)^2\cos(\phi_A))^2}{4\mu^2} \\ &= (\kappa(0)^2-\mu)A_2^2a_3^2, \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:sigma12_sq

nodes.name: Initial position
nodes.statement: This entails \begin{align} \begin{aligned} &\;aW(0)+ia^\perp W(0) \\ &= (W_2(0)-iW_1(0))(a_2+ia_1) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2}}{=} \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(0)}e^{i\vartheta(0)}\cdot a_3 \frac{\sigma_1+i\sigma_2}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}}e^{-i\vartheta(0)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:sigma12_sq}}{=} \frac{\sigma_1+i\sigma_2}{\kappa(0)A_2}. \end{aligned} \end{align} From this identity and $\sigma_1=1-a_3A_2\kappa(0),\sigma_2= \sqrt\mu (A_1a_3-b_3)$ we deduce \begin{align*} \gamma_2(0) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_2}}{=} \frac{1}{\kappa(0)(aW(0)+a_3)} = \frac{1}{\kappa(0)(\frac{\sigma_1}{\kappa(0)A_2}+a_3)} = A_2, \\ \gamma_1(0) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \frac{bW(0)+b_3}{aW(0)+a_3} \\ &= A_2\kappa(0)(bW(0)+b_3) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_b1b2}}{=} A_2\kappa(0) \Big( \frac{b_3}{a_3} aW(0)+ \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} a^\perp W(0)+b_3\Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:aW(0)}}{=} \frac{b_3}{a_3} \sigma_1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \sigma_2 + b_3A_2\kappa(0) \\ &= A_1. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Show gamma(0)=(A_1,A_2).

nodes.name: aW(0)+i a^perp W(0) identity
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\;aW(0)+ia^\perp W(0) \\ &= (W_2(0)-iW_1(0))(a_2+ia_1) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2}}{=} \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(0)}e^{i\vartheta(0)}\cdot a_3 \frac{\sigma_1+i\sigma_2}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}}e^{-i\vartheta(0)} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:sigma12_sq}}{=} \frac{\sigma_1+i\sigma_2}{\kappa(0)A_2}. \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:aW(0)

nodes.name: End position
nodes.statement: The same way we find $\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2 = (\kappa(L)^2-\mu)B_2^2a_3^2$ and deduce \begin{align*} aW(L)+ia^\perp W(L) &= (a_2+ia_1)(W_2(L)-iW_1(L)) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1}}{=} (a_2+ia_1)(W_2(0)-iW_1(0)) \frac{\kappa(0)\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(L)\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}} e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II}}{=} \big(aW(0)+ia^\perp W(0)\big) \frac{\kappa(0)\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}}{\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}\kappa(L)} \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}\sqrt{\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2}} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:aW(0)}}{=} \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}(\sigma_1+i\sigma_2)}{A_2\kappa(L)\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}} \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}\sqrt{\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2}} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(L)^2-\mu}}{A_2\kappa(L)\sqrt{\kappa(0)^2-\mu}} \frac{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}(\sigma_3+i\sigma_4)}{\sqrt{\sigma_3^2+\sigma_4^2}} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:sigma12_sq}}{=} \frac{\sigma_3+i\sigma_4}{B_2\kappa(L)}. \end{align*} As above we deduce $\gamma_1(L)=B_1,\gamma_2(L)=B_2$ so that it remains to show $e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}$.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Show gamma(L)=(B_1,B_2).

nodes.name: Angles
nodes.statement: To this end we prove the formulas \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a}--\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} for $\kappa(0),\ldots,2\kappa'(L)$ from the ''only if''-part. First we note that the formula for $\kappa(L)$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b} holds by our definition of $L$ from \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_III}. Then the formula for $\kappa(L)^2$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} is a direct consequence of assumption \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I} and the formula for $2\kappa'(L)$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} follows from $\mathrm{sign}(\kappa'(L))=\sigma$ and \begin{align*} 4\kappa'(L)^2 &= 4\kappa(L)^2-4\mu -\kappa(L)^4 \\ &= 4\cdot \frac{1+\mu(B_2^2a_3^2+(a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{2B_2a_3}-4\mu \\ &\;- \Big(2\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\sin(\phi_B)+ \frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3}\cos(\phi_B)\Big)^2 \\ &= 4\Big(\mu(a_3B_1-b_3)\cos(\phi_B) -\frac{1+\mu(-a_3^2B_2^2+ (a_3B_1-b_3)^2)}{B_2a_3} \sin(\phi_B)\Big)^2. \end{align*} The formulas for $\kappa(0),\kappa(0)^2,2\kappa'(0)$ follow from the definition of $a_3,b_3$ and $4(\kappa')^2=4\kappa^2-\kappa^4-4\mu$. With these formulas we deduce $e^{i\phi(0)}=e^{i\phi_A},e^{i\phi(L)}=e^{i\phi_B}$ from~\eqref{eq:b3a3_1},\eqref{eq:b3a3_2}, which is all what remained to be shown.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Verify kappa formulas and deduce boundary angles.

nodes.name: Dependence of the angle equation on l
nodes.statement: We remark that the dependency of the equation \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} with respect to $l$ can be made ''more explicit'' because of $\vartheta(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))=\vartheta(s)+l\Delta\theta_k$ for all $s\in\mathbb{R}$, see Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(ii).
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2

nodes.name: Proof of symmetry of orbitlike solutions (Corollary 1 = Theorem 2)
nodes.statement:
We first reduce the problem to the case of positively oriented solutions. So let $\gamma$ be a negatively oriented solution of~\eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} with $- ig(  rac{A_2}{A_1}\sin(\phi_A) + \cos(\phi_A) ig) 
otin (0,2)$. Let $-\kappa$ be its curvature function and $\phi$ its associated angle function via~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. Then $	ilde\gamma:=(-\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ is a positively oriented solution of the same boundary value problem with $(A_1,A_2,\phi_A)$ replaced by $(-A_1,A_2,\pi-\phi_A)$ because the curvature of $	ilde\gamma$ is $\kappa$ and its angle function $	ilde\phi$ satisfies $\phi+	ilde\phi\in \pi(2\mathbb{Z}+1)$, see~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. In particular the initial data of $	ilde\gamma,	ilde\phi$ satisfy $$  rac{	ilde\gamma_2(0)}{	ilde\gamma_1(0)} \sin(	ilde\phi(0)) + \cos(	ilde\phi(0)) =  rac{A_2}{-A_1} \sin(\pi-\phi_A) + \cos(\pi-\phi_A) = -  ig( rac{A_2}{A_1} \sin(\phi_A) + \cos(\phi_A) ig) 
otin (0,2) $$ as well as $(\pi-\phi_A)+(\pi-\phi_B)\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$. So once we have shown that the symmetry result is true for positively oriented orbitlike solutions, we also obtain that $	ilde\gamma$ and hence $\gamma$ is symmetric. So it remains to prove the result for positively oriented orbitlike solutions. \medskip Let $\gamma$ be a positively oriented solution of the given Dirichlet problem so that $a_1,\ldots,b_3,L$ satisfy \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3}--\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} by Theorem~ef{thm:DirProblemI}. We intend to show that $\gamma$ is symmetric about the point $s=L/2$ where $L$ denotes the hyperbolic length of the elastica. This will be done in the following steps: First we show $b_3=0$, then we verify that $\gamma_1(	frac{L}{2})=\sin(\phi(	frac{L}{2}))=0$ and that $\kappa$ is symmetric about $s=	frac{L}{2}$. Invoking the unique solvability of the ODE system~\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa} with such initial data we then deduce $$ \gamma_1(L/2+s)=-\gamma_1(L/2-s),\quad \gamma_2(L/2+s)=\gamma_2(L/2-s),\quad \phi(L/2+s)+\phi(L/2-s)\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z} $$ and the proof is finished. \medskip So we first prove $b_3=0$. Using $A_1=-B_1,A_2=B_2,\phi_A+\phi_B\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ and the formulas for $\kappa(0),\kappa(0)^2,\kappa(L),\kappa(L)^2$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} we deduce $$ \kappa(0)-\kappa(L)=-2\mu b_3  rac{A_1}{A_2},\qquad \kappa(0)^2-\kappa(L)^2=-4\mu b_3  ig( \sin(\phi_A)+ rac{A_1}{A_2}\cos(\phi_A) ig) $$ So if we had $b_3
eq 0$ then $0<\kappa\leq \|\kappa\|_\infty= rac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}<2$ would imply $$ (0,4) 
i \kappa(0)+\kappa(L) = 2 ig(  rac{A_2}{A_1}\sin(\phi_A)+\cos(\phi_A) ig) 
otin (0,4), $$ a contradiction. This proves $b_3=0$. \medskip From $b_3=0$ we get $\sigma_1=\sigma_3,\sigma_2=-\sigma_4$ by~\eqref{eq:sigmas} as well as $\kappa(0)=\kappa(L),\kappa'(0)=-\kappa'(L)$, see~\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a}--\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b}. So there is an $l\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that $$ L = -2s_* + 2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) $$ by the explicit form of the curvature function from~\eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1}. In particular, $\kappa$ is symmetric about $	frac{L}{2}$ and our next aim is to show $\gamma_1(	frac{L}{2})=\sin(\phi(	frac{L}{2}))=0$. To this end we notice that \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} implies  egin{equation} e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))} =  rac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)^2}{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}, \quad	ext{hence }  rac{\sigma_1-i\sigma_2}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}} = \pm e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))/2} = \pm e^{i(\vartheta(L/2)-\vartheta(0))}. \end{equation} Indeed, the formula for $L$ and Proposition~ef{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike} imply $$ \vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0) = \vartheta(-2s_*)+l\Delta	heta_k-\vartheta(0) = (l-1)\Delta	heta_k-2\vartheta(0) = 2  ig( \vartheta(	frac{L}{2}) -\vartheta(0) ig). $$ Additionally, by the choice of $a_1,a_2$ from~\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2} we get  egin{align*} a^\perp W(	frac{L}{2}) &= \Re\Big( (a_1+ia_2)\overline{(W_2+iW_1)(	frac{L}{2})}\Big) \ &= a_3 \Re\Big(  rac{\sigma_2+i\sigma_1}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}}e^{i\vartheta(0)}\cdot  rac{\sqrt{\kappa(	frac{L}{2})^2-\mu}}{\kappa(	frac{L}{2})} e^{i(-\vartheta(L/2)))} \Big) \ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:cor:angle_condition}}{=}  rac{ a_3\sqrt{\kappa(	frac{L}{2})^2-\mu}}{\kappa(	frac{L}{2})} \Re ig( \pm i e^{i\vartheta(L/2))}e^{-i\vartheta(L/2))}  ig) \ &= 0. \end{align*} As a consequence, $b_3=0$ implies $$ \gamma_1(	frac{L}{2}) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=}  rac{bW(	frac{L}{2})+b_3}{aW(	frac{L}{2})+a_3} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=}  rac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3}  rac{a^\perp W(	frac{L}{2})}{aW(	frac{L}{2})+a_3} = 0 $$ so that $\kappa'(	frac{L}{2})=0$ and~\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2} yield $$ 0 = \gamma_1(	frac{L}{2}) =  rac{b_3}{a_3} + rac{1}{2\mu a_3}  ig(\kappa(	frac{L}{2})^2\sin(\phi(	frac{L}{2}))+2\kappa'(	frac{L}{2})\cos(\phi(	frac{L}{2})) ig) =  rac{\kappa(	frac{L}{2})^2\sin(\phi(	frac{L}{2}))}{2\mu a_3}, $$ whence $\sin(\phi(L/2))=0$. As outlined at the beginning of the proof we conclude that the elastica is symmetric.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to positive orientation by reflection; show b_3=0 by contradiction, then that kappa is symmetric about L/2 and gamma_1(L/2)=sin(phi(L/2))=0, and conclude by ODE uniqueness.

nodes.name: Reduction to positive orientation
nodes.statement: We first reduce the problem to the case of positively oriented solutions. So let $\gamma$ be a negatively oriented solution of~\eqref{eq:DirichletBVP} with $-\big( \frac{A_2}{A_1}\sin(\phi_A) + \cos(\phi_A)\big) \notin (0,2)$. Let $-\kappa$ be its curvature function and $\phi$ its associated angle function via~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. Then $\tilde\gamma:=(-\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ is a positively oriented solution of the same boundary value problem with $(A_1,A_2,\phi_A)$ replaced by $(-A_1,A_2,\pi-\phi_A)$ because the curvature of $\tilde\gamma$ is $\kappa$ and its angle function $\tilde\phi$ satisfies $\phi+\tilde\phi\in \pi(2\mathbb{Z}+1)$, see~\eqref{eq:ODE_solution}. In particular the initial data of $\tilde\gamma,\tilde\phi$ satisfy $$ \frac{\tilde\gamma_2(0)}{\tilde\gamma_1(0)} \sin(\tilde\phi(0)) + \cos(\tilde\phi(0)) = \frac{A_2}{-A_1} \sin(\pi-\phi_A) + \cos(\pi-\phi_A) = - \big(\frac{A_2}{A_1} \sin(\phi_A) + \cos(\phi_A)\big) \notin (0,2) $$ as well as $(\pi-\phi_A)+(\pi-\phi_B)\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$. So once we have shown that the symmetry result is true for positively oriented orbitlike solutions, we also obtain that $\tilde\gamma$ and hence $\gamma$ is symmetric. So it remains to prove the result for positively oriented orbitlike solutions.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Reflect gamma_1 to reduce to positively oriented solutions.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 6
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma$ be a positively oriented solution of the given Dirichlet problem so that $a_1,\ldots,b_3,L$ satisfy \eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a3}--\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} by Theorem~\ref{thm:DirProblemI}. We intend to show that $\gamma$ is symmetric about the point $s=L/2$ where $L$ denotes the hyperbolic length of the elastica. This will be done in the following steps:
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Coefficients satisfy the Dirichlet conditions of Theorem 6.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: First we show $b_3=0$, then we verify that $\gamma_1(\tfrac{L}{2})=\sin(\phi(\tfrac{L}{2}))=0$ and that $\kappa$ is symmetric about $s=\tfrac{L}{2}$. Invoking the unique solvability of the ODE system~\eqref{eq:ODE_kappa} with such initial data we then deduce $$ \gamma_1(L/2+s)=-\gamma_1(L/2-s),\quad \gamma_2(L/2+s)=\gamma_2(L/2-s),\quad \phi(L/2+s)+\phi(L/2-s)\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z} $$ and the proof is finished.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Plan: b_3=0, gamma_1(L/2)=sin(phi(L/2))=0, symmetric kappa, ODE uniqueness.

nodes.name: b_3=0
nodes.statement:
So we first prove $b_3=0$. Using $A_1=-B_1,A_2=B_2,\phi_A+\phi_B\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ and the formulas for $\kappa(0),\kappa(0)^2,\kappa(L),\kappa(L)^2$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} we deduce $$ \kappa(0)-\kappa(L)=-2\mu b_3  rac{A_1}{A_2},\qquad \kappa(0)^2-\kappa(L)^2=-4\mu b_3  ig( \sin(\phi_A)+ rac{A_1}{A_2}\cos(\phi_A) ig) $$ So if we had $b_3
eq 0$ then $0<\kappa\leq \|\kappa\|_\infty= rac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}<2$ would imply $$ (0,4) 
i \kappa(0)+\kappa(L) = 2 ig(  rac{A_2}{A_1}\sin(\phi_A)+\cos(\phi_A) ig) 
otin (0,4), $$ a contradiction. This proves $b_3=0$.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Assume b_3 nonzero; contradiction with the angle condition.

nodes.name: kappa symmetric
nodes.statement: From $b_3=0$ we get $\sigma_1=\sigma_3,\sigma_2=-\sigma_4$ by~\eqref{eq:sigmas} as well as $\kappa(0)=\kappa(L),\kappa'(0)=-\kappa'(L)$, see~\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a}--\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b}. So there is an $l\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that $$ L = -2s_* + 2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) $$ by the explicit form of the curvature function from~\eqref{eq:DirProblem_W_2W_1}. In particular, $\kappa$ is symmetric about $\tfrac{L}{2}$ and our next aim is to show $\gamma_1(\tfrac{L}{2})=\sin(\phi(\tfrac{L}{2}))=0$.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: b_3=0 gives L=-2s_*+2l sqrt(2-k^2)K so kappa symmetric about L/2.

nodes.name: a perp W(L/2)=0
nodes.statement: To this end we notice that \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} implies \begin{equation} e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))} = \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)^2}{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}, \quad\text{hence } \frac{\sigma_1-i\sigma_2}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}} = \pm e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))/2} = \pm e^{i(\vartheta(L/2)-\vartheta(0))}. \end{equation} Indeed, the formula for $L$ and Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike} imply $$ \vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0) = \vartheta(-2s_*)+l\Delta\theta_k-\vartheta(0) = (l-1)\Delta\theta_k-2\vartheta(0) = 2 \big( \vartheta(\tfrac{L}{2}) -\vartheta(0)\big). $$ Additionally, by the choice of $a_1,a_2$ from~\eqref{eq:DirProblem_choice_a1a2} we get \begin{align*} a^\perp W(\tfrac{L}{2}) &= \Re\Big( (a_1+ia_2)\overline{(W_2+iW_1)(\tfrac{L}{2})}\Big) \\ &= a_3 \Re\Big( \frac{\sigma_2+i\sigma_1}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}}e^{i\vartheta(0)}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(\tfrac{L}{2})^2-\mu}}{\kappa(\tfrac{L}{2})} e^{i(-\vartheta(L/2)))} \Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:cor:angle_condition}}{=} \frac{ a_3\sqrt{\kappa(\tfrac{L}{2})^2-\mu}}{\kappa(\tfrac{L}{2})} \Re\big( \pm i e^{i\vartheta(L/2))}e^{-i\vartheta(L/2))} \big) \\ &= 0. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Angle condition gives a^perp W(L/2)=0.

nodes.name: Angle condition in the symmetry proof
nodes.statement: e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))} = \frac{(\sigma_1-i\sigma_2)^2}{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}, \quad\text{hence } \frac{\sigma_1-i\sigma_2}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}} = \pm e^{i(\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0))/2} = \pm e^{i(\vartheta(L/2)-\vartheta(0))}.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.label: eq:cor:angle_condition

nodes.name: Midpoint data
nodes.statement: As a consequence, $b_3=0$ implies $$ \gamma_1(\tfrac{L}{2}) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:explicit_formula_orbitlike_1}}{=} \frac{bW(\tfrac{L}{2})+b_3}{aW(\tfrac{L}{2})+a_3} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:a_1a_2a_3b_1b_2b_3}}{=} \frac{1}{\sqrt\mu a_3} \frac{a^\perp W(\tfrac{L}{2})}{aW(\tfrac{L}{2})+a_3} = 0 $$ so that $\kappa'(\tfrac{L}{2})=0$ and~\eqref{eq:a1a2b1b2_2} yield $$ 0 = \gamma_1(\tfrac{L}{2}) = \frac{b_3}{a_3} +\frac{1}{2\mu a_3} \big(\kappa(\tfrac{L}{2})^2\sin(\phi(\tfrac{L}{2}))+2\kappa'(\tfrac{L}{2})\cos(\phi(\tfrac{L}{2}))\big) = \frac{\kappa(\tfrac{L}{2})^2\sin(\phi(\tfrac{L}{2}))}{2\mu a_3}, $$ whence $\sin(\phi(L/2))=0$.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: gamma_1(L/2)=0 and sin(phi(L/2))=0.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: As outlined at the beginning of the proof we conclude that the elastica is symmetric.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry follows by ODE uniqueness.

nodes.name: Classification of orbitlike solutions for A_1=B_1=0 and symmetry breaking
nodes.statement: Let $A_1=B_1=0,A_2=B_2>0,\phi_A=\phi_B=0$. Then all orbitlike solutions of the Dirichlet problem \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP2} are given by $$ k=k_{m,n},\; L=\mathcal{L}_{m,n},\; s_*\in\mathbb{R} \qquad\text{where }m,n\in\mathbb{N} \text{ satisfy }1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2. $$ These solutions are symmetric if and only if $s_*\in \sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)\mathbb{Z}$. In particular, there are uncountably many nonsymmetric solutions.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: For data A_1=B_1=0, A_2=B_2, phi_A=phi_B=0 the orbitlike solutions are exactly the closed gamma_{m,n} with arbitrary s_*; they are symmetric iff s_* lies in a lattice, so uncountably many are nonsymmetric.
conclusions: Then all orbitlike solutions of the Dirichlet problem \eqref{eq:DirichletBVP2} are given by
These solutions are symmetric if and only if $s_*\in \sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)\mathbb{Z}$.
In particular, there are uncountably many nonsymmetric solutions.
nodes.label: cor:Symmetry_breaking

nodes.name: Proof of Classification of orbitlike solutions for A_1=B_1=0 and symmetry breaking
nodes.statement: Let the coefficients $a_1,\ldots,b_3$ and $\sigma,L$ be given as in the theorem so that it remains to identify all $s_*\in\mathbb{R},k\in (0,1),l\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I},\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} are satisfied. Due to $\sin(\phi_B)=0,\cos(\phi_B)=1$ and the formulas for $\kappa(L),\kappa(L)^2$ from \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula3b} the equation \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I} is satisfied for any choice of $s_*,k,l$. For our boundary data we have $\sigma_1=\sigma_3,\sigma_2=\sigma_4=-\sqrt\mu b_3$ so that equation \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} is equivalent to $\vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0)= 2m\pi$ for some $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Moreover, the formulas \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} imply $\kappa(0)=\kappa(L),\kappa'(0)=\kappa'(L)$ and thus $L=2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$. So we deduce from Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(i) $$ 2m\pi = \vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0)=n\Delta\theta_k,\quad \text{hence } 1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2,\; k=k_{m,n}, L=\mathcal{L}_{m,n}. $$ (In other words, the elastica closes up at $s=L$, see section~\ref{subsec:closed_elasticae}.) This yields the above characterization of the solutions. Moreover, as in the previous theorem one checks that these solutions are symmetric if and only if $\kappa$ is symmetric about $s=\frac{L}{2}$, which is true precisely when $s_*\in\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)\mathbb{Z}$. Since this is a countable set of real numbers, we obtain uncountably many solutions for any choice $s_*\notin \sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)\mathbb{Z}$, see~Figure~\ref{Fig:Symmetry_breaking}.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 6: the first equation holds automatically, the second forces closedness L=L_{m,n}, k=k_{m,n}; symmetry iff kappa symmetric about L/2.

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement: Let the coefficients $a_1,\ldots,b_3$ and $\sigma,L$ be given as in the theorem so that it remains to identify all $s_*\in\mathbb{R},k\in (0,1),l\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that \eqref{Gl:DirProblem_I},\eqref{Gl:DirProblem_II} are satisfied.

nodes.statement_short: Equation (60) reduces to vartheta(L)-vartheta(0)=2m pi.

nodes.statement: Moreover, the formulas \eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula2b},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4a},\eqref{eq:DirProblem_Formula4b} imply $\kappa(0)=\kappa(L),\kappa'(0)=\kappa'(L)$ and thus $L=2n\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: kappa(0)=kappa(L), kappa'(0)=kappa'(L) give L=2n sqrt(2-k^2)K.

nodes.name: Closedness
nodes.statement: So we deduce from Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}~(i) $$ 2m\pi = \vartheta(L)-\vartheta(0)=n\Delta\theta_k,\quad \text{hence } 1<\frac{2m}{n}<\sqrt 2,\; k=k_{m,n}, L=\mathcal{L}_{m,n}. $$ (In other words, the elastica closes up at $s=L$, see section~\ref{subsec:closed_elasticae}.) This yields the above characterization of the solutions.
nodes.section: 7 The Dirichlet boundary value problem, Proof of Theorem~3 and~2
nodes.statement_short: Hence k=k_{m,n}, L=L_{m,n}.

nodes.name: Symmetry criterion
nodes.statement: Moreover, as in the previous theorem one checks that these solutions are symmetric if and only if $\kappa$ is symmetric about $s=\frac{L}{2}$, which is true precisely when $s_*\in\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.statement: Since this is a countable set of real numbers, we obtain uncountably many solutions for any choice $s_*\notin \sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)\mathbb{Z}$, see~Figure~\ref{Fig:Symmetry_breaking}.

nodes.name: Proof of Fundamental system of the Lame-type equation w''+2dn^2 w=0
nodes.statement: In order to prove Proposition \ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike} we have to show that for all $k\in (0,1)$ the ODE $w''+2\mathrm{dn}^2(\cdot,k)w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $w_1$ is odd about 0, $w_2$ is even about 0, $w_2(0)>0>w_1'(0)$, \item[(ii)] $w_1(s)^2+w_2(s)^2=2-k^2 -\mathrm{dn}^2(s,k)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(iii)] $w_1(s)w_1'(s)+w_2(s)w_2'(s) = k^2\mathrm{dn}(s,k)\mathrm{cn}(s,k)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(iv)] $w_1'(s)^2+w_2'(s)^2=1-k^2+\mathrm{dn}^4(s,k)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(v)] $w_1(s)w_2'(s)-w_2(s)w_1'(s) = \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, \item[(vi)] $(w_1+iw_2)(s+2lK(k))= (w_1+iw_2)(s)e^{il\Delta\theta_k}$ for all $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$. \item[(vii)] $(w_1+iw_2)(-K(k))= e^{i(\pi-\Delta\theta_k)/2}$. \end{itemize} \medskip In the proof we make use of the special functions introduced in section~\ref{sec:Jacobi}. From \cite{Whit_modern_analysis}, p.570--575 we obtain that every solution of $w''+2\mathrm{dn}^2(\cdot,k)w=0$ is a linear combination of the so-called Halphen-Hermite solutions $w_+,w_-:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ (first discovered in \cite{Her_extrait,Hal_fonc_ell}) which are given by \begin{equation} w_\pm(s) = \frac{H(s\mp i\alpha,k)}{\Theta(s,k)}e^{s\zeta(\pm i\alpha,k)}\quad\text{for } \alpha\in\mathbb{C} \text{ s.t.} \mathrm{dn}^2(i\alpha,k)=2-k^2. \end{equation} Here, the functions $H,\Theta,\zeta:\mathbb{C}\times(0,1)\to\mathbb{C}$ denote Jacobi's eta, theta and zeta functions from section~\ref{sec:Jacobi}. By Jacobi's imaginary transformation (see 161.01 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}) we have $$ \mathrm{dn}(i\alpha,k)^2 = \frac{\mathrm{dn}^2(\alpha,k')}{\mathrm{cn}^2(\alpha,k')} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:Jacobi_trigonometric_identities}}{=} \frac{1-(k')^2\mathrm{sn}^2(\alpha,k')}{1-\mathrm{sn}^2(\alpha,k')} = 1 + \frac{k^2\mathrm{sn}^2(\alpha,k')}{1-\mathrm{sn}^2(\alpha,k')} \qquad (k':=\sqrt{1-k^2}) $$ so that one possible choice is $\alpha=\alpha_k$ where $\mathrm{sn}(\alpha_k,k')=k'$, i.e. $\alpha_k:=F(k',k')$, see \eqref{eq:Jac_Inverse}. From the series representation of these special functions in \eqref{eq:JacobianTheta_series} we deduce $w_-=\bar{w}_+$ so that 141.01 and 1051.02 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} imply that $\Re(w_\pm)$ is odd and $\Im(w_\pm)$ is even. We then define $w_1,w_2:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ through the formula \begin{equation} w_1(s)+iw_2(s) := \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\Im(w_+(0))} w_+(s) \end{equation} so that (i) holds. \medskip By Proposition 6 in \cite{Val_Heun} for $m_1=m_2=m_3=0,N=1,m_0=1,s=\frac{1}{2},\sigma=2$ the product of the two Hermite-Halphen solutions, i.e. $w_+w_-=|w_+|^2$ and thus $w_1^2+w_2^2$, is a real multiple of the function $2-k^2-\mathrm{dn}^2(\cdot,k)$. Hence, \eqref{eq:def_w1w2} and the oddness of $w_1$ yield $w_1(0)=0,w_2(0)=\sqrt{1-k^2}$ so that (ii) holds. Differentiating (ii) and using \eqref{eq:Jacobi_ODE_1terOrdnung},\eqref{eq:Jacobi_ODE_2terOrdnung} we get (iii) and (iv). Part (v) follows from the constancy of the Wronskian and $w_1(0)=w_2'(0)=0,w_2(0)=\sqrt{1-k^2},w_1'(0)=-\sqrt{2-k^2}$ by (i),(ii),(iv). \medskip We now prove (vi) and (vii). Using 1051.04 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook} we get \begin{align*} w_+(s+2lK(k)) &= \frac{H(s+2lK(k)-i\alpha_k,k)}{\Theta(s+2lK(k),k)}e^{(s+2lK(k))\zeta(i\alpha_k,k)} \\ &= \frac{(-1)^l H(s-i\alpha_k,k)}{\Theta(s,k)}e^{s\zeta(i\alpha_k,k)} e^{2lK(k)\zeta(i\alpha_k,k)} \\ &= w_+(s) e^{l(2K(k)\zeta(i\alpha_k,k)+\pi i)}. \end{align*} Using various identities from \cite{ByrFri_handbook} (see below for details) we find \begin{align*} &\; K(k)\zeta(i\alpha_k,k) \\ &= K(k)i\cdot \Big( -\zeta(\alpha_k,k') - \frac{\pi \alpha_k}{2K(k)K'(k)} +\frac{\mathrm{sn}(\alpha_k,k')\mathrm{dn}(\alpha_k,k')}{\mathrm{cn}(\alpha_k,k')} \Big) \\ &= K(k)i\cdot \Big( - \zeta(\alpha_k,k') - \frac{\pi F(k',k')}{2K(k)K'(k)} + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2} \Big) \\ &= K(k)i\cdot \Big( - E(k',k') + \frac{E(k')}{K(k')}F(k',k') - \frac{\pi F(k',k')}{2K(k)K'(k)} + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2} \Big) \\ &= i\cdot \Big( - E(k',k')K(k) + \frac{F(k',k')}{K(k')}(E(k')K(k)-\frac{\pi}{2}) + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) \Big) \\ &= i\cdot \Big( - E(k',k')K(k) + \frac{F(k',k')}{K(k')}(K(k')(K(k)-E(k))) + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) \Big) \\ &= i\cdot \Big( - (E(k',k')K(k) + F(k',k')(E(k)-K(k))) + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) \Big) \\ &= i\cdot \Big( - \frac{\pi}{2}\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k) + \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k) \Big) \\ &= i\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\Delta\theta_k-\pi). \end{align*} In the first equality we used 143.02, in the second we used $\mathrm{sn}(\alpha_k,k')=k'$, in the third 130.02 and 140.01, then 110.10 in the fifth and 150.03 in the seventh and the eigth equality results from the definition of $\Delta\theta_k$, see~\eqref{eq:def_rotation}. This proves (vi). Finally, we have \begin{align*} (w_1+iw_2)(-K(k)) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:Hermite_Halphen}}{=} e^{-K(k)\zeta(i\alpha_k,k)} = e^{i(\pi-\Delta\theta_k)/2} \end{align*} because of $(w_1^2+w_2^2)(-K(k))=1$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}~(ii) and because $H(-K(k)-i\alpha_k,k)$, $\Theta(-K(k),k)$ are real and positive for all $k\in (0,1)$ by \eqref{eq:JacobianTheta_series}.
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Construct w_1+iw_2 as a normalized Hermite-Halphen solution H(s-i alpha)/Theta(s) e^{s zeta(i alpha)}; derive the identities from Heun-function results and theta-function formulas. nodes.name: Proof of Identities for the fundamental system W_1, W_2 (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Next we prove Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}, i.e. that the functions $W_1,W_2$ given by $$ W_j(s)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} w_j(-K(k)+\frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}) \quad (j=1,2) $$ satisfy the following identities: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $W_1^2+W_2^2 = \frac{\kappa^2-\mu}{\kappa^2}$, \item[(ii)] $W_1'= \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_1 - \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_2 $, \item[(iii)] $W_2' = \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_1 + \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_2$, \item[(iv)] $W_1W_2'-W_2W_1' = \frac{\sqrt\mu}{2}$, \item[(v)] $(W_1+iW_2)(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))=(W_1+iW_2)(s)e^{il\Delta\theta_k}$ for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$, \item[(vi)] $(W_1+iW_2)(s)= (-W_1+iW_2)(-s-2s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k}$ for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$. \end{itemize} \medskip For the proof we set $z:=-K(k)+ \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}$ so that \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike},\eqref{eq:def_Wj} give \begin{align} \begin{aligned} w_j(z)= \sqrt{2-k^2}W_j(s),&\quad w_j'(z)= (2-k^2)W_j'(s) \quad (j=1,2)\\ \kappa(s) &= \frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\mathrm{dn}(z+K(k),k),\\ \kappa'(s) &= -\frac{2k^2}{2-k^2}\mathrm{sn}(z+K(k),k)\mathrm{cn}(z+K(k),k). \end{aligned} \end{align} Using the identities from \eqref{eq:Jac_Additionstheoreme} we get \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \mathrm{dn}(z,k) &= \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\mathrm{dn}(z+K(k),k)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)}, \\ \mathrm{sn}(z,k)\mathrm{cn}(z,k) &= - \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2} \mathrm{sn}(z+K(k),k)\mathrm{cn}(z+K(k),k)}{\mathrm{dn}^2(z+K(k),k)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{k^2} \frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}. \end{aligned} \end{align} In particular, using that $w_1,w_2$ are linearly independent by Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike} (i) as well as \begin{align*} W_j''(s) = \frac{1}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}}w_j''(z) = - \frac{2}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \mathrm{dn}^2(z,k) w_j(z) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn}}{=} - 2\mu\kappa(s)^{-2} W_j(s) \quad\text{for $j=1,2$}, \end{align*} we get that $\{W_1,W_2\}$ is a fundamental system of the given ODE. Now we exploit \eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s},\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn} and Proposition~\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike} in order to prove (i)-(vi). The first item follows from \begin{align*} W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2 &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{w_1(z)^2+w_2(z)^2}{2-k^2} \stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(ii)}{=} 1-\frac{\mathrm{dn}^2(z,k)}{2-k^2} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn}}{=} \frac{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}{\kappa(s)^2}. \\ \intertext{The assertion (ii) is true because of} W_1'(s) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{1}{2-k^2} w_1'(z) \\ &= \frac{1}{2-k^2} \frac{w_1(z)(w_1w_1'+w_2w_2')(z)-w_2(z)(w_1w_2'-w_2w_1')(z)}{(w_1^2+w_2^2)(z)} \\ &\hspace{-1.2cm}\stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(ii)-(iv)}{=} \frac{1}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \frac{k^2\mathrm{dn}(z,k)\mathrm{cn}(z,k)\mathrm{sn}(z,k) W_1(s)- \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}W_2(s)}{W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn}}{=}\frac{4(1-k^2)}{(2-k^2)^2} \frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^3} \frac{W_1(s)}{W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2} - \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{2-k^2} \frac{W_2(s)}{W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2} \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}.(i)}{=} \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} W_1(s) - \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)}W_2(s). \\ \intertext{Similarly, (iii) follows from} W_2'(s) &= \frac{1}{2-k^2} \frac{w_2(z)(w_1w_1'+w_2w_2')(z)+w_1(z)(w_1w_2'-w_2w_1')(z)}{(w_1^2+w_2^2)(z)} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)}W_1(s) + \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} W_2(s). \\ \intertext{ The items (iv),(v) follow directly from Proposition~\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}~(iv),(v). Finally, we set $t:= -s-2s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ so that (vi) results from} W_1(s)+iW_2(s) &= (w_1+iw_2) \big( -K(k)+\frac{-(t+s_*)+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \big) \\ &= (w_1+iw_2) \big( K(k)-\frac{t+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} + (2l-2)K(k)\big) \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(vi)}{=} (w_1+iw_2) \big(K(k)-\frac{t+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\big) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k} \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(i)}{=} (-w_1+iw_2) \big(-K(k)+\frac{t+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\big) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k} \\ &= (-W_1(t)+iW_2(t)) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Change variables z=-K+(s+s_*)/sqrt(2-k^2) and transfer the identities of Proposition 2 using the addition formulas for Jacobi functions.

nodes.name: Restatement
nodes.statement: Next we prove Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}, i.e. that the functions $W_1,W_2$ given by $$ W_j(s)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} w_j(-K(k)+\frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}) \quad (j=1,2) $$ satisfy the following identities: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $W_1^2+W_2^2 = \frac{\kappa^2-\mu}{\kappa^2}$, \item[(ii)] $W_1'= \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_1 - \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_2 $, \item[(iii)] $W_2' = \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)}W_1 + \frac{\mu \kappa'}{\kappa(\kappa^2-\mu)} W_2$, \item[(iv)] $W_1W_2'-W_2W_1' = \frac{\sqrt\mu}{2}$, \item[(v)] $(W_1+iW_2)(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))=(W_1+iW_2)(s)e^{il\Delta\theta_k}$ for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$, \item[(vi)] $(W_1+iW_2)(s)= (-W_1+iW_2)(-s-2s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k}$ for $s\in\mathbb{R},l\in\mathbb{Z}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Restate the identities.

nodes.name: Change of variables
nodes.statement: For the proof we set $z:=-K(k)+ \frac{s+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}$ so that \eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike},\eqref{eq:def_Wj} give \begin{align} \begin{aligned} w_j(z)= \sqrt{2-k^2}W_j(s),&\quad w_j'(z)= (2-k^2)W_j'(s) \quad (j=1,2)\\ \kappa(s) &= \frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\mathrm{dn}(z+K(k),k),\\ \kappa'(s) &= -\frac{2k^2}{2-k^2}\mathrm{sn}(z+K(k),k)\mathrm{cn}(z+K(k),k). \end{aligned} \end{align} Using the identities from \eqref{eq:Jac_Additionstheoreme} we get \begin{align} \begin{aligned} \mathrm{dn}(z,k) &= \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\mathrm{dn}(z+K(k),k)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)}, \\ \mathrm{sn}(z,k)\mathrm{cn}(z,k) &= - \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2} \mathrm{sn}(z+K(k),k)\mathrm{cn}(z+K(k),k)}{\mathrm{dn}^2(z+K(k),k)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{k^2} \frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}. \end{aligned} \end{align}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Set z and express kappa, kappa', dn, sn cn in s.

nodes.name: Change of variables z vs s
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} w_j(z)= \sqrt{2-k^2}W_j(s),&\quad w_j'(z)= (2-k^2)W_j'(s) \quad (j=1,2)\\ \kappa(s) &= \frac{2}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\mathrm{dn}(z+K(k),k),\\ \kappa'(s) &= -\frac{2k^2}{2-k^2}\mathrm{sn}(z+K(k),k)\mathrm{cn}(z+K(k),k). \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.label: eq:formulas_z_vs_s

nodes.name: dn, sn cn in terms of kappa
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{dn}(z,k) &= \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\mathrm{dn}(z+K(k),k)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \frac{1}{\kappa(s)}, \\ \mathrm{sn}(z,k)\mathrm{cn}(z,k) &= - \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2} \mathrm{sn}(z+K(k),k)\mathrm{cn}(z+K(k),k)}{\mathrm{dn}^2(z+K(k),k)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{2\sqrt{1-k^2}}{k^2} \frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2}. \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.label: eq:formulas_dnsncn

nodes.name: Fundamental system
nodes.statement: In particular, using that $w_1,w_2$ are linearly independent by Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike} (i) as well as \begin{align*} W_j''(s) = \frac{1}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}}w_j''(z) = - \frac{2}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \mathrm{dn}^2(z,k) w_j(z) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn}}{=} - 2\mu\kappa(s)^{-2} W_j(s) \quad\text{for $j=1,2$}, \end{align*} we get that $\{W_1,W_2\}$ is a fundamental system of the given ODE.
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: W_1,W_2 solve W''+2 mu kappa^{-2}W=0.

nodes.name: Identities (i)-(vi)
nodes.statement: Now we exploit \eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s},\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn} and Proposition~\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike} in order to prove (i)-(vi). The first item follows from \begin{align*} W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2 &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{w_1(z)^2+w_2(z)^2}{2-k^2} \stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(ii)}{=} 1-\frac{\mathrm{dn}^2(z,k)}{2-k^2} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn}}{=} \frac{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}{\kappa(s)^2}. \\ \intertext{The assertion (ii) is true because of} W_1'(s) &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_z_vs_s}}{=} \frac{1}{2-k^2} w_1'(z) \\ &= \frac{1}{2-k^2} \frac{w_1(z)(w_1w_1'+w_2w_2')(z)-w_2(z)(w_1w_2'-w_2w_1')(z)}{(w_1^2+w_2^2)(z)} \\ &\hspace{-1.2cm}\stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(ii)-(iv)}{=} \frac{1}{(2-k^2)^{3/2}} \frac{k^2\mathrm{dn}(z,k)\mathrm{cn}(z,k)\mathrm{sn}(z,k) W_1(s)- \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}W_2(s)}{W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2} \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:formulas_dnsncn}}{=}\frac{4(1-k^2)}{(2-k^2)^2} \frac{\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^3} \frac{W_1(s)}{W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2} - \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}}{2-k^2} \frac{W_2(s)}{W_1(s)^2+W_2(s)^2} \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}.(i)}{=} \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} W_1(s) - \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)}W_2(s). \\ \intertext{Similarly, (iii) follows from} W_2'(s) &= \frac{1}{2-k^2} \frac{w_2(z)(w_1w_1'+w_2w_2')(z)+w_1(z)(w_1w_2'-w_2w_1')(z)}{(w_1^2+w_2^2)(z)} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)}W_1(s) + \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} W_2(s). \\ \intertext{ The items (iv),(v) follow directly from Proposition~\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}~(iv),(v). Finally, we set $t:= -s-2s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)$ so that (vi) results from} W_1(s)+iW_2(s) &= (w_1+iw_2) \big( -K(k)+\frac{-(t+s_*)+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \big) \\ &= (w_1+iw_2) \big( K(k)-\frac{t+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} + (2l-2)K(k)\big) \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(vi)}{=} (w_1+iw_2) \big(K(k)-\frac{t+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\big) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k} \\ &\stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(i)}{=} (-w_1+iw_2) \big(-K(k)+\frac{t+s_*}{\sqrt{2-k^2}}\big) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k} \\ &= (-W_1(t)+iW_2(t)) e^{i(l-1)\Delta\theta_k}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the identities of Proposition 2.

nodes.name: Proof of Properties of the angle function vartheta (orbitlike)
nodes.statement: Next we prove the assertions from Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}, namely $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\qquad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{\frac{-\sqrt{\mu}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cos(\vartheta)}{\sin(\vartheta)}{-\sin(\vartheta)}{\cos(\vartheta)} $$ as well as \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $\vartheta(-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)) = \frac{l-1}{2}\Delta\theta_k$, \item[(ii)] $\vartheta(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(s) = l\Delta\theta_k$, \item[(iii)] $\vartheta(-s_*+s)+\vartheta(-s_*-s) = -\Delta\theta_k$. \end{itemize} To this end we set $c(s):= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(s)}$ so that the defining equation for $\vartheta$ \eqref{eq:def_theta} reads $$ \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} = c(s) \vecII{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))}. $$ Differentiating both sides and using Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(ii),(iii) we arrive at \begin{align*} &-c(s)\vartheta'(s) \vecII{\cos(\vartheta(s))}{\sin(\vartheta(s))} + c'(s) \vecII{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))} \quad =\quad \vecII{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} + \frac{\sqrt\mu\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-W_2(s)}{W_1(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))} - \frac{\sqrt\mu\kappa(s)^2c(s)}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{\cos(\vartheta(s))}{\sin(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*} This identity gives $$ \vartheta'(s) = \frac{\sqrt{\mu}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)},\qquad c'(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)}c(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}} $$ and thus the first claim follows from \begin{align*} \matII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)}{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} &= \matII{0}{c(s)}{-c(s)\vartheta'(s)}{c'(s)} \matII{\cos(\vartheta(s))}{\sin(\vartheta(s))}{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*} Now we prove (i),(ii),(iii). For $l\in\mathbb{Z}$ we have \begin{align*} \vartheta(-s_*+ l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(-s_*) &= \int_{-s_*}^{-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \vartheta'(s) \,ds\\ &= \int_{-s_*}^{-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \frac{\sqrt{\mu}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \,ds \\ &= \int_0^{lK(k)} \frac{\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{\mu} \kappa(\sqrt{2-k^2}s-s_*)^2}{2(\kappa(\sqrt{2-k^2}s-s_*)^2-\mu)} \,ds \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} \int_0^{lK(k)} \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{(2-k^2)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2-1+k^2} \,ds \\ &= \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2} \int_0^{lK(k)} \frac{\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{(2-k^2)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2-1+k^2} \,ds \\ &= \frac{l}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \int_0^{K(k)} \frac{\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{1-k^2(2-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2} \,ds. \end{align*} Here we used $\mathrm{dn}^2=1-k^2\mathrm{sn}^2$ and $\mathrm{dn}(2K(k)-s,k)=\mathrm{dn}(2K(k)+s,k)=\mathrm{dn}(s,k)$ in the last equation, see~\eqref{eq:Jacobi_trigonometric_identities}. The proof of (i) is finished once we have proved that the second factor equals $\Delta\theta_k$. Using the formula 412.04 from \cite{ByrFri_handbook} for $\alpha:=k\sqrt{2-k^2}>k$ we get \begin{align*} &\;2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \int_0^{K(k)} \frac{ \mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{1-k^2(2-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2} \,ds \\ &= 2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \Big( K(k) + \frac{\pi \sqrt{\alpha^2-k^2} (1-\Lambda_0(\arcsin(\sqrt{(1-\alpha^2)(k')^{-2}}),k))}{2\alpha\sqrt{1-\alpha^2}} \Big) \\ &= 2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \Big( K(k) + \frac{\pi(1-\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k)) }{2\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}} \Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_rotation}}{=} \Delta\theta_k. \end{align*} So (i) is proved once we have shown $\vartheta(-s_*)=-\Delta\theta_k/2$. This identity, however, follows from $-2\pi<\vartheta(-s_*)\leq 0$ and \begin{align*} e^{i\vartheta(-s_*)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta}}{=} \frac{(W_2-iW_1)(-s_*)}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_Wj}}{=} (w_2-iw_1)(-K(k)) = -i(w_1+iw_2)(-K(k)) \stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(vii)}{=} e^{- i\Delta\theta_k /2}. \end{align*} Item (ii) holds thanks to the $2\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)-$periodicity of $\vartheta'$ and (i), namely $$ \vartheta(s+ 2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(s) = \int_{s}^{s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \vartheta'(z) \,dz\\ = \int_{-s_*}^{-s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \vartheta'(z) \,dz = l\Delta\theta_k $$ Finally, $\vartheta'(-s_*+s)=\vartheta'(-s_*-s)$ and $2\vartheta(-s_*)=-\Delta\theta_k$ imply~(iii).
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the polar representation of (W_1,W_2) to get vartheta'; integrate vartheta' over a period using Byrd-Friedman 412.04 to obtain Delta theta_k.

nodes.name: Restatement
nodes.statement: Next we prove the assertions from Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_orbitlike}, namely $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt\mu \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\qquad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{\frac{-\sqrt{\mu}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cos(\vartheta)}{\sin(\vartheta)}{-\sin(\vartheta)}{\cos(\vartheta)} $$ as well as \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $\vartheta(-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)) = \frac{l-1}{2}\Delta\theta_k$, \item[(ii)] $\vartheta(s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(s) = l\Delta\theta_k$, \item[(iii)] $\vartheta(-s_*+s)+\vartheta(-s_*-s) = -\Delta\theta_k$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Restate the assertions.

nodes.name: vartheta' and matrix form
nodes.statement: To this end we set $c(s):= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(s)}$ so that the defining equation for $\vartheta$ \eqref{eq:def_theta} reads $$ \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} = c(s) \vecII{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))}. $$ Differentiating both sides and using Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_orbitlike}~(ii),(iii) we arrive at \begin{align*} &-c(s)\vartheta'(s) \vecII{\cos(\vartheta(s))}{\sin(\vartheta(s))} + c'(s) \vecII{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))} \quad =\quad \vecII{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} + \frac{\sqrt\mu\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-W_2(s)}{W_1(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))} - \frac{\sqrt\mu\kappa(s)^2c(s)}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{\cos(\vartheta(s))}{\sin(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*} This identity gives $$ \vartheta'(s) = \frac{\sqrt{\mu}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)},\qquad c'(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)}c(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}} $$ and thus the first claim follows from \begin{align*} \matII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)}{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} &= \matII{0}{c(s)}{-c(s)\vartheta'(s)}{c'(s)} \matII{\cos(\vartheta(s))}{\sin(\vartheta(s))}{-\sin(\vartheta(s))}{\cos(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the polar form to get vartheta' and the matrix identity.

nodes.name: Integral for (i)
nodes.statement: Now we prove (i),(ii),(iii). For $l\in\mathbb{Z}$ we have \begin{align*} \vartheta(-s_*+ l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(-s_*) &= \int_{-s_*}^{-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \vartheta'(s) \,ds\\ &= \int_{-s_*}^{-s_*+l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \frac{\sqrt{\mu}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \,ds \\ &= \int_0^{lK(k)} \frac{\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{\mu} \kappa(\sqrt{2-k^2}s-s_*)^2}{2(\kappa(\sqrt{2-k^2}s-s_*)^2-\mu)} \,ds \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_kappa_orbitlike}}{=} \int_0^{lK(k)} \frac{\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{(2-k^2)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2-1+k^2} \,ds \\ &= \sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2} \int_0^{lK(k)} \frac{\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{(2-k^2)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2-1+k^2} \,ds \\ &= \frac{l}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \int_0^{K(k)} \frac{\mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{1-k^2(2-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2} \,ds. \end{align*} Here we used $\mathrm{dn}^2=1-k^2\mathrm{sn}^2$ and $\mathrm{dn}(2K(k)-s,k)=\mathrm{dn}(2K(k)+s,k)=\mathrm{dn}(s,k)$ in the last equation, see~\eqref{eq:Jacobi_trigonometric_identities}. The proof of (i) is finished once we have proved that the second factor equals $\Delta\theta_k$.
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Write the increment of vartheta as an elliptic integral.

nodes.name: Evaluate integral
nodes.statement: Using the formula 412.04 from \cite{ByrFri_handbook} for $\alpha:=k\sqrt{2-k^2}>k$ we get \begin{align*} &\;2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \int_0^{K(k)} \frac{ \mathrm{dn}(s,k)^2}{1-k^2(2-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)^2} \,ds \\ &= 2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \Big( K(k) + \frac{\pi \sqrt{\alpha^2-k^2} (1-\Lambda_0(\arcsin(\sqrt{(1-\alpha^2)(k')^{-2}}),k))}{2\alpha\sqrt{1-\alpha^2}} \Big) \\ &= 2\sqrt{2-k^2}\sqrt{1-k^2} \Big( K(k) + \frac{\pi(1-\Lambda_0(\arcsin(k'),k)) }{2\sqrt{1-k^2}\sqrt{2-k^2}} \Big) \\ &\stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_rotation}}{=} \Delta\theta_k. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Byrd-Friedman 412.04 yields Delta theta_k.

nodes.name: Initial value
nodes.statement: So (i) is proved once we have shown $\vartheta(-s_*)=-\Delta\theta_k/2$. This identity, however, follows from $-2\pi<\vartheta(-s_*)\leq 0$ and \begin{align*} e^{i\vartheta(-s_*)} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_theta}}{=} \frac{(W_2-iW_1)(-s_*)}{\sqrt{2-k^2}} \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_Wj}}{=} (w_2-iw_1)(-K(k)) = -i(w_1+iw_2)(-K(k)) \stackrel{\ref{prop:w1w2_orbitlike}.(vii)}{=} e^{- i\Delta\theta_k /2}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: vartheta(-s_*)=-Delta theta_k/2 from Proposition 2 (vii).

nodes.name: (ii) and (iii)
nodes.statement: Item (ii) holds thanks to the $2\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)-$periodicity of $\vartheta'$ and (i), namely $$ \vartheta(s+ 2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k))-\vartheta(s) = \int_{s}^{s+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \vartheta'(z) \,dz\\ = \int_{-s_*}^{-s_*+2l\sqrt{2-k^2}K(k)} \vartheta'(z) \,dz = l\Delta\theta_k $$ Finally, $\vartheta'(-s_*+s)=\vartheta'(-s_*-s)$ and $2\vartheta(-s_*)=-\Delta\theta_k$ imply~(iii).
nodes.section: 8.1 Proof of Proposition 2, Proposition~3 and Proposition~4
nodes.statement_short: Periodicity and symmetry of vartheta' give (ii),(iii).

nodes.name: Proof of Fundamental system for the wavelike Lame-type equation
nodes.statement: We first show that for all $k\in (0,1)$ the ordinary differential equation $w''- \frac{2(1-k^2)}{\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)}w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$ such that \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $w_1$ is odd about 0, $w_2$ is even about 0, $w_2(0)>0>w_1'(0)$, \item[(ii)] $\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)(w_2(s)^2 - w_1(s)^2) = 1-k^2+(2k^2-1)\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(iii)] $\mathrm{cn}^3(s,k)(w_2(s)w_2'(s) - w_1(s)w_1'(s)) = (1-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(iv)] $w_2(s)w_1'(s)-w_1(s)w_2'(s)= -k\sqrt{(1-k^2)(2k^2-1)}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(v)] The functions $\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)w_1,\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)w_2$ have unique smooth extensions $\hat w_1,\hat w_2:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that the functions $w_1:=\frac{\hat w_1}{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)},w_2:=\frac{\hat w_2}{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)}$ build a fundamental system on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$. Moreover, $\hat w_2$ is positive on $\mathbb{R}$, $s\hat w_1(s)$ is negative on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ and, as $s\to\pm\infty$, we have $\hat w_1(s)\to \mp\infty,\hat w_2(s)\to\infty$ exponentially and $\hat w_1(s)/\hat w_2(s)\to \mp 1$. \end{itemize} \medskip The proof is similar to the orbitlike case. We define $$ w_\pm (s) := \frac{\Theta_1(s\pm\alpha_k,k)}{\Theta(s,k)} e^{\mp s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} \quad\text{where }\mathrm{dn}^2(\alpha_k,k)=k^2, \text{ i.e. }\alpha_k:= F(k'/k,k) $$ for $\Theta,\Theta_1,\zeta$ as in section~\ref{sec:Jacobi}. Notice that $k\in (\frac{1}{\sqrt 2},1)$ implies $k'/k\in (0,1)$ and thus $\alpha_k$ is real. From Proposition~6 in \cite{Val_Heun} (for parameters $m_1=0,m_2=1,m_3=0,m_0=0,A=2k^2,s=\frac{2k^2-1}{4},\sigma=2k^2-1$) we infer that \begin{equation} w_1(s):= \frac{k(w_+(s) - w_-(s))}{(w_+(0)+w_-(0))\mathrm{cn}(s,k)},\qquad w_2(s):= \frac{k(w_+(s) + w_-(s))}{(w_+(0)+w_-(0))\mathrm{cn}(s,k)} \end{equation} is a fundamental system of the ODE on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus \{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)=0\}$, which satisfies (i) thanks to $w_\pm(-s)=w_\mp(s)$. The same proposition tells us that the product $w_+w_-$ is a real multiple of the function $1-k^2+(2k^2-1)\mathrm{cn}^2(\cdot,k)$ so that our choice for $w_1,w_2$ yields (ii). Differentiating this identity gives (iii) and (iv). Item (v) follows from the constancy of the Wronskian and $w_2(0)w_1'(0)-w_1(0)w_2'(0)= -k \sqrt{(1-k^2)(2k^2-1)}$. Finally, \eqref{eq:defn_w1w2_wavelike} shows that property (v) holds for the choice \begin{align*} \hat w_1(s) &:= \frac{k(w_+(s) - w_-(s))}{w_+(0)+w_-(0)} =\frac{k(\Theta_1(s+\alpha_k,k)e^{-s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} - \Theta_1(s-\alpha_k,k)e^{s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)}}{ (w_+(0)+w_-(0))\Theta(s,k)}, \\ \hat w_2(s) &:= \frac{k(w_+(s) + w_-(s))}{w_+(0)+w_-(0)} = \frac{k(\Theta_1(s+\alpha_k,k)e^{-s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} + \Theta_1(s-\alpha_k,k)e^{s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)}}{ (w_+(0)+w_-(0))\Theta(s,k)}, \end{align*} since $\zeta(\alpha_k,k)>0$ and $\Theta_1(\cdot,k),\Theta(\cdot,k)$ are positive periodic functions. Notice that the all complex zeros of $\Theta_1,\Theta$ are known to be non-real, see 1051.07 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}.
nodes.statement_short: Construct w_1,w_2 from theta-function solutions Theta_1(s+-alpha_k)/Theta(s) e^{-+s zeta(alpha_k)} and use Heun-function results for the product identity.

nodes.statement: We first show that for all $k\in (0,1)$ the ordinary differential equation $w''- \frac{2(1-k^2)}{\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)}w=0$ has a fundamental system $\{w_1,w_2\}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$ such that \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $w_1$ is odd about 0, $w_2$ is even about 0, $w_2(0)>0>w_1'(0)$, \item[(ii)] $\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)(w_2(s)^2 - w_1(s)^2) = 1-k^2+(2k^2-1)\mathrm{cn}^2(s,k)$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(iii)] $\mathrm{cn}^3(s,k)(w_2(s)w_2'(s) - w_1(s)w_1'(s)) = (1-k^2)\mathrm{sn}(s,k)\mathrm{dn}(s,k)$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(iv)] $w_2(s)w_1'(s)-w_1(s)w_2'(s)= -k\sqrt{(1-k^2)(2k^2-1)}$ on $(-K(k),K(k))$, \item[(v)] The functions $\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)w_1,\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)w_2$ have unique smooth extensions $\hat w_1,\hat w_2:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that the functions $w_1:=\frac{\hat w_1}{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)},w_2:=\frac{\hat w_2}{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)}$ build a fundamental system on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$. Moreover, $\hat w_2$ is positive on $\mathbb{R}$, $s\hat w_1(s)$ is negative on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ and, as $s\to\pm\infty$, we have $\hat w_1(s)\to \mp\infty,\hat w_2(s)\to\infty$ exponentially and $\hat w_1(s)/\hat w_2(s)\to \mp 1$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Restate the properties.

nodes.name: Theta solutions
nodes.statement: The proof is similar to the orbitlike case. We define $$ w_\pm (s) := \frac{\Theta_1(s\pm\alpha_k,k)}{\Theta(s,k)} e^{\mp s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} \quad\text{where }\mathrm{dn}^2(\alpha_k,k)=k^2, \text{ i.e. }\alpha_k:= F(k'/k,k) $$ for $\Theta,\Theta_1,\zeta$ as in section~\ref{sec:Jacobi}. Notice that $k\in (\frac{1}{\sqrt 2},1)$ implies $k'/k\in (0,1)$ and thus $\alpha_k$ is real.
nodes.statement_short: Define w_+- via Theta_1, Theta, zeta with real alpha_k.

nodes.name: Fundamental system
nodes.statement: From Proposition~6 in \cite{Val_Heun} (for parameters $m_1=0,m_2=1,m_3=0,m_0=0,A=2k^2,s=\frac{2k^2-1}{4},\sigma=2k^2-1$) we infer that \begin{equation} w_1(s):= \frac{k(w_+(s) - w_-(s))}{(w_+(0)+w_-(0))\mathrm{cn}(s,k)},\qquad w_2(s):= \frac{k(w_+(s) + w_-(s))}{(w_+(0)+w_-(0))\mathrm{cn}(s,k)} \end{equation} is a fundamental system of the ODE on each connected component of $\mathbb{R}\setminus \{\mathrm{cn}(\cdot,k)=0\}$, which satisfies (i) thanks to $w_\pm(-s)=w_\mp(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Heun result gives the fundamental system w_1,w_2 and (i).

nodes.name: Product identity
nodes.statement: The same proposition tells us that the product $w_+w_-$ is a real multiple of the function $1-k^2+(2k^2-1)\mathrm{cn}^2(\cdot,k)$ so that our choice for $w_1,w_2$ yields (ii). Differentiating this identity gives (iii) and (iv).
nodes.statement_short: Product w_+w_- gives (ii); differentiate for (iii),(iv).

nodes.name: Wronskian
nodes.statement: Item (v) follows from the constancy of the Wronskian and $w_2(0)w_1'(0)-w_1(0)w_2'(0)= -k \sqrt{(1-k^2)(2k^2-1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Item (v) from constancy of the Wronskian.

nodes.name: Smooth extensions
nodes.statement: Finally, \eqref{eq:defn_w1w2_wavelike} shows that property (v) holds for the choice \begin{align*} \hat w_1(s) &:= \frac{k(w_+(s) - w_-(s))}{w_+(0)+w_-(0)} =\frac{k(\Theta_1(s+\alpha_k,k)e^{-s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} - \Theta_1(s-\alpha_k,k)e^{s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)}}{ (w_+(0)+w_-(0))\Theta(s,k)}, \\ \hat w_2(s) &:= \frac{k(w_+(s) + w_-(s))}{w_+(0)+w_-(0)} = \frac{k(\Theta_1(s+\alpha_k,k)e^{-s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} + \Theta_1(s-\alpha_k,k)e^{s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)}}{ (w_+(0)+w_-(0))\Theta(s,k)}, \end{align*} since $\zeta(\alpha_k,k)>0$ and $\Theta_1(\cdot,k),\Theta(\cdot,k)$ are positive periodic functions. Notice that the all complex zeros of $\Theta_1,\Theta$ are known to be non-real, see 1051.07 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit hat w_1, hat w_2 give (v).

nodes.name: Proof of Properties of the angle function vartheta (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Now we prove Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike}. For $W_1,W_2,\vartheta$ as in \eqref{eq:def_Wj_wavelike},\eqref{eq:def_theta_wavelike} we have to prove that the following identities hold on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$: $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\quad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. $$ \medskip We proceed as in the orbitlike case. With $c(s):= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(s)}$ we may write $$ \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} = c(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}. $$ Differentiating both sides and using Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}~(ii),(iii) we arrive at \begin{align*} &-c(s)\vartheta'(s) \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))} + c'(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} \; =\; \vecII{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_2(s)}{W_1(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2c(s)}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*} This identity gives $$ \vartheta'(s) = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)},\qquad c'(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}} $$ and the claim follows from \begin{align*} \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} &= \matII{0}{c}{-c\vartheta'}{c'}\matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{ -\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: As in the orbitlike case: differentiate the hyperbolic polar representation of (W_1,W_2) and compare coefficients.

nodes.name: Restatement
nodes.statement: Now we prove Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike}. For $W_1,W_2,\vartheta$ as in \eqref{eq:def_Wj_wavelike},\eqref{eq:def_theta_wavelike} we have to prove that the following identities hold on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\kappa=0\}$: $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\quad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Restate the identities.

nodes.name: Differentiate
nodes.statement: We proceed as in the orbitlike case. With $c(s):= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(s)}$ we may write $$ \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} = c(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}. $$ Differentiating both sides and using Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}~(ii),(iii) we arrive at \begin{align*} &-c(s)\vartheta'(s) \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))} + c'(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} \; =\; \vecII{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_2(s)}{W_1(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2c(s)}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the hyperbolic polar form using Proposition 12.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: This identity gives $$ \vartheta'(s) = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)},\qquad c'(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}} $$ and the claim follows from \begin{align*} \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} &= \matII{0}{c}{-c\vartheta'}{c'}\matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{ -\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Read off vartheta' and c'.
